# PR Audit Bundle — Comprehensive audit, product and UI/UX fixes
- **Branch:** `audit/claude-comprehensive-review`
- **Base:** `main`
- **Head commit:** `a4b688cc3e9514454f59163be1ca0f309e37d699`
- **PR:** https://github.com/Masteader/budget-tracker/pull/3
- **Excluded from the diff (generated/binary):** `ai_service/static/**`, `ai_service/_landing_impl.py`, lockfiles.

## 1. Implementation Plan & Intent

### Objective
Comprehensive security and engineering audit of Budget Tracker (Supabase/Postgres, FastAPI `ai_service`, Flutter app, React web), plus the owner's product decisions: Islamic Nafaqah family mode, admin/co-admin permissions, household type (family / roommates), zero-SMS policy, support/VIP e-mail delivery, and two independent review rounds (Gemini/Argon round 1, Fable rounds 1–2). Master report: `docs/review/audit/MASTER_AUDIT_REPORT.md`; independent review and status: `docs/review/audit/fable_review.md`; every fix: `docs/review/FIX_LOG.md`.

### Architectural Approach
- **Database is the source of truth for authorization.** RLS on every table, `SECURITY DEFINER` RPCs with pinned `search_path` and actor checks, column-level grants for the few client writes, triggers for invariants (creator binding, owner-or-admin writes, Nafaqah ledger guard, cycle-key derivation, budget spend).
- **Backend uses JWT-only authentication** (`X-Signature` optional, verified when present), explicit household authorization on every service-role query, `Decimal`/halala money, structured attribution columns (`spent_by`, `beneficiary_type`, `beneficiary_id`) instead of free-text tags.
- **Nafaqah (rule 02)**: no spousal split; wife-paid shared expense → debt the husband owes (append-only `spouse_reimbursements`, overpayment refused under an advisory lock); wife personal → per-cycle allowance only (not household budgets); explicit provider per household (default primary admin, admin-changeable); financial role per membership; only wife/provider/admin classify; when the wife leaves, her ledger in that household is removed.
- **Household type** stored per household (`family` / `roommates`), chosen at creation, admin-changeable; roommates settle with pairwise debts + simplification.
- **Permissions**: members edit/delete only their own transactions; admins edit all; only admins withdraw from shared pools; co-admins; protected primary admin; legacy rows without a creator are admin-only.
- **Live database**: migrations up to `20261020600000` are applied. Five more (`20261020700000`, `750000`, `800000`, `900000`, `20261021000000`) are NOT applied. The first four were rehearsed on a faithful replica of live (`docs/review/audit/live_db_preflight_round3.md`, verdict: safe); the fifth (Saudi taxonomy + BNPL schedule) passed the full local chain from the live baseline (§3b of the same doc). Tested rollbacks in `docs/review/rollback/`. Per `AGENTS.md`, the owner applies them, then deploys `ai_service`, then the app.

- **Product and UI/UX review fixes (2026-10-21)**: one LLM call per confirmed expense via a signed `preview_token` (HMAC, `PREVIEW_TOKEN_SECRET`); user-corrected amount/category accepted on commit without re-parsing; receipt photo uploaded only after the insert; DB is the only store (JSON/in-memory fallbacks removed); Saudi taxonomy (8 codes, 23 sub-codes) and biweekly Tabby/Tamara schedule; local reminders; one "until payday" hero; honest per-card error states; guided household setup; visible overspend; one Nafaqah question with real names; feed Nafaqah badges; light-mode contrast ≥ 4.5:1; one money formatter; Cairo font; single honest landing page (`web_app/` only). Reviews: `docs/review/audit/product_review.md`, `docs/review/audit/ux_review.md`.

### Files Modified & Summary of Changes
Grouped list below (generated from `git diff --stat`). Per-area detail: `docs/review/audit/{db,ai_service,flutter_logic,ui_web,final_review_backend,final_review_app,fable_review,e2e_results,dependency_audit,translation_qa,android_build,live_db_preflight*}.md`.

### Rule 01–05 Compliance Check
- **Rule 01** stack unchanged (Flutter, FastAPI, React/Vite, Supabase); CI removed at the owner's request.
- **Rule 02** per-household payday cycle (default 27th, Asia/Riyadh; SQL/Python/Dart parity checked over 60,388 date×payday pairs); Nafaqah rules 1–4 as above; ZATCA TLV decoder hardened; roommate debt simplification.
- **Rule 03** en/ar/ur via `AppLocalizations` (key parity + no hardcoded strings enforced by `test/ui_l10n_guard_test.dart`), Arabic plurals, RTL-directional layout, theme tokens.
- **Rule 04** zero SMS (code, schema channel and permissions removed; guard tests), service key server-side only, RLS multi-tenancy, admin/co-admin model, JWT-only API.
- **Rule 05** TDD: every fix has a regression test; all suites green (below).

 ## 4. Communication Guidelines Between Components
 
-1. **Client to Supabase:** Flutter app interacts directly with Supabase for CRUD operations governed by Row Level Security (RLS) using the **Anon Key**.
-2. **Client to AI Backend:** Heavy computing tasks (Gemini Vision OCR, conversational Arabic audio/text expense extraction, PDF statement generation) are routed to the FastAPI backend.
-3. **Backend to Supabase:** The FastAPI service communicates with Supabase using the **Service Role Key** (bypassing RLS) strictly for internal processing, validation, and analytics.
+1. **Client to Supabase:** the Flutter app uses Supabase directly with the **publishable (anon) key**; every read and write is governed by Row Level Security, and ledger or role changes go through `SECURITY DEFINER` RPCs.
+2. **Client to AI Backend:** AI and server-side logic (receipt OCR, chat expense extraction, salary cycles, settlements, Nafaqah, PDF statements, support) go to FastAPI with the user's Supabase JWT (`Authorization: Bearer`). `X-Signature` is optional defense in depth.
+3. **Backend to Supabase:** FastAPI uses the **secret / service-role key** (bypasses RLS), so every route re-checks the verified JWT user's household membership and admin rights itself (`auth.verify_household_access`, `household_permissions.py`).
+4. **Web to Backend:** `web_app` only calls the anonymous `POST /public/inquiries` endpoint.
+5. **Deployment order:** database migrations first, then `ai_service`, then the app build.

 ## 1. Saudi Salary & Payday Cycle Alignment
 
-- **The 27th Standard Payday:** In the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, public and most private sector salaries are disbursed on the **27th of each Gregorian month**.
-- **Cycle Identification (`cycle_key`):**
-  - All budgets, salary records, and recurring reserves are indexed by `cycle_key` in format `YYYY-MM`.
-  - A cycle runs from the 27th of month $M$ to the 26th of month $M+1$.
+- **Payday per household:** salary cycles follow `households.payday_day` (1–31, default **27**, the common Saudi payday). Only a household admin changes it (`PUT /households/{id}/payday`). Never hard-code the 27th in new code.
+- **Cycle Identification (`cycle_key`, `YYYY-MM`):**
+  - A cycle runs from the payday of one month to the day before the next payday, on the **Asia/Riyadh** calendar date. A payday beyond the month's length is clamped to its last day; payday 1 means the calendar month.
+  - With payday > 15 the key names the month the cycle **ends** in (payday 27: 27 Oct → 26 Nov is `2026-11`); with payday ≤ 15 it names the month it starts in.
+  - SQL (`get_saudi_cycle_for_timestamp`), Python (`salary_cycle.get_cycle_for_date`) and Dart compute the same key; triggers fill `transactions.cycle_key` and clients cannot forge it.
 - **Payday Check-In:**
-  - When the date reaches or passes the 27th, prompt the user with the Payday Check-in Sheet to record their salary, overtime, bonus, and deductions.
-  - Automatically provide the 1-tap Salary Distribution Assistant to fund secondary wallets and bank accounts.
-- **Cycle Rollover Handling:**
-  - Give users an explicit choice for unspent category funds:
-    - **Option A (Category Rollover):** Unspent funds rollover into the new cycle's category cushion (`previous_cycle_delta`).
-    - **Option C (Sweep to Savings):** Unspent funds are swept into an emergency savings reserve, resetting categories clean.
+  - When the household payday arrives, prompt the user with the Payday Check-in Sheet to record their salary, overtime, bonus, and deductions.
+  - Offer the 1-tap Salary Distribution Assistant to fund secondary wallets and bank accounts.
+- **Cycle Rollover Handling:** the household chooses its rule (`households.rollover_rule`, `GET|PUT /households/{id}/rollover-rule`, admin to change):
+  - `send_to_savings` (default): leftover funds are swept into the savings reserve; categories start fresh.
+  - `rollover_to_categories`: leftover funds increase each category in the new cycle (`previous_cycle_delta`).
+  - `fresh_start`: allocations reset to baseline with no carryover.

   - In Islamic jurisprudence, the husband bears complete legal financial responsibility (*Nafaqah*) for housing, food, clothing, and essential family maintenance.
   - **Strict Prohibition:** NEVER impose automatic 50/50 expense splits between husband and wife.
   - If a wife pays for household groceries or expenses out of her personal funds, track it as **Reimbursable Debt** owed by the husband.
+- **Family mode rules (owner decision on audit item UI-24, authoritative).** A household is in family mode when one of its memberships has `household_memberships.financial_role = 'spouse'` (roles are per household; `users.financial_role` only caches the active household's). The husband is the household's explicit Nafaqah provider, `households.nafaqah_provider_user_id` (owner decision 2026-10-21): by default the primary admin, changed by any admin to another non-spouse member (`set_nafaqah_provider`, `PUT /households/{id}/nafaqah/provider`); never inferred from roles or admin rights. Without a provider, new classified expenses are refused. `wife_personal` purchases count against her allowance only, never the category budgets; edits that would leave the reimbursement ledger overpaid are refused (`ledger_would_be_overpaid`).
+  1. **Nafaqah is on the husband.** Shared family/household expenses are his responsibility. There is **no 50/50 or any percentage split** between the spouses anywhere in family mode (API, app banners, settlement cards, chat). `split_ratio` and "Shared 50/50" belong to roommate/partner households only.
+  2. **Wife pays for something shared** (household, children/dependents, the husband) from her own money → `transactions.nafaqah_class = 'wife_reimbursable'` with `nafaqah_spouse_id` = the wife. It is a debt the husband owes her. The app shows the outstanding balance and history, and records partial or full repayments in the append-only `spouse_reimbursements` ledger (`record_spouse_reimbursement`); paying back more than is outstanding is rejected.
+  3. **Wife buys something personal for herself** → `nafaqah_class = 'wife_personal'`. Not a debt: it is charged to her personal allowance ("مصروفها") for the salary cycle (`cycle_key`, household payday to the day before the next). The husband or a household admin (never the wife herself) sets the amount per cycle (`member_allowances`, `set_member_allowance`); the app shows allocated / spent / remaining, and overspend shows a negative remainder (never blocked).
+  4. **Husband pays for shared things** (or buys something for his wife) → an ordinary household expense: no class, no debt.

+  - Money is `numeric(14,2)` in SQL, `Decimal`/integer halalas in Python. Ledger writes go only through the `SECURITY DEFINER` RPCs with a pinned `search_path` and actor checks; the API passes the verified JWT subject as `p_actor_user_id` and checks the wife belongs to the URL's household (no IDOR).
+  - Roommate mode (peers, no spouse) is unaffected: equal splits and multi-roommate debt simplification as below.
 - **Shared Living Groups (Roommates / Flatmates):**

   - Use the Multi-Roommate Settlement Engine with multi-way debt simplification to compute net balances without circular transfers.

 ## 2. Supabase API Key Segregation
 
-- **Anon Public Key (`SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` / `SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`):**
-  - Safe for client distribution (Flutter mobile app, React web app).
+- **Publishable / Anon Key (`SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY`, alias `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY`):**
+  - Safe for client distribution (the Flutter app; `web_app` does not talk to Supabase at all).
   - All queries are strictly constrained by PostgreSQL Row Level Security (RLS).
-- **Service Role Secret Key (`SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`):**
-  - STRICTLY FORBIDDEN from being embedded or compiled into the Flutter mobile app or client-side assets.
-  - Only stored in server-side `.env` and used exclusively by the Python `ai_service` for administrative background tasks, webhooks, and migrations.
+- **Secret / Service Role Key (`SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` or `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`):**
+  - An `sb_secret_…` key or a legacy `service_role` JWT, in either variable (`ai_service/supabase_client.py` `describe_supabase_key`: an `sb_secret_` key wins over a legacy JWT; anon/publishable values are never used and are logged as ignored). Requires `supabase>=2.16.0`.
+  - STRICTLY FORBIDDEN from being embedded or compiled into the Flutter mobile app or client-side assets (the app rejects such keys at startup).
+  - Only stored in server-side environment variables and used exclusively by the Python `ai_service`, which bypasses RLS and therefore re-checks the verified JWT user's household membership and admin rights on every route. Migrations are applied in the Supabase SQL editor (database first, then backend, then app), never by the service.
 
 ## 3. Household Multi-Tenancy & Row Level Security (RLS)
 
-- Every sensitive relational table (`transactions`, `budgets`, `accounts`, `account_transfers`, `income_records`, `recurring_bills`, `installment_plans`, `household_dependents`, `reimbursement_debts`) MUST have Row Level Security enabled.
-- Queries and RLS policies must strictly enforce tenancy isolation:
+- **Every** `public` table MUST have Row Level Security enabled (today: `users`, `households`, `household_memberships`, `household_invites`, `invite_attempt_log`, `household_dependents`, `household_category_settings`, `cost_control_codes`, `cost_control_sub_categories`, `transactions`, `budgets`, `accounts`, `account_transfers`, `income_records`, `installment_plans`, `member_allowances`, `spouse_reimbursements`, `api_quota`). `supabase/tests/14_audit_catalog_guardrails.sql` checks the catalog.
+- Policies scope rows to the caller's active household through the helper, wrapped in `SELECT` so it is evaluated once per statement (DB-13):
   ```sql
-  household_id IN (SELECT household_id FROM public.users WHERE id = auth.uid())
+  household_id = (SELECT public.get_auth_user_household_id())
   ```
-- Personal accounts are restricted to the owner:
+- Personal accounts are visible to their owner; shared pools to the household, and only admins change them:
   ```sql
-  owner_user_id = auth.uid() OR is_shared_pool = true
+  owner_user_id = (SELECT auth.uid())
+    OR (is_shared_pool = true AND household_id = (SELECT public.get_auth_user_household_id()))
   ```
+- `SECURITY DEFINER` functions pin `search_path`; no policy targets `PUBLIC`/`anon`, and `anon` can execute no function in `public` (same guardrail test).
 - Never bypass RLS in client requests.
 
-## 4. API & Webhook Security
+## 4. Household Roles & Permissions (owner decision on DB-16 / DB-18)
 
-- **Webhook Signature Verification:** Webhooks sent to `ai_service` must validate an `X-Webhook-Secret` HMAC-SHA256 signature.
-- **Firewall Token Middleware:** Backend static assets and API routes must enforce firewall token authentication where applicable.
+Applies to family and roommate households alike. The database enforces every rule; `ai_service` (service role, bypasses RLS) re-checks them explicitly with the verified JWT user; the app only hides actions the server would refuse and explains a 403.
+
+- **Roles:** `household_memberships.role` is `admin` or `member`. The **primary admin** is `households.owner_user_id` (backfilled from the longest-standing admin; passes to the longest-standing remaining admin when their membership ends). Other admins are **co-admins** with the same rights, except that they can never demote or remove the primary admin.
+- **Transactions:** the creator is `transactions.user_id = auth.uid()`, bound at insert (filled in when a client omits it, rejected when it names someone else) and never changed. A member edits or deletes only their own transactions; an admin any transaction of the household. Rows without a creator are admin-only. API-created transactions must carry the verified JWT user; enrichment, installment linking and settlements check owner-or-admin (`ai_service/household_permissions.py`).
+- **Money movement:** only admins move money out of a shared pool (`transfer_between_accounts`); a personal account is debited only by its owner. Members may still pay into the pool and move money between their own accounts.
+- **Role changes:** only through the SECURITY DEFINER RPCs `promote_member_to_admin`, `revoke_admin`, `transfer_primary_admin` (and `set_member_role` / `remove_member`), each with a pinned `search_path`, an actor check (`p_actor_user_id` is honoured only for the service role) and household scoping. Clients hold no write privilege on `household_memberships`, `users.role` or `households.owner_user_id`. Any admin promotes members and revokes co-admins; only the primary admin transfers primary admin. The last admin can never be demoted, and a sole admin cannot leave while members remain.
+- **API endpoints:** `GET /households/{id}/members` (any member), `POST|DELETE /households/{id}/members/{user_id}/admin` (admins), `POST /households/{id}/primary-admin` (primary admin). Never take the acting user from a request body.
+- **Family Nafaqah:** the wife's allowance is set by the husband or any admin (co-admins included), never by the wife herself; the husband is the household's explicit Nafaqah provider (`households.nafaqah_provider_user_id`, default the primary admin, changed only by an admin through `set_nafaqah_provider`). Invite codes are readable by admins only, and an existing member can never claim an invite of their own household.
+
+## 5. API & Webhook Security
+
+- **User authentication:** every non-public `ai_service` route verifies the caller's Supabase JWT itself (`auth.get_current_user_id` / `verify_household_access`). Never take the acting user from the body or from a shared secret.
+- **Request signatures (`X-Signature`, HMAC-SHA256 of the exact body with `WEBHOOK_SECRET`):** defense in depth on user routes, NEVER their authentication. `auth.verify_signature_if_present` runs on every router in `main.py`: when a valid Supabase JWT authenticates the request, an invalid, malformed or unverifiable signature (including `WEBHOOK_SECRET` unset in production) MUST NOT reject it; it is logged (rate limited, route and a hash of the user id, never secret values) and the request continues. Without a valid JWT a bad signature is 401. Reason: `WEBHOOK_SECRET` has been rotated and every installed app build signs with the old value. A genuine server-to-server webhook route that has no user JWT MUST require a valid signature (`utils.verify_signature`, missing signature = reject). The Flutter app signs only when built with the optional `--dart-define=WEBHOOK_SECRET` and must never fail to start without it.
+- **Firewall Token Middleware:** requests arriving through a proxy/tunnel need a verified Bearer JWT (401 + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` otherwise). `X-App-Token` (`APP_AUTH_TOKEN`) is accepted there only as a legacy pass for old app builds and is never user authentication; current clients do not send it.
 - **Receipt Storage Privacy:** Receipt images stored in Supabase Storage (`receipts` bucket) must enforce authenticated access policies ensuring only household members can view receipts uploaded within their household folder.

+   - Database: `python3 supabase/tests/run_tests.py --psql --rebuild --db <throwaway_db>` against a **local** PostgreSQL (libpq `PGHOST`/`PGPORT`/`PGUSER`); `--apply-from PREFIX` applies new migrations to an existing local replica, `--stop-before PREFIX` and `--no-tests` build a baseline. Never point the runner at a real Supabase project.
+   - Web: `cd web_app && npm run lint && npm run build`
+   - End-to-end: `tests/e2e/` (local services and mocks only)
+6. **Database changes** ship as a new timestamped file in `supabase/migrations/` with a proof test in `supabase/tests/NN_*.sql` (the convention of the 20261019/20261020 batches).
 
 ## 2. Zero Static Analysis Warnings
 
 - Run `flutter analyze` inside `flutter_app/` before completing work.
-- The project must compile with **zero errors and zero analyzer warnings**.
+- The project must compile with **zero errors and zero analyzer warnings** (`No issues found!`), and `npm run lint` in `web_app/` must be clean.
 - Keep dependencies updated and resolve all deprecation notices promptly.

+# PR & External Argon Audit Pipeline Rules
+
+## 1. Branch Isolation & Main Protection
+- NEVER commit or merge directly to `main` locally.
+- All features, bugfixes, and audit rounds MUST be developed on a dedicated branch (`feat/<name>`, `fix/<name>`, or `audit/<name>`).
+- Merging into `main` is strictly forbidden until the Pull Request receives explicit `APPROVED` status from the External Argon Auditor.
+
+## 2. Mandatory Pre-PR Verification Gate
+Before pushing any branch for review or generating an audit bundle, you MUST run and pass:
+1. `cd flutter_app && flutter analyze` (Zero warnings/errors)
+2. `cd flutter_app && flutter test` (All tests passing)
+3. `cd ai_service && .venv\Scripts\pytest -v` (All backend tests passing)
+
+## 3. Two-Stage External Audit Loop
+1. **Submission (`submit-for-audit.md`):**
+   - Push the branch to `origin`.
+   - Generate `docs/review/PR_AUDIT_BUNDLE.md` containing:
+     - **Section 1: Implementation Plan & Architectural Intent** (What was requested, why this approach was chosen, which files were modified, and compliance with Rules 01–05).
+     - **Section 2: Test & Analyzer Output Summary**.
+     - **Section 3: Baseline Context & Unified Diff (`git diff main...HEAD`)**.
+   - Copy the bundle to the Windows clipboard (`Get-Content docs/review/PR_AUDIT_BUNDLE.md -Raw | Set-Clipboard`) so the user can paste it directly to the External Auditor.
+2. **Addressing Review (`address-review.md`):**
+   - Fetch the External Auditor's comments from the GitHub PR via the GitHub REST API (`https://api.github.com/repos/Masteader/budget-tracker/pulls`) or `gh` CLI (or `docs/review/AUDIT_FEEDBACK.md` if provided locally).
+   - Address every finding systematically, write/update tests for each fix, push the new commit to the PR branch, and regenerate the updated audit bundle.

@@ -0,0 +1,44 @@
+---
+description: Fetch external audit review comments from the active GitHub PR (via GitHub Public REST API or gh CLI) or local feedback file, implement all requested fixes, verify tests, update the PR, and generate a delta audit bundle.
+---
+
+# Workflow: Address External PR Review & Update Diff
+
+1. **Fetch the Latest PR Audit Comments**
+   - First, check if the user pasted feedback into `docs/review/AUDIT_FEEDBACK.md` or directly in the prompt.
+   - Next, query the public GitHub REST API via PowerShell to retrieve the open PR and its comments for the current branch (`$branch = git branch --show-current`):
+     ```powershell
+     $prs = Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://api.github.com/repos/Masteader/budget-tracker/pulls?state=open"
+     $pr = $prs | Where-Object { $_.head.ref -eq $branch } | Select-Object -First 1
+     if ($pr) {
+       Write-Output "=== PR #$($pr.number): $($pr.title) ==="
+       Write-Output "=== ISSUE COMMENTS ==="
+       Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://api.github.com/repos/Masteader/budget-tracker/issues/$($pr.number)/comments" | ForEach-Object { Write-Output "[$($_.user.login) at $($_.created_at)]:`n$($_.body)`n---" }
+       Write-Output "=== REVIEW BODIES ==="
+       Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://api.github.com/repos/Masteader/budget-tracker/pulls/$($pr.number)/reviews" | ForEach-Object { Write-Output "[$($_.user.login) - $($_.state)]:`n$($_.body)`n---" }
+       Write-Output "=== INLINE CODE COMMENTS ==="
+       Invoke-RestMethod -Uri "https://api.github.com/repos/Masteader/budget-tracker/pulls/$($pr.number)/comments" | ForEach-Object { Write-Output "[$($_.path):$($_.line)]:`n$($_.body)`n---" }
+     }
+     ```
+
+2. **Parse Findings & Build an Action Checklist**
+   - Extract every `CRITICAL`, `HIGH`, `MEDIUM`, and `LOW` / `NIT` item from the latest review comment.
+   - Track each item using `manage_task` before modifying code.
+
+3. **Implement Fixes Following TDD (Rule 05)**
+   - For each review item, add or update the corresponding unit/widget/pytest test first.
+   - Implement the code fix cleanly without breaking Rules 01–05.
+
+4. **Run Full Verification Gate**
+   - Run `cd flutter_app && flutter analyze`
+   - Run `cd flutter_app && flutter test`
+   - Run `cd ai_service && .venv\Scripts\pytest -v`
+
+5. **Commit, Push to PR Branch, and Generate Re-Audit Bundle**
+   - Commit the review fixes: `git commit -m "fix(review): address external audit findings for PR"`
+   - Push to the active PR branch: `git push origin HEAD`
+   - Update `docs/review/PR_AUDIT_BUNDLE.md` with:
+     - **1. Audit Resolution Table:** Every finding ID, how it was fixed, and exact file/line references.
+     - **2. Delta Diff (Changes in this Review Round):** `git diff HEAD~1...HEAD`
+     - **3. Full Cumulative PR Diff against `main`:** `git diff main...HEAD`
+   - Copy `docs/review/PR_AUDIT_BUNDLE.md` to clipboard via `Set-Clipboard` and notify the user.

@@ -0,0 +1,34 @@
+---
+description: Package the implementation plan, verification results, and unified git diff against main, push the branch to GitHub, and copy the complete audit bundle to clipboard for External Argon Audit.
+---
+
+# Workflow: Submit Branch & Diff for External Audit
+
+1. **Ensure Branch Safety**
+   - Verify you are NOT on `main` (`git branch --show-current`). If on `main`, create and switch to a feature/fix branch (`git checkout -b feat/<short-name>` or `fix/<short-name>`) before committing.
+
+2. **Run Mandatory Verification Suite**
+   - Run `cd flutter_app && flutter analyze`
+   - Run `cd flutter_app && flutter test`
+   - Run `cd ai_service && .venv\Scripts\pytest -v`
+   - Do not proceed until all checks pass with zero warnings or failures.
+
+3. **Stage, Commit, and Push Branch to GitHub**
+   - Stage and commit all changes using Conventional Commits.
+   - Push the branch to remote: `git push -u origin HEAD`
+   - Check if `gh` is available (`where.exe gh`). If installed and authenticated, create or update the PR using `gh pr create --fill` (if not already open). If `gh` is not installed, print the direct GitHub PR URL: `https://github.com/Masteader/budget-tracker/pull/new/<branch-name>`.
+
+4. **Generate `docs/review/PR_AUDIT_BUNDLE.md`**
+   - Create or overwrite `docs/review/PR_AUDIT_BUNDLE.md` (ensure it is either git-ignored or excluded from the code diff) with this exact structure:
+     - **Header:** Branch name, base branch (`main`), head commit SHA, and PR URL (or creation URL).
+     - **1. Implementation Plan & Intent:**
+       - **Objective:** What problem/feature this PR solves.
+       - **Architectural Approach:** How it was designed and why.
+       - **Files Modified & Summary of Changes:** Bullet list of every touched file and what changed.
+       - **Rule 01–05 Compliance Check:** Brief note confirming Saudi 27th cycle/Nafaqah, RTL/trilingual l10n, RLS security, and TDD coverage.
+     - **2. Verification Output:** Summary of `flutter analyze`, `flutter test`, and `pytest` results.
+     - **3. Unified Diff (`main...HEAD`):** Append the complete raw output of `git diff main...HEAD` inside a ```` ```diff ```` block.
+
+5. **Copy Bundle to Clipboard & Notify User**
+   - Run in PowerShell: `Get-Content -Path "docs/review/PR_AUDIT_BUNDLE.md" -Raw | Set-Clipboard`
+   - Inform the user that the complete Plan + Diff Audit Bundle is now copied to their clipboard and ready to paste into the External Auditor chat (or open as a PR on GitHub).

+## Summary & Architectural Intent
+<!--
+Provide a clear, high-level summary of:
+- What problem or feature does this PR address?
+- What architectural design choices were made and why?
+-->
+
+## Type of Change
+- [ ] `feat`: New feature or capability
+- [ ] `fix`: Bug fix or security hardening
+- [ ] `test`: New or updated tests
+- [ ] `refactor`: Code change that neither fixes a bug nor adds a feature
+- [ ] `docs`: Documentation, spec, or plan update
+- [ ] `chore`: Tooling, dependencies, or configuration
+
+## Files Modified & Summary of Changes
+<!--
+List every modified, created, or deleted file and a 1-line description of the change.
+- `path/to/file`: Description of change
+-->
+
+## Rule 01–06 Compliance Verification Checklist
+Before submitting this PR, verify that all applicable project rules are strictly satisfied:
+
+- [ ] **Rule 01: Architecture & Tech Stack**
+  - [ ] Inter-service contracts respected (Client -> Supabase with Anon key, Client -> AI service, AI Service -> Supabase with Service Role key).
+  - [ ] No architectural layer violations.
+- [ ] **Rule 02: Saudi Fintech & Islamic Compliance**
+  - [ ] Payday cycle aligns with 27th Gregorian cycle (`cycle_key` format `YYYY-MM`).
+  - [ ] ZATCA Phase 2 TLV barcode scanning compatibility preserved.
+  - [ ] Islamic Nafaqah principles respected (no automatic 50/50 spousal splits; wife contributions tracked as reimbursable debt).
+  - [ ] Multi-roommate debt simplification and zero-based account balance invariants maintained.
+- [ ] **Rule 03: UI/UX & Design System**
+  - [ ] Sovereign OS / Iced Ocean theme consistency (dark/light palettes, glassmorphism, rounded corners).
+  - [ ] Strict trilingual localization (Arabic primary RTL, English, Urdu) via `AppLocalizations` / `web_app/src/i18n`.
+  - [ ] Zero hardcoded user-facing strings; directional paddings/layouts use `Directional` APIs.
+- [ ] **Rule 04: Security & Privacy**
+  - [ ] Zero SMS interception policy maintained (no SMS permissions/listeners).
+  - [ ] `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` strictly absent from client mobile/web code.
+  - [ ] PostgreSQL Row Level Security (RLS) enabled and verified on all sensitive tables.
+  - [ ] Client balance mutations prevented; atomic financial RPCs used.
+- [ ] **Rule 05: Code Quality & Testing**
+  - [ ] Test-Driven Development (TDD) followed: new/updated tests written first.
+  - [ ] `flutter analyze` completed with **0 warnings and 0 errors**.
+  - [ ] `flutter test` passes (all unit/widget tests green).
+  - [ ] `pytest -v` in `ai_service` passes (all backend tests green).
+  - [ ] Zero stubbed code, dummy handlers, or placeholder `TODO` comments.
+- [ ] **Rule 06: PR & External Argon Audit Pipeline**
+  - [ ] Dedicated feature/fix branch used (never committed directly to `main`).
+  - [ ] Audit bundle prepared via `.agent/workflows/submit-for-audit.md` (or `.agents/workflows/submit-for-audit.md`).
+
+## Verification Test Commands & Evidence
+```bash
+# Flutter Analyzer
+cd flutter_app && flutter analyze
+
+# Flutter Test Suite
+cd flutter_app && flutter test
+
+# Python FastAPI AI Microservice Test Suite
+cd ai_service && .venv\Scripts\pytest -v
+```

+│ • Dashboard & Bills   │           │ • Cycles, settlement│       │ • accounts ... │
+│ • Live Feed           │ ◄──────── │ • Nafaqah, inquiries│       │ • Storage      │
+└──────────┬────────────┘  JSON     └─────────────────────┘       └───────▲────────┘
+           └──────────── supabase_flutter (publishable key, RLS, Realtime) ┘
 ```
 
+- The app talks to Supabase directly (publishable key, Row Level Security, Realtime) and to the
+  FastAPI service for AI and server-side logic.
+- Every user route of the API is authenticated by the caller's Supabase JWT. `X-Signature` is an
+  optional integrity check, never the credential (see [Security Notes](#security-notes)).
+- The API uses the privileged Supabase key and re-checks household membership and admin rights
+  itself ([`.agents/rules/04-security-and-privacy.md`](.agents/rules/04-security-and-privacy.md)).
+

 ## Features
 
-- 🧾 **ZATCA QR & Vision OCR Scanner**: Instant TLV decoding and line-item categorization.
-- 💬 **Conversational AI Expense Chat**: Natural Saudi dialect parser with interactive previews.
-- 🎙️ **Voice Entry**: Quick hands-free logging with automatic item and merchant extraction.
-- 📅 **Salary-Cycle & Recurring Bills**: Saudi 27th payday alignment, reserve tracking, and 1-tap bill payments.
-- 🔒 **Privacy-First & Zero SMS Interception**: Completely standalone without background SMS listeners or SMS permissions.
+- 🧾 **ZATCA QR & Vision OCR Scanner**: TLV decoding and line-item categorization.
+- 💬 **Conversational AI Expense Chat**: Saudi dialect parser with interactive previews.
+- 🎙️ **Voice Entry**: hands-free logging with item and merchant extraction.
+- 📅 **Salary Cycles & Recurring Bills**: cycles follow the household payday
+  (`households.payday_day`, default 27th, Asia/Riyadh dates), bill reserves and BNPL installments.
+- 👪 **Family Nafaqah & Roommate Settlements**: no spousal percentage splits, wife reimbursement
+  ledger and personal allowance; multi-roommate debt simplification.
+- 🛡️ **Admin / co-admin permissions**: the database and the API enforce who may move shared money
+  and edit other members' transactions.
+- ✉️ **Support & VIP early-access email**: in-app and web forms are emailed to the team.
+- 🔒 **Zero SMS Interception**: no SMS permissions, listeners or SMS ingestion anywhere.
+

+
+## Running the Tests
+
+| Suite | Command | Notes |
+|---|---|---|
+| API (pytest) | `cd ai_service && python -m pytest -v` | Hermetic: in-memory Supabase fake, no network, no real LLM. `tests/test_sms_removal.py` enforces the zero-SMS policy. |
+| Flutter | `cd flutter_app && flutter test` and `flutter analyze` | Analyzer must report no issues. |
+| Database (SQL) | `PGHOST=localhost PGPORT=<port> PGUSER=postgres python3 supabase/tests/run_tests.py --psql --rebuild --db bt_tests` | Needs a **local** PostgreSQL server and `psql`. See below. |
+| Web | `cd web_app && npm ci && npm run lint && npm run build` | No unit tests; lint + type-checked build. |
+| End-to-end | see `tests/e2e/` | Local services and mocks only, never live. |
+
+Database runner (`supabase/tests/run_tests.py`) flags:
+
+- `--psql`: use the local `psql` binary with the libpq variables (`PGHOST`, `PGPORT`, `PGUSER`,
+  `PGPASSWORD`). Without it the runner uses `docker exec` into a container named
+  `budget_tracker_review_pg`.
+- `--rebuild`: drop and recreate `--db`, then replay stubs, `schema.sql`, `seed.sql` and all
+  migrations before the tests (implies `--psql`). **Never point it at a real Supabase project.**
+- `--db NAME`: database to use (default `$DB_NAME`, else `live_rebuilt_round5`).
+- `--stop-before PREFIX` (with `--rebuild`): replay only migrations sorting before `PREFIX`.
+- `--apply-from PREFIX` (without `--rebuild`): apply migrations at or after `PREFIX` to an existing
+  local replica first.
+- `--no-tests`: only rebuild / apply.
+- Positional file names run a subset, e.g. `20_admin_permissions_and_co_admins.sql`.
+
+---
+
+## Deployment Order
+
+Ship changes in this order: **database → backend → app**.
+
+1. **Database:** apply new migrations in the SQL Editor, one file per run, in filename order.
+   Before and after, run the checks in
+   [`docs/review/audit/live_db_preflight_checks.sql`](docs/review/audit/live_db_preflight_checks.sql)
+   (procedure: [`docs/review/audit/live_db_preflight.md`](docs/review/audit/live_db_preflight.md)).
+2. **Backend:** deploy `ai_service` (it calls RPCs the migrations create). It still accepts older
+   app builds.
+3. **App:** release a new build with all `--dart-define` values and the release keystore.
+
+Details and couplings: [`docs/review/audit/MASTER_AUDIT_REPORT.md`](docs/review/audit/MASTER_AUDIT_REPORT.md) §6.2.

+#### Contact, support and VIP early-access email
+
+`POST /public/inquiries` (anonymous; web app, landing pages) and `POST /support/inquiries`
+(in-app, requires the user's Supabase JWT, which supplies the sender identity) email each request
+to `CONTACT_RECIPIENT_EMAIL` from `MAIL_FROM` with `Reply-To` set to the person who submitted it.
+With SMTP, use the credentials of the `fmscoinfo@fmsco.com.sa` mailbox; with Resend, verify the
+`fmsco.com.sa` domain (SPF and DKIM records) first, or providers will reject or spam-folder the
+mail. Subjects look like `[Budget Tracker] VIP early access — <email>` or
+`[Budget Tracker] Support — <email>`.
+
+```json
+{"type": "vip_early_access" | "support" | "contact", "email": "you@example.com",
+ "name": "optional", "message": "required for support/contact", "locale": "ar", "source": "web" | "landing" | "app"}
+```
+
+The endpoints answer `200 {"status": "sent"}` only after the provider accepted the email, `503`
+when no provider is configured (logged as an error; nothing is sent), `502` when the provider
+fails, `422` for invalid input and `429` past the limits (public: 5 per IP and 3 per email per
+hour; app: 5 per user per hour; 200 per hour overall). Set either `RESEND_API_KEY` or the `SMTP_*`
+variables on the deployment, or every form shows an error.
+
+The page served at `/` is the `web_app` production build committed in `ai_service/static/`
+(`ai_service/landing_page.py` serves a tiny inline fallback page only when `static/index.html` is
+missing; the same module holds the `/auth/confirm` and `/auth/callback` pages).
+Refresh it after changing `web_app/` so the live VIP form posts to the same origin:
+
+```bash
+cd web_app && npm ci && VITE_API_BASE_URL= npm run build
+rm -rf ../ai_service/static/assets && cp -r dist/assets ../ai_service/static/
+cp dist/index.html dist/favicon.svg ../ai_service/static/
+```
+
+### Web App (`web_app/.env`, Vite)
+
+| Variable | Description |
+|---|---|
+| `VITE_API_BASE_URL` | Backend for the VIP form. Unset: `https://budget.fmsco.com.sa`; empty string: same origin (the build served by `ai_service`); e.g. `http://localhost:8000` for local work |

 | Flag | Required | Description |
 |---|---|---|
-| `SUPABASE_URL` | ✅ | Same as above |
-| `SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | ✅ | Public key (safe for clients) |
-| `FASTAPI_BASE_URL` | ✅ | Full URL to the FastAPI backend |
+| `SUPABASE_URL` | ✅ | Supabase project URL (`https://` required in release builds) |
+| `SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | ✅ | Public key (safe for clients; `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` accepted as alias). Service-role / `sb_secret_` keys are rejected at startup. |
+| `FASTAPI_BASE_URL` | ✅ | Full URL to the FastAPI backend (`https://` required in release builds) |
+| `WEBHOOK_SECRET` | ❌ | Optional HMAC key: when set, POST bodies carry an `X-Signature` header (defense in depth). The user's Supabase JWT is the credential: a signature that does not match the backend's current `WEBHOOK_SECRET` (e.g. after a rotation) is logged and ignored while the JWT is valid. Leave it out and requests are sent unsigned |

@@ -220,13 +319,23 @@ docker compose up --build
 
 ## Security Notes
 
-- The **service role key** must **never** appear in the Flutter app or any client-side code.
-- The **WEBHOOK_SECRET** is an HMAC-SHA256 shared secret — rotate it if compromised.
-- All Supabase tables have **Row Level Security (RLS)** enabled — users can only access their household's data.
-- Transaction and receipt audit data is stored securely in Supabase with household-isolated Row Level Security.
+- The **secret / service-role key** must **never** appear in the Flutter app or any client-side code.
+- **Authentication** of every user route is the caller's Supabase JWT (`Authorization: Bearer`).
+- **`X-Signature`** (HMAC-SHA256 of the exact body with `WEBHOOK_SECRET`) is defense in depth, never
+  the authentication of a user route. With a valid JWT, an invalid or unverifiable signature (also
+  when `WEBHOOK_SECRET` is unset) is logged (rate limited, route + hashed user id) and the request is
+  served; without a valid JWT it is 401. Compatibility: `WEBHOOK_SECRET` has already been rotated on
+  Railway, so every installed app build signs with the old value; rejecting those signatures would
+  break all their chat and receipt calls. A server-to-server webhook route without a JWT must
+  require a valid signature (`utils.verify_signature`); none exists today.
+- **`X-App-Token`** (`APP_AUTH_TOKEN`) is only a legacy pass at the firewall for old app builds; it
+  never authenticates a user (every route still verifies the JWT). The current app does not send it.
+- All `public` tables have **Row Level Security (RLS)** enabled — users only see their household's
+  data; ledger and role changes go through `SECURITY DEFINER` RPCs with actor checks.
+- Secret rotation: [`docs/runbooks/security-secret-rotation.md`](docs/runbooks/security-secret-rotation.md).

+# SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=<sb_secret-key-or-legacy-service-role-jwt>   # alternative name
 # Optional: Only needed if using legacy HS256 tokens (not needed for modern ECC/ES256)
 # SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET=<your-supabase-jwt-secret>
 
 # ── LiteLLM / Gemini ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 # Model string accepted by LiteLLM: https://docs.litellm.ai/docs/providers
+# Set it explicitly: when unset, receipt OCR, chat and the support agent each fall back to a
+# different built-in default.
 LITELLM_MODEL=gemini/gemini-3.6-flash-lite
 
 # Provide the API key for whichever provider you use:
 GOOGLE_API_KEY=<your-google-ai-studio-api-key>
+# GEMINI_API_KEY=<same key>                # alternative name, read by the support agent only
 # OPENAI_API_KEY=<your-openai-key>         # uncomment if using OpenAI
 # ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=<your-anthropic-key>   # uncomment if using Claude
 
 # ── Security ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
-# Shared HMAC secret between the Flutter app and this service.
+# User routes are authenticated by the caller's Supabase JWT, not by these values.
+# HMAC key for the X-Signature header (defense in depth, never user authentication). With a
+# valid JWT, unsigned requests are served and an invalid/stale signature (e.g. app builds signing
+# with a rotated secret) is logged and ignored; without a valid JWT a bad signature is 401. If this
+# is empty, signatures cannot be verified and are treated the same way. Server-to-server webhook
+# routes without a JWT (none today) must require a valid signature.
 # Generate with: python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))"
 WEBHOOK_SECRET=<generate-a-random-hex-string>
 
-# App-level auth token for firewall middleware (Flutter <-> FastAPI)
+# Legacy firewall pass for old app builds only (never user authentication; current builds do not
+# send X-App-Token). Rotate it if it was ever exposed.
 APP_AUTH_TOKEN=<generate-a-random-token>
 
+# HMAC key (at least 32 characters) for the preview_token of chat / receipt previews: a commit
+# that sends the token back is saved without a second LLM call. Use the same value on every
+# instance. Unset (or shorter), each process uses a random key and logs a warning: a commit that
+# reaches another instance, or comes after a restart, is parsed by the LLM again (still correct).
+# Rotating it only makes open previews re-parse. Never ship it to the app.
+# Generate with: python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(32))"
+PREVIEW_TOKEN_SECRET=<generate-a-random-hex-string>
+
+# ── Contact / support / VIP early-access email (POST /public/inquiries, /support/inquiries)
+# Without a provider these endpoints answer 503 and nothing is sent (they never fake success).
+# Recipient of every inquiry (defaults to abedmowafaq@gmail.com when unset).
+CONTACT_RECIPIENT_EMAIL=abedmowafaq@gmail.com
+# Sender of every inquiry email (Reply-To is always the person who submitted the form).
+# Defaults to the company mailbox below when unset.
+MAIL_FROM=Budget Tracker <fmscoinfo@fmsco.com.sa>
+# Option A (recommended on Railway, which blocks outbound SMTP on non-Pro plans): Resend HTTP API.
+# The fmsco.com.sa domain must be verified in Resend (SPF + DKIM DNS records) to send as MAIL_FROM.
+# RESEND_API_KEY=<your-resend-api-key>
+# RESEND_FROM=<optional; overrides MAIL_FROM for Resend only>
+# Option B: SMTP (used when RESEND_API_KEY is empty). TLS is mandatory.
+# Use the SMTP server and credentials of the fmscoinfo@fmsco.com.sa mailbox itself, otherwise
+# the server may refuse to send as that address or recipients may treat it as spoofed.
+# SMTP_HOST=<smtp-host-of-the-fmsco.com.sa-mailbox>
+# SMTP_PORT=587
+# SMTP_SECURITY=starttls          # starttls (587) or ssl (465); defaults from the port
+# SMTP_USERNAME=fmscoinfo@fmsco.com.sa
+# SMTP_PASSWORD=<mailbox-password-or-app-password>
+# SMTP_FROM=<optional; overrides MAIL_FROM for SMTP only>
+# Per-IP limits use X-Forwarded-For only from these proxy IPs (comma-separated).
+# TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS=127.0.0.1,::1
+# Trust X-Forwarded-For from any peer: 1 = yes, 0 = no; unset = yes on Railway (RAILWAY_ENVIRONMENT).
+# ASSUMPTION: with 1 (or unset on Railway) the service must be reachable ONLY through Railway's
+# HTTP edge (or the proxy chain counted below). Any other ingress (a Railway TCP proxy, private
+# networking from another service, a public port) lets a caller send its own X-Forwarded-For and
+# pick its rate-limit identity. Set 0 (and TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS) if such ingress exists.
+# TRUST_PROXY_HEADERS=
+# Proxies appending to X-Forwarded-For in front of the app (Railway edge = 1). Must EQUAL the
+# real hop count: too high and the client-supplied entry before the real one is used.
+# TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS=1
 
 # ── Server ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
+# production on every deployment. UNSET COUNTS AS PRODUCTION. Use development (or dev, local,
+# test) on your machine: it shows /docs, skips signature checks when WEBHOOK_SECRET is empty and
+# lets requests through when the usage-quota check is inconclusive.
+ENV=development
 PORT=8000
 RELOAD=false    # Set to true for hot-reload during development
+# Shared store for rate limits across workers/instances; without it limits are per process.
+# docker-compose.yml does not start a Redis service: point this at your own instance.
+# REDIS_URL=redis://<host>:6379/0

-    <div class="faqit" onclick="tgFaq(this)"><button class="faqtr"><span data-i18n="fq1">هل يقرأ التطبيق رسائل SMS البنكية؟</span><span class="faqic">+</span></button><div class="faqbd" data-i18n="fa1">لا تماماً. التطبيق لا يطلب إذن قراءة الرسائل نهائياً. الإدخال يدوي أو صوتي أو عبر مسح QR الفاتورة فقط — خصوصيتك وأمان هاتفك خط أحمر.</div></div>
-    <div class="faqit" onclick="tgFaq(this)"><button class="faqtr"><span data-i18n="fq2">كيف يعمل مسح فاتورة ZATCA بالذكاء الاصطناعي؟</span><span class="faqic">+</span></button><div class="faqbd" data-i18n="fa2">تفتح كاميرا التطبيق وتمسح رمز QR لأي فاتورة إلكترونية سعودية متوافقة مع ZATCA. يستخرج التطبيق اسم المنشأة، الإجمالي، وضريبة القيمة المضافة 15% والتاريخ فورياً.</div></div>
-    <div class="faqit" onclick="tgFaq(this)"><button class="faqtr"><span data-i18n="fq3">كيف أُضيف أسماء أبنائي وشريكي لتوزيع المصاريف؟</span><span class="faqic">+</span></button><div class="faqbd" data-i18n="fa3">من إعدادات التطبيق تحت "هوية المنزل"، أضف أسماء الشريك والأبناء. عند تسجيل أي مصروف تختار بضغطة زر "لصالح من" لتقسيم النفقات بدقة وشفافية.</div></div>
-    <div class="faqit" onclick="tgFaq(this)"><button class="faqtr"><span data-i18n="fq4">هل يمكنني تعديل معاملة أو تصنيفها بعد حفظها؟</span><span class="faqic">+</span></button><div class="faqbd" data-i18n="fa4">نعم بكل تأكيد. يمكنك تعديل المبلغ، الفئة، الفئة الفرعية، أو الدافع والمستفيد لأي معاملة في أي وقت من سجل المعاملات.</div></div>
-    <div class="faqit" onclick="tgFaq(this)"><button class="faqtr"><span data-i18n="fq5">ما الفرق بين الفئة الرئيسية والفئة الفرعية؟</span><span class="faqic">+</span></button><div class="faqbd" data-i18n="fa5">الفئة الرئيسية مثل (مطاعم وتغذية)، والفئة الفرعية أدق مثل (وجبات سريعة — البيك، كنتاكي). يمكنك تخصيص فئاتك الفرعية لتناسب نمط إنفاق أسرتك بدقة.</div></div>
-    <div class="faqit" onclick="tgFaq(this)"><button class="faqtr"><span data-i18n="fq6">هل التطبيق متوفر للتحميل الآن؟</span><span class="faqic">+</span></button><div class="faqbd" data-i18n="fa6">التطبيق قيد المرحلة التجريبية المتقدمة وسيُطرح قريباً على Google Play وApp Store وAppGallery. يمكنك التواصل مع المطور للحصول على وصول تجريبي مبكر.</div></div>
-  </div>

-  <!-- LEGAL & COMPLIANCE -->
-  <div class="legc">
-    <div class="sh"><span class="seye">LEGAL</span><h2 class="stit" style="font-size:clamp(22px,3vw,32px)" data-i18n="lt">الشروط والخصوصية</h2></div>
-    <div class="ltabs">
-      <button class="ltab on" onclick="swLeg('p',this)" data-i18n="ll1">سياسة الخصوصية</button>
-      <button class="ltab"    onclick="swLeg('t',this)" data-i18n="ll2">شروط الاستخدام</button>
-    </div>
-    <div id="lp" class="lscr">
-      <h4 data-i18n="lp1h">جمع البيانات والخصوصية</h4><p data-i18n="lp1p">لا نقوم بجمع أو طلب بيانات بنكية أو صلاحيات SMS. تُخزّن كافة بيانات الميزانية مشفرة داخل قاعدة بيانات Supabase المؤمنة ولا يتم بيعها أو مشاركتها.</p>
-      <h4 data-i18n="lp2h">معالجة الذكاء الاصطناعي</h4><p data-i18n="lp2p">تُعالج الرسائل النصية والصوتية بواسطة نماذج الذكاء الاصطناعي لاستخراج بيانات المصروف فقط ولا تُستخدم لتدريب نماذج عامة دون موافقة.</p>
-      <h4 data-i18n="lp3h">حذف الحساب والبيانات</h4><p data-i18n="lp3p">يحق للمستخدم طلب الحذف الكامل لحسابه وسجلاته في أي وقت عبر إعدادات التطبيق أو عبر مراسلة الدعم الفني.</p>
-    </div>
-    <div id="lt2" class="lscr" style="display:none">
-      <h4 data-i18n="lt1h">نطاق الاستخدام</h4><p data-i18n="lt1p">المنصة مخصصة لإدارة وحوكمة ميزانيات الأسر والأفراد في المملكة العربية السعودية للاستخدام الشخصي غير التجاري.</p>
-      <h4 data-i18n="lt2h">المسؤولية المالية</h4><p data-i18n="lt2p">التطبيق يقدم أدوات تنظيمية واقتراحات استرشادية مبنية على الذكاء الاصطناعي ولا يُعد بديلاً عن المشورة المالية الرسمية.</p>
-      <h4 data-i18n="lt3h">التحديثات والتطوير</h4><p data-i18n="lt3p">تحتفظ إدارة منصة FMSCO بحق تحديث المزايا والشروط دورياً لتحسين جودة وأمان الخدمة مع إشعار المستخدمين.</p>
-    </div>

-function updSim(v) {
-  document.getElementById('sv').textContent = v;
-  const t = new Date().getDate();
-  let d = parseInt(v) - t;
-  if (d <= 0) d += 30;
-  const r = Math.round(12000 / Math.max(d, 1));
-  const res = Math.max(0, 12000 - r * d);
-  document.getElementById('sd').innerHTML = d + ' <small style="font-size:13px">' + (L === 'ar' ? 'يوم' : 'days') + '</small>';
-  document.getElementById('sr').innerHTML = r.toLocaleString() + ' <small style="font-size:13px">' + (L === 'ar' ? 'ر.س/يوم' : 'SAR/day') + '</small>';
-  document.getElementById('sres').innerHTML = res.toLocaleString() + ' <small style="font-size:13px">' + (L === 'ar' ? 'ر.س' : 'SAR') + '</small>';
-}
-
-document.getElementById('pslider').addEventListener('input', function() {
-  updSim(this.value);
-});

-const KT = { k1: 50, k2: 97, k3: 31, k4: 100 };
-function aniK(id, tg, dur) {
-  const el = document.getElementById(id);
-  if (!el) return;
-  let s = 0;
-  const st = tg / (dur / 16);
-  (function u() {
-    s = Math.min(s + st, tg);
-    el.textContent = Math.round(s);
-    if (s < tg) requestAnimationFrame(u);
-  })();
-}
-
-new IntersectionObserver((en) => {
-  en.forEach(e => {

-    }
-  });
-}, { threshold: 0.3 }).observe(document.querySelector('.kpis'));
-
-function tgFaq(el) {

-  document.querySelectorAll('.faqit').forEach(i => i.classList.remove('op'));
-  if (!op) el.classList.add('op');
-}

+SIGNATURE_HEADER = "X-Signature"
+_INVALID_SIGNATURE_DETAIL = "Invalid request signature."
+# A stale signature is logged at most once per (route, user) per interval.
+_STALE_SIGNATURE_LOG_INTERVAL_SECONDS = 300.0
+_STALE_SIGNATURE_LOG_MAX_KEYS = 2048
+_STALE_SIGNATURE_LOGGED: dict = {}
+

+def _reset_stale_signature_log() -> None:
+    """Forget which stale-signature warnings were emitted (tests)."""
+    _STALE_SIGNATURE_LOGGED.clear()
+

+def _user_ref(user_id: str) -> str:
+    """Short, non-reversible reference to a user for logs (never the raw id)."""
+    import hashlib
+
+    return hashlib.sha256(str(user_id).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:12]
+
+
+def _warn_ignored_signature(route: str, user_id: str) -> None:
+    now = _monotonic()
+    key = (route, _user_ref(user_id))
+    last = _STALE_SIGNATURE_LOGGED.get(key)
+    if last is not None and now - last < _STALE_SIGNATURE_LOG_INTERVAL_SECONDS:
+        return
+    if len(_STALE_SIGNATURE_LOGGED) >= _STALE_SIGNATURE_LOG_MAX_KEYS:
+        cutoff = now - _STALE_SIGNATURE_LOG_INTERVAL_SECONDS
+        for stale_key in [k for k, t in _STALE_SIGNATURE_LOGGED.items() if t < cutoff]:
+            _STALE_SIGNATURE_LOGGED.pop(stale_key, None)
+        if len(_STALE_SIGNATURE_LOGGED) >= _STALE_SIGNATURE_LOG_MAX_KEYS:
+            _STALE_SIGNATURE_LOGGED.clear()
+    _STALE_SIGNATURE_LOGGED[key] = now
+    if not os.environ.get("WEBHOOK_SECRET", "").strip():
+        reason = "cannot be verified (WEBHOOK_SECRET is not set)"
+    else:
+        reason = "does not match WEBHOOK_SECRET (app build signing with a rotated secret?)"
+    logger.warning(
+        "Ignoring %s header on %s for user %s: it %s. The request is authenticated by its JWT.",
+        SIGNATURE_HEADER, route, key[1], reason,
     )
 
 
+async def verify_signature_if_present(request: Request) -> None:
+    """
+    Router-wide dependency: X-Signature is defense in depth on user routes, never their
+    authentication (the Supabase JWT is).
+
+    - No header, or a valid signature: nothing to do.
+    - Invalid or unverifiable signature (wrong HMAC, malformed, or WEBHOOK_SECRET unset in
+      production) WITH a valid JWT: served, with a rate-limited warning naming the route and a
+      hash of the user id. Compatibility: WEBHOOK_SECRET has been rotated, so every installed
+      app build signs with the old value; rejecting would break all their chat/receipt calls.
+    - Invalid signature WITHOUT a valid JWT: 401 (there is no credential at all).
+
+    Routes where the signature IS the authentication (server-to-server webhooks without a JWT;
+    none today) must call ``utils.verify_signature`` themselves and reject a missing or invalid
+    signature.
+    """
+    signature = request.headers.get(SIGNATURE_HEADER)
+    if signature is None:
+        return
+    body = await request.body()  # cached on the request; the route reads the same bytes
+    if verify_signature(body, signature):
+        return
+
+    claims = None
+    auth_header = request.headers.get("Authorization", "")
+    if auth_header.startswith("Bearer "):
+        try:
+            claims = await decode_token(auth_header[7:].strip())
+        except HTTPException:
+            claims = None
+    if not claims or not claims.get("sub"):
+        logger.info("Rejected request with an invalid %s header and no valid JWT.", SIGNATURE_HEADER)
+        raise HTTPException(status_code=status.HTTP_401_UNAUTHORIZED, detail=_INVALID_SIGNATURE_DETAIL)

-  - "لي / لي لحالي / ع حسابي الشخصي" -> "me"

+  - "للعيال / للأولاد / للأطفال / للبنات" -> "children"

+def _cue_in(text: str, cue: str) -> bool:
+    """Whether ``cue`` occurs in ``text`` as a word (see _NEW_CATEGORY_CUES)."""
+    import re
+
+    if cue.isascii():
+        return re.search(r"\b" + re.escape(cue) + r"\b", text) is not None
+    if " " in cue:
+        return cue in text
+    stem = cue[2:] if cue.startswith("ال") and len(cue) > 4 else cue
+    pattern = rf"(?<![{_ARABIC_LETTER}])(?:[وبلف])?(?:ال|لل)?{re.escape(stem)}(?![{_ARABIC_LETTER}])"
+    return re.search(pattern, text) is not None
+
+
+def new_category_sub_code(category_code: str, text: str) -> Optional[str]:
+    """The sub-code of a new category for the text (its default when no cue matches)."""
+    subs = NEW_CATEGORY_SUB_CODES.get(category_code)
+    if not subs:
+        return None
+    lower = text.lower()
+    for sub_code, cues in subs:
+        if not cues or any(_cue_in(lower, cue) for cue in cues):
+            return sub_code
+    return subs[-1][0]
+
+
+def new_category_for_text(text: str) -> Optional[str]:
+    """One of the new household categories when the text names it, else None."""
+    lower = text.lower()
+    for code, cues in _NEW_CATEGORY_CUES:
+        if any(_cue_in(lower, cue) for cue in cues):
+            return code
+    return None
+
+
+def resolve_category_in_taxonomy(category_code: Optional[str], codes: list) -> str:
+    """
+    The code to store for a parsed (not user-chosen) category: itself when the taxonomy has it,
+    the legacy code for a new system code whose migration is not applied yet, OPEX-MISC for a code
+    the model made up. An empty taxonomy (lookup failed) leaves the decision to the database.
+    """
+    code = (category_code or DEFAULT_CATEGORY_CODE).strip() or DEFAULT_CATEGORY_CODE
+    known = {getattr(c, "code", None) for c in codes or []}
+    if not known or code in known:
+        return code
+    legacy = LEGACY_CATEGORY_FALLBACK.get(code, DEFAULT_CATEGORY_CODE)
+    return legacy if legacy in known else DEFAULT_CATEGORY_CODE

+    if token is None:
+        return None
+    check = verify_preview_token(token, KIND_CHAT, user_id, household_id)  # InvalidPreviewToken

+        logger.info("Chat preview token %s: re-parsing.", check.status)
+        return None

+        return None
+    try:
+        return ParsedChatExpense(**check.payload)
+    except Exception as exc:  # signed by us, so only a format change between releases
+        raise InvalidPreviewToken("payload no longer valid") from exc
+

--- a/ai_service/graph.py
+++ /dev/null
@@ -1,382 +0,0 @@
-"""
-LangGraph state machine for the Budget Tracker AI microservice.
-
-Flow:
-  receive_sms → extract_fields → lookup_category → check_budget
-             → [reallocate_if_needed] → write_transaction → END
-
-Every node receives the full AgentState and returns a partial dict
-with only the fields it mutates — LangGraph merges the rest automatically.
-"""
-
-from __future__ import annotations
-
-import json
-import logging
-import os
-import re
-from datetime import datetime, date, timezone
-from typing import Any
-
-import litellm
-from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END
-
-import supabase_client as db
-from models import AgentState, CostControlCode
-
-logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
-
-# ─── Module-level cache for cost control codes (loaded once at import time) ───
-_cost_codes: list[CostControlCode] = []
-
-ARABIC_TO_ENGLISH_DIGITS = str.maketrans("٠١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩", "0123456789")
-
-
-# =============================================================================
-# HELPERS
-# =============================================================================
-
-def _normalise_arabic(text: str) -> str:
-    """Transliterate Arabic-Indic numerals to ASCII digits."""
-    return text.translate(ARABIC_TO_ENGLISH_DIGITS)
-
-
-def _get_cost_codes() -> list[CostControlCode]:
-    """Return cached cost control codes, fetching from Supabase on first call."""
-    global _cost_codes
-    if not _cost_codes:
-        _cost_codes = db.fetch_all_cost_control_codes()
-    return _cost_codes
-
-
-def _first_day_of_month(dt: datetime) -> date:
-    return dt.date().replace(day=1)
-
-
-# =============================================================================
-# NODE 1 — receive_sms
-# Deduplication guard. Returns early if SMS was already processed.
-# =============================================================================
-
-def receive_sms(state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]:
-    logger.info("[receive_sms] sender=%s household=%s", state.sender, state.household_id)
-
-    # Allowed sender whitelist
-    allowed = [s.strip().lower() for s in os.environ.get("ALLOWED_SENDERS", "snb,alrajhi").split(",")]
-    if state.sender.lower() not in allowed:
-        logger.warning("[receive_sms] Rejected: sender '%s' not in whitelist.", state.sender)
-        return {"rejection_reason": f"Sender '{state.sender}' is not a whitelisted bank."}
-
-    # Duplicate check
-    if db.is_duplicate_sms(state.raw_sms, state.household_id):
-        logger.warning("[receive_sms] Duplicate SMS detected — skipping.")
-        return {"rejection_reason": "Duplicate SMS received within the deduplication window."}
-
-    return {}   # pass-through
-
-
-# =============================================================================
-# NODE 2 — extract_fields
-# Uses LiteLLM to parse amount, currency, merchant, and timestamp from raw SMS.
-# =============================================================================
-
-EXTRACTION_SYSTEM_PROMPT = """
-You are a financial SMS parser for Saudi banks (SNB and Al Rajhi Bank).
-
-Your job is to extract structured data from a bank SMS notification.
-Respond ONLY with a valid JSON object — no markdown, no explanation.
-
-Required fields:
-  "amount"    : float  (the transaction amount; convert Arabic numerals if needed)
-  "currency"  : string (default "SAR"; use "USD", "EUR" if explicitly stated)
-  "merchant"  : string (business or person name; translate to English if Arabic)
-  "timestamp" : string (ISO-8601 datetime; use the device received_at if not in SMS)
-  "is_transaction": bool (false if this is an OTP, balance inquiry, or marketing SMS)
-
-Rules:
-- Arabic-Indic digits (٠-٩) must be converted to standard digits (0-9).
-- If the merchant is in Arabic, provide an English transliteration.
-- If no timestamp is in the SMS, output the value of received_at provided below.
-- NEVER include any text outside the JSON object.
-""".strip()
-
-
-def extract_fields(state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]:
-    logger.info("[extract_fields] Extracting from SMS (len=%d).", len(state.raw_sms))
-
-    normalised_sms = _normalise_arabic(state.raw_sms)
-    model = os.environ.get("LITELLM_MODEL", "gemini/gemini-2.0-flash-lite")
-
-    user_content = (
-        f"SMS text:\n{normalised_sms}\n\n"
-        f"received_at: {state.received_at}\n"
-        f"sender: {state.sender}"
-    )
-
-    try:
-        response = litellm.completion(
-            model=model,
-            messages=[
-                {"role": "system", "content": EXTRACTION_SYSTEM_PROMPT},
-                {"role": "user", "content": user_content},
-            ],
-            temperature=1.0,
-            max_tokens=300,
-        )
-        raw_json = response.choices[0].message.content.strip()
-
-        # Strip markdown fences if model disobeys the system prompt
-        raw_json = re.sub(r"^```(?:json)?\n?", "", raw_json)
-        raw_json = re.sub(r"\n?```$", "", raw_json)
-
-        parsed = json.loads(raw_json)
-    except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
-        logger.error("[extract_fields] JSON parse error: %s | raw=%s", exc, raw_json)
-        return {"error": f"LLM returned non-JSON response: {exc}"}
-    except Exception as exc:
-        logger.error("[extract_fields] LiteLLM call failed: %s", exc)
-        return {"error": f"LiteLLM error: {exc}"}
-
-    if not parsed.get("is_transaction", True):
-        return {"rejection_reason": "SMS is not a financial transaction (OTP/marketing)."}
-
-    # Parse timestamp
-    try:
-        ts = datetime.fromisoformat(parsed["timestamp"].replace("Z", "+00:00"))
-    except Exception:
-        ts = datetime.now(timezone.utc)
-
-    logger.info(
-        "[extract_fields] amount=%.2f currency=%s merchant=%s timestamp=%s",
-        parsed.get("amount", 0), parsed.get("currency", "SAR"),
-        parsed.get("merchant", "?"), ts.isoformat(),
-    )
-
-    return {
-        "amount": float(parsed.get("amount", 0)),
-        "currency": parsed.get("currency", "SAR"),
-        "merchant": parsed.get("merchant", "Unknown"),
-        "timestamp": ts,
-        "extraction_raw": raw_json,
-    }
-
-
-# =============================================================================
-# NODE 3 — lookup_category
-# Keyword-matches the merchant against cost_control_codes.
-# Falls back to OPEX-MISC.
-# =============================================================================
-
-def lookup_category(state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]:
-    if state.error or state.rejection_reason:
-        return {}
-
-    logger.info("[lookup_category] merchant='%s'", state.merchant)
-    codes = _get_cost_codes()
-    match = db.match_category(state.merchant or "", codes)
-
-    if match:
-        logger.info("[lookup_category] Matched: %s (%s)", match.code, match.category)
-        return {"category_code": match.code, "category_name": match.category}
-    else:
-        # Fallback to OPEX-MISC
-        misc = next((c for c in codes if c.code == "OPEX-MISC"), None)
-        code = misc.code if misc else "OPEX-MISC"
-        name = misc.category if misc else "Miscellaneous"
-        logger.warning("[lookup_category] No keyword match — falling back to %s.", code)
-        return {"category_code": code, "category_name": name}
-
-
-# =============================================================================
-# NODE 4 — check_budget
-# Fetches the current month's budget for this category.
-# =============================================================================
-
-def check_budget(state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]:
-    if state.error or state.rejection_reason:
-        return {}
-
-    month = _first_day_of_month(state.timestamp or datetime.now(timezone.utc))
-    logger.info(
-        "[check_budget] household=%s category=%s month=%s amount=%.2f",
-        state.household_id, state.category_code, month, state.amount,
-    )
-
-    budget = db.fetch_budget(state.household_id, state.category_code, month)
-    if not budget:
-        # No budget set — log transaction without budget enforcement
-        logger.warning("[check_budget] No budget row found; proceeding without enforcement.")
-        return {
-            "budget_id": None,
-            "allocated_amount": None,
-            "spent_amount": None,
-            "remaining_balance": None,
-        }
-
-    return {
-        "budget_id": budget.id,
-        "allocated_amount": budget.allocated_amount,
-        "spent_amount": budget.spent_amount,
-        "remaining_balance": budget.remaining_amount,
-    }
-
-
-# =============================================================================
-# NODE 5 — reallocate_if_needed
-# If amount > remaining_balance, pull the deficit from flexible budgets.
-# =============================================================================
-
-def reallocate_if_needed(state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]:
-    if state.error or state.rejection_reason:
-        return {}
-
-    # No enforcement needed if no budget was found or there's sufficient balance
-    if state.remaining_balance is None or state.amount <= state.remaining_balance:
-        return {}
-
-    deficit = state.amount - state.remaining_balance
-    logger.warning(
-        "[reallocate] Budget insufficient! amount=%.2f remaining=%.2f deficit=%.2f",
-        state.amount, state.remaining_balance, deficit,
-    )
-
-    month = _first_day_of_month(state.timestamp or datetime.now(timezone.utc))
-    flexible = db.fetch_flexible_budgets(state.household_id, month, exclude_code=state.category_code)
-
-    if not flexible:
-        logger.warning("[reallocate] No flexible budgets available — proceeding anyway.")
-        return {}
-
-    # Cascade deductions across flexible budgets if needed
-    remaining_deficit = deficit
-    source_budget = None
-
-    for flex_budget in flexible:
-        if remaining_deficit <= 0:
-            break
-        deduction = min(remaining_deficit, flex_budget.remaining_amount)
-        if state.budget_id:
-            db.reallocate_budget(flex_budget.id, state.budget_id, deduction)
-        remaining_deficit -= deduction
-        if source_budget is None:
-            source_budget = flex_budget  # track primary source for tagging
-        logger.info(
-            "[reallocate] Reallocated %.2f from '%s' (id=%s) to '%s' (id=%s).",
-            deduction, flex_budget.category_code, flex_budget.id,
-            state.category_code, state.budget_id,
-        )
-
-    return {
-        "is_reallocated": True,
-        "reallocated_from_budget_id": source_budget.id if source_budget else None,
-        "reallocated_from_category": source_budget.category_code if source_budget else None,
-    }
-
-
-# =============================================================================
-# NODE 6 — write_transaction
-# Inserts the final transaction record into Supabase.
-# The DB trigger handles updating budgets.spent_amount automatically.
-# =============================================================================
-
-def write_transaction(state: AgentState) -> dict[str, Any]:
-    if state.error or state.rejection_reason:
-        return {}
-
-    logger.info("[write_transaction] Inserting transaction for household=%s.", state.household_id)
-
-    transaction_id = db.insert_transaction(
-        household_id=state.household_id,
-        amount=state.amount,
-        currency=state.currency,
-        merchant=state.merchant or "Unknown",
-        category_code=state.category_code or "OPEX-MISC",
-        timestamp=state.timestamp.isoformat() if state.timestamp else datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(),
-        raw_sms=state.raw_sms,
-        is_reallocated=state.is_reallocated,
-        reallocated_from_budget_id=state.reallocated_from_budget_id,
-    )
-
-    logger.info("[write_transaction] Done. transaction_id=%s", transaction_id)
-    return {"transaction_id": transaction_id}
-
-
-# =============================================================================
-# ROUTING — conditional edges
-# =============================================================================
-
-def route_after_receive(state: AgentState) -> str:
-    """If rejected at receive stage, skip to END."""
-    if state.rejection_reason:
-        return "end"
-    return "extract_fields"
-
-
-def route_after_extract(state: AgentState) -> str:
-    """If extraction failed or SMS is non-transactional, skip to END."""
-    if state.error or state.rejection_reason:
-        return "end"
-    return "lookup_category"
-
-
-def route_after_check_budget(state: AgentState) -> str:
-    """Decide whether reallocation is needed."""
-    if state.error or state.rejection_reason:
-        return "end"
-    if (
-        state.remaining_balance is not None
-        and state.amount is not None
-        and state.amount > state.remaining_balance
-    ):
-        return "reallocate_if_needed"
-    return "write_transaction"
-
-
-# =============================================================================
-# GRAPH ASSEMBLY
-# =============================================================================
-
-def build_graph() -> Any:
-    """Compile and return the LangGraph StateGraph."""
-    builder = StateGraph(AgentState)
-
-    # Add nodes
-    builder.add_node("receive_sms", receive_sms)
-    builder.add_node("extract_fields", extract_fields)
-    builder.add_node("lookup_category", lookup_category)
-    builder.add_node("check_budget", check_budget)
-    builder.add_node("reallocate_if_needed", reallocate_if_needed)
-    builder.add_node("write_transaction", write_transaction)
-
-    # Entry point
-    builder.set_entry_point("receive_sms")
-
-    # Edges
-    builder.add_conditional_edges(
-        "receive_sms",
-        route_after_receive,
-        {"end": END, "extract_fields": "extract_fields"},
-    )
-    builder.add_conditional_edges(
-        "extract_fields",
-        route_after_extract,
-        {"end": END, "lookup_category": "lookup_category"},
-    )
-    builder.add_edge("lookup_category", "check_budget")
-    builder.add_conditional_edges(
-        "check_budget",
-        route_after_check_budget,
-        {
-            "end": END,
-            "reallocate_if_needed": "reallocate_if_needed",
-            "write_transaction": "write_transaction",
-        },
-    )
-    builder.add_edge("reallocate_if_needed", "write_transaction")
-    builder.add_edge("write_transaction", END)
-
-    return builder.compile()
-
-
-# Module-level compiled graph (imported by main.py)
-sms_graph = build_graph()
