+## 4. Architectural Recommendations & Modernization Blueprint
+
+1. **One source of truth for authorization.** Most High findings are one class of bug: the backend uses a privileged Supabase client and re-implements household checks by hand. Prefer forwarding the user's JWT to PostgREST so RLS enforces access, and reserve the secret key for narrow `SECURITY DEFINER` RPCs that check `auth.uid()` membership themselves. This removes the IDOR class instead of patching instances.
+2. **Money as integers end to end.** Store and compute halalas as `bigint` (or keep `numeric(14,2)` with `CHECK` constraints in DB), `Decimal` in Python (done), and a `Money` value type over `int` in Dart (MOB-29). Ban `double` for currency via an analyzer lint.
+3. **Single cycle specification.** `get_saudi_cycle_for_timestamp` is canonical. Keep the 109 vectors as a shared JSON fixture consumed by the SQL, pytest and Flutter suites so the three implementations cannot drift again.
+4. **Replayable migrations.** Re-baseline from live (`supabase db pull`), renumber duplicates, (the owner chose not to use GitHub Actions; run the gate commands in §5 before each release).
+5. **No shared secrets in clients.** Finish the move to JWT-only: after the new backend is live and old builds age out, stop accepting `X-App-Token`. `WEBHOOK_SECRET` is already optional in app builds (MOB-23, resolved): leave it out; a stale signature from an old build is logged and ignored while the JWT is valid.
+6. **Durable idempotency and quotas.** Make Redis mandatory in production (or add an `idempotency_keys` table) so dedup and rate limits hold across instances (API-33, MOB-06/12).
+7. **Domain decisions encoded in schema.** Add `is_tabarru` and household-scoped sub-categories. UI-24 (`transactions.nafaqah_class`, `member_allowances`, `spouse_reimbursements`) and DB-16/DB-18 (creator binding, owner-or-admin writes, admin-only pool withdrawals, co-admins with a protected primary admin) are decided and enforced in the database.
+8. **Mobile hardening.** Tokens are now in `flutter_secure_storage` (MOB-19); certificate/https enforcement already added; build a release APK in CI to validate the Android changes made here.
+9. **Repository hygiene.** SMS/dev simulation scripts, the legacy SMS pipeline and the `sms` transaction channel are deleted (API-25, guarded by tests); keep secrets only in environment/secret managers; keep `.env` out of Docker build context (`.dockerignore` added).
+

+## 6. Owner Actions & Release Plan
+
+### 6.1 Before anything else
+1. **Rotate secrets.** Owner reports (2026-10-20) that a new `WEBHOOK_SECRET` is set on Railway and the values shared for the audit are test-only. **Still confirm `APP_AUTH_TOKEN` was rotated** — the old values remain in public git history (gitleaks finds 9 hits in `f17eb2b`).
+2. **Service key.** Owner reports the `sb_secret_…` key is set on Railway. Either `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` or `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` works; an `sb_secret_` key wins over a legacy JWT and an anon/publishable value is ignored with a startup warning. Requires `supabase>=2.16.0` (older supabase-py rejects `sb_secret_` keys). The service fails closed without a privileged key, so a wrong value shows up immediately as 500s.
+3. **Check** `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET`: it is empty, so only ES256 tokens verified against the project JWKS are accepted. If the project still signs user tokens with the legacy HS256 secret, set it or every request returns 401.
+4. **Set** `ENV=production`, `TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS`, and `REDIS_URL` on the production service.
+5. **Email delivery:** set `RESEND_API_KEY` (preferred on Railway, which blocks SMTP ports below the Pro plan; `fmsco.com.sa` verified) or `SMTP_HOST`/`SMTP_PORT`/`SMTP_USERNAME`/`SMTP_PASSWORD` for the `fmscoinfo@fmsco.com.sa` mailbox. Optional: `CONTACT_RECIPIENT_EMAIL` (default `abedmowafaq@gmail.com`), `MAIL_FROM`. Until set, the forms return a clear error.
+6. **Supabase Auth emails** (sign-up, password reset) are configured in the Supabase dashboard, not in this repo: set Authentication → SMTP Settings → Sender email to `fmscoinfo@fmsco.com.sa` so all mail comes from one address.
+7. **Set** `PREVIEW_TOKEN_SECRET` (32+ random characters, e.g. `openssl rand -hex 32`), the same value on every Railway instance. It signs chat/receipt previews so a confirmed expense is saved without a second LLM call. Without it each process uses a random key (logged as a warning): everything still works, but the saving only applies when the commit reaches the instance that issued the preview.
+8. **Backups.** Scheduled daily backups are deferred by the owner (they need the Supabase Pro plan). This is a known risk: until they exist, a bad write or deletion on live cannot be undone from a daily snapshot. A one-off manual dump before applying the pending migrations is still required and costs nothing: `pg_dump --schema=public --data-only` (plus `--schema-only`) with the database connection string from Dashboard → Connect, stored off the server.
+
+### 6.2 Deployment order
+1. **Database:** follow [`live_db_preflight.md`](live_db_preflight.md).
+   - **✅ Applied to live on 2026-10-20** (owner-approved): read-only data backup taken first; all 14 files applied in order with no errors; part B matched §7 exactly (`budgets_spent_total` 9112.42 and `accounts_balance_total` 360.00 unchanged); the 14 versions are recorded in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. Verified compatible with the currently deployed (pre-audit) backend and app: they always send an explicit `source`, and service-role inserts pass the new creator trigger unchanged.
+   - **Verdict: safe to apply.** Live was compared read-only with the repo, and a faithful local replica of live passed the 14-file batch with the DB suite at 20/20.
+   - **Order:** apply the pre-flight `20261020005000_preflight_live_alignment.sql` first, then the 13 audit migrations `20261020010000` … `20261020400000`. Use the SQL editor, one file per run, in order (§5).
+   - **Before:** run part A of [`live_db_preflight_checks.sql`](live_db_preflight_checks.sql) and note the totals.
+   - **After:** run part B and compare with §7.
+   - **Drift that matters:**
+     - `reallocate_budget` is missing on live; `20261020030000` creates it.
+     - Live-only `households.rollover_rule` is captured by the pre-flight.
+     - Live's `rls_auto_enable()` loses its anon EXECUTE.
+     - All 14 live transactions have no recorded creator and become admin-only (owner decision).
+   - **MOB-03 answered:** live `transactions` has no `paid_by` / `beneficiary` columns.
+   - **Coupling:** `20261020200000` rejects new `source = 'sms'` rows, so ship it with the new app build. `20261020300000` and `20261020400000` go before the backend that calls their RPCs.
+   - **CLI:** do not use `supabase db push` until the DB-15 re-baseline (§5.3).
+   - **Rollback:** [`../rollback/20261020_audit_batch_rollback_snapshot.sql`](../rollback/20261020_audit_batch_rollback_snapshot.sql).
+   - **Pending (rounds 2, 3 and 3b): five files, not yet applied to live.** In order: `20261020700000_fable_db_hardening.sql` → `20261020750000_installment_pay_atomic.sql` → `20261020800000_household_roles_and_nafaqah_integrity.sql` → `20261020900000_household_type_and_round2_fixes.sql` → `20261021000000_saudi_taxonomy_and_bnpl_schedule.sql`. Follow [`live_db_preflight_round3.md`](live_db_preflight_round3.md) §6 for the first four and its "Round 3b" section for the fifth (run its read-only pre-check first: live has one code and four sub-categories the repo does not; on a collision the file aborts cleanly). Never re-run an earlier file after `900000`. Rollbacks: [`../rollback/`](../rollback/) (newest first).
+2. **Backend:** deploy `ai_service` from this branch. The HEAD backend needs all five pending files applied first. It accepts both old app builds (`X-App-Token` at the firewall, plus their JWT) and the new JWT-only client. **Signed requests:** installed builds sign with the pre-rotation `WEBHOOK_SECRET`; with their valid JWT the stale signature is logged (rate limited) and the request is served, so chat and receipts keep working. Only a bad signature without a valid JWT is 401. Older app builds keep working with the permission migration: their inserts without `user_id` are attributed to the signed-in user, and a refused edit, delete or pool transfer comes back as an error the old app already shows (its optimistic delete rolls back) instead of a silent no-op.
+3. **Mobile:** release a new build with all `--dart-define` values (documented in the root `README.md`, "Flutter App (`--dart-define` flags)") and a release keystore (`key.properties`).
+4. **Later:** once old builds are gone, remove `X-App-Token` acceptance and tighten the join-code policy (DB-17). `WEBHOOK_SECRET` is already optional in app builds.
+
+### 6.3 Product decisions needed
+None open. Decided by the owner on 2026-10-20:
+- DB-16 / DB-18: only admins move money out of shared pools and edit or delete other members' transactions; admins can appoint co-admins, who cannot demote the primary admin.
+- Legacy transactions without a recorded creator (`user_id IS NULL`) stay admin-only (no creator is guessed); every new transaction is attributed to the user who entered it.

+# ai_service audit (Python backend) — 2026-10-19
+
+Scope: `ai_service/**` (FastAPI app, routes, auth, rate limiting, Supabase client, salary cycle,
+ZATCA decoder, settlement engine, installments, support agent, tests, Docker), checked against
+`AGENTS.md` and `.agents/rules/*`. Secret values are never reproduced here; leaked values are
+referred to by name and SHA-256 prefix only.
+
+Branch: `worktree-agent-adf77fe78f2b74766` (base `f17eb2b`).
+
+## Test results
+
+Command (from `ai_service/`): `/opt/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider`
+
+| | Result |
+|---|---|
+| Baseline (`f17eb2b`) | **11 failed, 127 passed, 6 skipped**. The 11 failures were tests reaching the network (`mockproject.supabase.co` via the proxy, 502). With a developer `.env` present these tests talk to the live Supabase project instead (API-24). |
+| Final (`d1b60db`) | **251 passed, 6 skipped, 0 failed** (hermetic: no `.env`, no sockets to non-loopback hosts, no LLM calls). |

+New test modules: `test_api_audit.py`, `test_jwt_hardening.py`, `test_supabase_key_validation.py`,
+`test_rate_limit_and_env.py`, `test_input_hardening.py`, `test_salary_cycle_riyadh.py`,
+`test_zatca_tlv.py`, `test_settlement_audit.py`, `test_budget_cycle_lookup.py`, plus
+`tests/fakes.py` (in-memory Supabase) and `tests/secret_scan.py` (digest-based scanner).

+## Findings
+
+| ID | Sev | Title | Status |

+## Details
+
+### API-01 — Critical — Leaked secrets in a public repo; broken scanner
+- **Where:** `ai_service/tests/test_sec04_jwt_and_secrets.py:113-145` (raw values as regex literals; scanned only `flutter_app/lib` and `ai_service/routes`), `tests/test_security_posture.py:6-7`, `tests/test_secret_config.py:20`, `send_simulated_sms.py:13` and `test_chat_endpoint.py:10` (fallback default), `docs/runbooks/security-secret-rotation.md:5-6`, `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-02-…:241,248`, `…2026-10-05-…:89`, `…2026-10-15-security-hardening.md:64,1834-1835,1906-1907`.
+- **Root cause:** the "leaked secret" test embedded the very values it looked for, and the dev scripts used the live webhook secret as a default. Digests: WEBHOOK_SECRET `f516a232df76…`, legacy 64-hex token `c3d7f5e65951…`, APP_AUTH_TOKEN `34164266f633…`.
+- **Impact:** anyone can forge `X-Signature`/`X-App-Token`. After API-30 neither is an authentication factor any more, but both remain in git history.
+- **Fix:** `tests/secret_scan.py` stores only SHA-256 digests; candidate tokens (64-hex, `bt_sec_*`, `sb_secret_*`, JWTs) are hashed and compared, plus structural checks (real-looking `bt_sec_`/`sb_secret_` keys, `service_role` JWTs). Scans `*.py *.dart *.ts(x) *.js *.md *.json *.yaml` across `flutter_app/lib`, `ai_service`, `web_app/src`, `docs`. Values redacted to `<redacted: rotated>`; dev-script defaults removed.
+- **Tests:** `test_working_tree_secret_scanner` (failed on the two dev scripts before their fix), `test_secret_scanner_detects_leaked_digest_and_structural_patterns`.
+- **Owner action:** rotate `WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `APP_AUTH_TOKEN` (git history keeps the old values); consider history rewrite.
+
+### API-02 — High — Installment payment IDOR
+- **Where:** `routes/budgets.py:201-215`, `installment_service.py:365-391`.
+- **Root cause:** no auth dependency; `pay_installment(plan_id)` updated by id only with the service-role client.
+- **Repro:** `POST /budgets/installments/<any plan id>/pay` with only the (public) app token.
+- **Fix:** JWT required; plan's household resolved server-side; membership verified; update scoped by `household_id`.
+- **Tests:** `test_pay_installment_requires_authentication`, `test_pay_installment_of_foreign_household_is_forbidden`, `test_every_non_public_route_rejects_anonymous_requests`.
+

+- **Where:** `routes/budgets.py:317-348`, `salary_cycle.py:814-839`.
+- **Root cause:** `cost_control_sub_categories` has no `household_id`; rename/list routes had no auth.
+- **Fix:** JWT required; rename only under a parent category owned by a household and only by an admin of it; shared/system definitions are read-only (403). Proper per-household overrides need a schema change (owner/supabase).
+- **Tests:** `test_sub_category_routes_require_authentication`, `test_rename_of_shared_system_sub_category_is_forbidden`, `test_rename_of_own_custom_sub_category_by_admin_succeeds`.
+

+- **Where:** `chat_parser.py:507`, `receipt_scanner.py` (enrich branch), `dedup_engine.py:119-156`.
+- **Root cause:** `update(...).eq("id", enrich_tx_id)` without household filter; service role bypasses RLS; result reported "enriched" regardless.
+- **Fix:** `enrich_transaction_items(..., household_id=)` scopes the update and returns False when nothing matched → `status: error`.
+- **Tests:** `test_chat_enrichment_cannot_touch_foreign_transaction`, `test_receipt_enrichment_cannot_touch_foreign_transaction`.

+- **Root cause:** `original_transaction_id` not checked against `household_id`; `_adjust_original_transaction` was a `@staticmethod` calling `cls.recalculate_budgets` (NameError swallowed).
+- **Fix:** ownership check before creating the plan (404), scoped update, classmethod with recalculation; route requires `household_id` and JWT.
+- **Tests:** `test_installment_creation_cannot_adjust_foreign_transaction`, `test_installment_creation_requires_household_and_auth`, `test_installment_adjusts_own_transaction_and_recalculates`.

+- **Where:** `salary_cycle.py:632-652` (`add_category_and_budget`), `salary_cycle.py:842-901` (`remove_sub_category_for_household`).
+- **Fix:** only the household's own custom code is edited; new codes inserted with `household_id`; shared definitions never purged.
+- **Tests:** `test_add_category_does_not_modify_shared_system_category`, `test_add_new_category_is_scoped_to_household`, `test_remove_sub_category_never_purges_shared_definition`.

+### API-07 — High — Supabase key role never validated
+- **Where:** `supabase_client.py:24-38`, `is_supabase_configured`.
+- **Root cause:** `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY or SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` — first non-empty wins. The owner env sets `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` to a JWT with role `anon`; docker-compose passes the real key as `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, which was ignored.
+- **Impact (pre-fix):** all queries ran as `anon`: membership lookups empty → every household route 403; `consume_quota` (service_role-only) failed → quota silently skipped (API-08); writes failed into container-local JSON fallbacks.
+- **Fix:** keys classified without logging (`sb_secret_`/`service_role` accepted; `anon`, `authenticated`, `sb_publishable_`, unknown rejected); first privileged key wins; `get_client()` fails closed; CRITICAL startup log (`main._log_security_configuration`).
+- **Tests:** `test_supabase_key_validation.py` (4 tests).
+- **Owner action:** set `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` to an `sb_secret_…` key (or remove it so the service-role key is used). With the current env, DB-backed routes now fail closed with 500 instead of answering 403.
+- **SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET empty:** HS256 user tokens are rejected (fail closed, covered by `test_empty_secret_fails_closed_for_hs256`); only ES256 tokens verifiable via the project JWKS pass. If the project still signs with the legacy HS256 secret, every user request will 401 — either migrate to asymmetric JWT signing keys or set the secret.
+
+### API-08 — High — Quota fail-open / mis-keyed window
+- **Where:** `rate_limiter.py:126-171`.
+- **Fix:** inconclusive DB quota → 503 in production; window keyed by verified user.
+- **Tests:** `test_quota_fails_closed_in_production_when_rpc_errors`, `test_quota_denied_by_db_returns_429`, `test_sliding_window_is_per_user_not_per_client_supplied_household`.
+

+- **Where:** `rate_limiter.py:28-87`.
+- **Root cause:** member `str(now)` collides; rejected entries stay in the ZSET; `_get_redis` retried a 2 s connect each request while Redis was down; `redis` missing from requirements (ImportError → silent per-process memory limiter).
+- **Fix:** unique members, `ZREM` on rejection, 30 s back-off, `redis>=5.0.0`.
+- **Tests:** `test_redis_counts_concurrent_requests_with_identical_timestamps`, `test_redis_rejected_requests_do_not_consume_window`, `test_redis_outage_backs_off_instead_of_reconnecting_every_request`.

+### API-12 — Medium — JWT verification gaps
+- **Where:** `auth.py:43-125`.
+- **Findings:** `exp` not required (a token without `exp` never expires), no `role == authenticated` check, `alg` defaulted to HS256 when missing, each unknown `kid` triggered a blocking 5 s JWKS fetch on the event loop, 401 detail echoed exception text. Algorithm confusion/`none` were already rejected (verified by test).
+- **Fix:** explicit allow-list (ES256 via JWKS EC P-256 keys / HS256 via secret), required `exp/iat/sub`, pinned issuer/audience/role, 30 s leeway, JWKS refresh at most once per 60 s, token length cap, generic 401.
+- **Tests:** `test_jwt_hardening.py` (12 tests incl. ES256 via JWKS).
+

+- **Where:** `auth.py:146-180`. **Fix:** `users.household_id` consulted only when the memberships query errors. **Test:** `test_stale_users_household_id_does_not_grant_access`.

+- **Where:** `salary_cycle.py:43,96,148,…`, `supabase_client.py:244-251` (insert), `salary_cycle.py:1065` (toggle).
+- **Repro:** at 2026-10-26T22:30Z (01:30 Riyadh on the 27th) `get_cycle_for_date()` returned `2026-10`; DB trigger files the same transaction under `2026-11`.
+- **Fix:** `utils.riyadh_today()` / `riyadh_date_for_timestamp()` (fixed UTC+3) everywhere; insert uses the household payday; activation uses the salary cycle.
+- **Tests:** `test_salary_cycle_riyadh.py` (Oct 28 → 2026-11, Dec 27 → 2027-01, payday 30/31 in Feb incl. 2028 leap year, midnight boundary, insert and activation).

+### API-15 — Medium — ZATCA decoder
+- **Where:** `receipt_scanner.py:35-75`.
+- **Repro:** total tag `NaN` decoded to `float('nan')` and flowed into the amount; truncated buffers produced short values; `0x81`-prefixed long names were misparsed.
+- **Fix:** strict base64 (std/url-safe, optional padding), exact TLV parsing, BER lengths, strict UTF-8, decimal amounts via regex + `Decimal`.
+- **Tests:** `test_zatca_tlv.py` (15 cases).
+
+### API-16 / API-17 — High/Medium — Nafaqah rules
+- **Where:** `routes/households.py:376-396`, `settlement_engine.py:16-188` (legacy), `227-257` (Nafaqah), `436-443` (v2 roles).
+- **Fix:** family households (a member with `financial_role = spouse`) never split 50/50 — the husband carries shared expenses; wife-paid household/husband/children/dependent expenses are owed back in full unless flagged Tabarru' (`is_tabarru`/`is_gift`; the schema has no such column yet — owner/supabase); role detection uses `financial_role`, not admin rights; `split_ratio` limited to [0,1] and only for roommate/partner households; response gains `mode`.
+- **Tests:** `test_settlement_audit.py` (family/no-50-50, wife-paid owed in full, dependent-by-id, Tabarru', admin wife, ratio bounds).
+- **Follow-up (UI-24 owner decision):** the wife's debt and allowance are now persisted and explicit. `nafaqah_service.py` classifies expenses (`wife_reimbursable` / `wife_personal`, only when the wife paid), keeps the ledger in halalas and writes through the DB RPCs with the verified caller as `p_actor_user_id`. New routes in `routes/nafaqah.py`: `GET /households/{id}/nafaqah`, `GET|POST /households/{id}/nafaqah/reimbursements`, `GET|PUT /households/{id}/nafaqah/allowance` (403 not allowed, 409 overpayment / not a family, 422 bad input or a wife from another household). `POST /households/{id}/reimbursements` records into the Nafaqah ledger in family households and refuses any other direction. The chat parser suggests the class («اشتريت لنفسي…» → personal; «دفعت فاتورة البيت / أغراض البيت / للعيال» → reimbursable) and accepts the user's confirmed `nafaqah_class` (`wife_reimbursable` / `wife_personal` / `none`; any split value → 422). Both settlement engines honour `nafaqah_class`. Tests: `tests/test_nafaqah.py` (69 cases).
+

+- **Tests:** `test_three_way_split_conserves_every_halala`, `test_simplification_*`, `test_completed_installment_plan_has_no_residual_halala`.
+

+### API-30 — High — Client contract (Flutter)
+- **Fix (`8c7ab2b`):** verified JWT alone passes the firewall (old `X-App-Token` still accepted there for old builds); firewall answers 401 + `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer` for missing/invalid/expired credentials; chat/receipt endpoints authenticate by JWT and no longer require `X-Signature` (so `WEBHOOK_SECRET` can be rotated without breaking installed builds; `utils.verify_signature` kept for server-to-server webhooks); `Idempotency-Key` dedupes commits per (user, endpoint, key) and replays the stored result (`Idempotent-Replayed: true`, 409 while in flight); `client_occurred_at` validated (≤ 5 min future, ≤ 90 days old) and used as the transaction time.
+- **Tests:** `test_verified_jwt_alone_passes_firewall_without_app_token`, `test_firewall_answers_401_for_missing_or_expired_jwt`, `test_chat_commit_needs_jwt_not_webhook_signature`, `test_idempotency_key_dedupes_replayed_commit`, `test_client_occurred_at_becomes_transaction_timestamp`, `test_idempotency_store_is_shared_across_instances_via_redis`.
+- **Limitation:** without `REDIS_URL` the idempotency store is per process; durable dedupe across instances needs Redis or an `idempotency_keys` table (owner/supabase).

+## External review (Gemini) — Nafaqah items
+
+Branch `audit/gemini-nafaqah` (from `682fdd3`). Each claim was checked against the code and, where it mattered, against the installed `postgrest` 2.33.0 in `/opt/venv` plus downloaded postgrest-py 0.14.0, 0.15.0, 0.16.8, 0.16.11, 0.17.2, 0.18.0 and 1.0.1 wheels (`supabase>=2.5.0` allows `postgrest>=0.14`).
+
+| Item | Verdict | Fix (commit) | Tests |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| BLOCKER 4a — settlement read `users.household_id` | **Confirmed.** `users.household_id` is only the *active* household (`switch_active_household`, migration `20261018_household_memberships_and_switching.sql`); a wife viewing another household dropped out of `_household_family_roles`, so the family was settled as `shared_split` (50/50). `calculate_settlement_v2` had the same lookup, so roommate detection was affected too. | Both engines use `nafaqah_service.load_family_context` (`household_memberships`, as the DB's `nafaqah_husband_id` does) and raise instead of guessing "not a family" (`b5449f3`). | `test_nafaqah.py::test_partner_settlement_finds_wife_through_memberships`, `::test_settlement_v2_finds_wife_and_roommates_through_memberships` |
+| BLOCKER 4b — settlement ignored repayments; payday hard-coded | **Confirmed.** Family repayments go to `spouse_reimbursements` (no `is_settlement` transaction), and neither `/settlement` nor `/settlement-v2` read that table. Both called `get_salary_cycle_dates()` with the default 27th. | Family mode reports the Nafaqah ledger: `wife_reimbursable` advances minus repayments, all time and to the halala, the same figure as `GET /nafaqah` and `get_spouse_reimbursement_balance()`; response gains `nafaqah` (gross / reimbursed / outstanding); "settled" threshold is 0.01 SAR in family mode. Cycle dates use `get_household_payday` (`b5449f3`). Behaviour change: an unclassified row (no `nafaqah_class`) is an ordinary household expense, as the column is defined; pre-UI-24 rows are no longer guessed into a debt. | `::test_partner_settlement_reflects_recorded_reimbursements`, `::test_partner_settlement_route_matches_nafaqah_summary`, `::test_partner_settlement_uses_household_payday` (payday 10) |
+| BLOCKER 5 — scanned receipts had no Nafaqah | **Confirmed.** `process_receipt_scan` never set `paid_by`/`beneficiary`/`nafaqah_class`; the Flutter receipt flows had no selector. | `nafaqah_service.resolve_expense_nafaqah` classifies chat and receipts alike: `/agent/scan-receipt` takes `paid_by`, `beneficiary`, `nafaqah_class`, `nafaqah_spouse_id`, returns the suggestion (plus `household_mode`, `recorder_role`, `wives`) in preview and duplicate responses, and stores it (`4415a62`). App: `NafaqahReviewSection` in the receipt sheet, batch review sheet and multi-page scanner (the last from the Nafaqah summary, as it saves without a preview); direct-insert fallbacks keep `nafaqah_class` + `nafaqah_spouse_id` together; offline drafts carry the choice and the sync worker replays it; a 422 is shown, not bypassed by a direct insert (`6530aa3`). Strings `nafaqah_choose_wife(_required)` in en/ar/ur. | `test_nafaqah.py::test_receipt_*`, `::test_wife_scanned_*`, `::test_husband_scanned_receipt_is_plain_household_expense`; Flutter `test/models/nafaqah_preview_test.dart`, `test/screens/batch_receipt_scanner_screen_test.dart` (family cases), `ui_l10n_guard_test.dart` |

But 0.14–1.0 return `None` only when PostgREST's detail text is exactly "The result contains 0 rows"; otherwise, and for every other error, they raise `APIError(code="204", "Missing response")`, masking the cause. | `postgrest_compat.first_row` (`limit(1)`) in `get_allowance` and `household_permissions` (`household_owner_id`, `member_role`, `assert_can_modify_transaction`) (`97d9416`). | `test_nafaqah.py::test_allowance_lookup_does_not_rely_on_maybe_single`, `test_household_permissions.py::test_permission_lookups_do_not_rely_on_maybe_single` |

Every RAISE of the mapped RPCs already sets an SQLSTATE (28 checked: all of `20261020300000` and the role RPCs/triggers of `20261020400000`; the overpayment RAISE has `HINT = 'overpayment'`). Only `set_member_role` / `remove_member` raise P0001, and neither the API nor the app calls them. Neither migration was edited. Gap fixed: a re-raised error carries only the dict or its `repr` (`str(APIError)` is a Python dict repr, not JSON); `postgrest_compat.db_error_fields` reads attributes, a dict argument, `.json()`, or the repr (`97d9416`). | `::test_db_errors_from_real_postgrest_exceptions_are_mapped`, `::test_rpc_overpayment_race_returns_409`, `test_household_permissions.py::test_role_rpc_errors_map_from_real_postgrest_exceptions`; DB test 19 §6 (SQLSTATE 22023 + HINT) and §11 (guard: every mapped RAISE has ERRCODE) |

The card sends the class derived from the confirmed chips and the chosen wife (`6530aa3`). | `::test_chat_class_contradicting_explicit_attribution_is_rejected`, `::test_chat_consistent_class_and_attribution_are_stored`, `::test_chat_multi_wife_household_takes_the_chosen_wife`, `::test_chat_rejects_a_spouse_id_that_is_not_allowed`; Flutter `pending_expense_confirmation_card_test.dart` (stale chip, wife choice) |

+Out of scope here (files owned by the concurrent stream), same `maybe_single()` risk: `auth.py:200` (on postgrest ≤ 1.0 a zero-row membership lookup raises and falls back to `users.household_id`, the stale-membership path of API-13), `supabase_client.py:568/629/698/812` (unguarded `res.data` when 2.33 returns `None`; swallowed by `except`, so the JSON-file default is used), and `salary_cycle.py:274` (`simulate_affordability` reads `resp.data` without a `None` check, so with 2.33 it raises `AttributeError` when the category has no budget row for the month).
+## External review (Gemini) — platform items
+
+Second-opinion review of this branch (2026-10-20). Each claim was checked against the code at
+`682fdd3`, the installed libraries in `/opt/venv` (supabase-py 2.33.0, postgrest 2.33.0,
+Starlette 1.9.0) and published wheels of older supabase-py releases, inspected offline and probed
+with `python -I` against mocked HTTP (`respx`), never against a live service.
+
+| Item | Verdict | Fix |
+|---|---|---|
+| BLOCKER 1 — supabase-py too old for `sb_secret_` keys; key selection | **Confirmed** (lower bound) + **partly confirmed** (selection) | `3627484` |
+| BLOCKER 2 — `WEBHOOK_SECRET` / `APP_AUTH_TOKEN` contradiction | **Confirmed** (docs/app/backend disagreed); firewall logic **not** a bug | `03ce01e`, policy revised in the follow-up commit (stale signature + valid JWT = warn and serve) |
+| BLOCKER 3 — quota RPC shape → 503 | **Partly confirmed**: no 503 with the current client and SQL, but any wrapped shape would 503 | `6be0159` |
+| HIGH 3 — JWKS lock-out and blocking fetch | **Confirmed** (both) | `4df94fb` |
+| HIGH 5 — hard-coded payday 27 | **Confirmed** (and two more call sites) | `d857855` |
+| MEDIUM 6 — `raw_sms` reads/writes | **Not a bug**: the column exists by design | docs only |
+
+### BLOCKER 1 — supabase-py and `sb_secret_` keys
+- **Library evidence.** `supabase/_sync/client.py` in every release up to **2.15.3** rejects any key
+  that does not match `^[A-Za-z0-9-_=]+\.[A-Za-z0-9-_=]+\.?[A-Za-z0-9-_.+/=]*$` with
+  `SupabaseException("Invalid API key")` (2.5.0 line 60–63, 2.15.3 line 61–64). An `sb_secret_…`
+  key has no dot, so `create_client` raised; reproduced with 2.15.3 in a scratch venv. **2.16.0** is
+  the first release without the check (verified for 2.16.0, 2.17.0, 2.18.x, 2.22.x, 2.23.0, 2.33.0).
+- **Headers.** 2.16.0 and 2.33.0 both send `apikey: <key>` and `Authorization: Bearer <key>` (the
+  identical value) to PostgREST and Storage, which is exactly what supabase-js 2.x sends without a
+  session (`SupabaseClient._getAccessToken` falls back to the key; `fetchWithAuth`), and supabase-js
+  is the client Supabase documents for the new keys. Supabase's "send on `apikey`, not `Authorization`"
+  warning is about Edge Functions' `verify_jwt` and `pg_net`; `ai_service` uses neither (only
+  PostgREST, RPCs and Storage). So the "wrong header" part is **not confirmed** for this service.
+- **Decision:** `supabase>=2.16.0` in `ai_service/requirements.txt` (was `>=2.5.0`). `/opt/venv` has
+  2.33.0. The full pytest suite was also run in a scratch venv with exactly `supabase==2.16.0`
+  (gotrue 2.12.4, postgrest 1.1.1, storage3 0.12.2): all green.
+- **Key selection (`supabase_client.describe_supabase_key`).** Before: the loop returned on the
+  first privileged key in `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` order, so an anon value
+  in the other variable was silently skipped and a legacy JWT beat an `sb_secret_` key. Now both
+  variables are always inspected: an `sb_secret_` key wins over a legacy `service_role` JWT
+  (`SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` first on a tie), anon/publishable/authenticated/unknown values are never
+  used, an ignored value or a second different privileged key produces a warning (startup log in
+  `main._log_security_configuration` and at client creation), and with no privileged key the
+  startup log is CRITICAL and `get_client()` fails closed. A bare `sb_secret_` prefix is not a key.
+- **Tests:** `tests/test_supabase_key_validation.py` (33 cases: each variable alone with
+  sb_secret / service_role JWT / anon / authenticated / publishable / bare prefix / garbage /
+  other-role JWT; every mixed pair; both privileged; identical and different sb_secret keys;
+  startup log levels without echoing values; requirements lower bound; the installed client
+  accepts the key offline and sends it as `apikey`).
+
+### BLOCKER 2 — `WEBHOOK_SECRET` / `APP_AUTH_TOKEN`
+- **Contradiction confirmed.** README (`README.md:217`) and the app
+  (`flutter_app/lib/supabase_config.dart:74`, StateError in release builds) said the backend requires
+  the signature; `routes/chat.py` and `routes/receipts.py` no longer verified it; `main.py:27`
+  imported `verify_signature` without using it; rule 04 §5 still mandated signature verification.
+- **Firewall (`main.py:224` `token_valid or bearer_valid`) is not a bug.** It is a coarse pass for
+  proxied requests; every non-public route verifies the JWT itself. New tests prove it:
+  `test_app_token_alone_never_grants_access_to_user_routes` (every API route via the proxy with only
+  `X-App-Token` → 401/403/422) and `test_app_token_with_invalid_or_expired_bearer_cannot_reach_user_data`
+  (expired, forged and malformed Bearer next to a valid `X-App-Token` → 401). They passed before the
+  change, confirming the behaviour.
+- **Design now implemented everywhere:** user routes are authenticated by the Supabase JWT.
+  `auth.verify_signature_if_present` is a dependency of every router (`main.py`). No header or a
+  valid signature: nothing happens. An invalid, malformed or unverifiable signature (including
+  `WEBHOOK_SECRET` unset in production) **with a valid JWT is served**: a warning is logged at most
+  once per route and user per 5 minutes, naming the route template and a 12-character SHA-256 of
+  the user id, never secret or signature values. Without a valid JWT a bad signature is 401.
+  **Why not reject:** the owner has already rotated `WEBHOOK_SECRET` on Railway, so every installed
+  build signs with the old value; the first version of this fix (`03ce01e`, present-but-invalid →
+  401) would have broken all existing users' chat and receipt calls on deploy. The signature never
+  authenticated anyone (its key ships in the APK), so ignoring a stale one loses no security. There is currently no server-to-server
+  route without a JWT (`test_every_non_public_route_rejects_anonymous_requests` guards that); such a
+  route must call `utils.verify_signature`, which rejects a missing signature. `X-App-Token` stays a
+  legacy firewall pass only. Flutter: `WEBHOOK_SECRET` is optional (no StateError), and
+  `BaseApiClient` signs only when a secret is supplied (`signingSecret`, injectable for tests).
+- **Deployment:** installed builds keep working after the rotation (stale signature logged, JWT
+  authenticates). The warning count shows how many old builds remain; new builds can drop the define.
+- **Tests:** `tests/test_api_audit.py` (stale signature with a valid JWT is never 401 on any API
+  route; malformed/empty/stale header with JWT → 200; stale chat commit with JWT → 200; bad signature
+  without a valid JWT (none, expired, malformed) → 401; warning rate limited per route and user,
+  repeats after the interval, contains the hash but not the user id, secret or signature; production
+  without `WEBHOOK_SECRET` + JWT → 200 with a warning; `utils.verify_signature` stays strict for future
+  server-to-server routes; valid signature without JWT never reaches data), Flutter
+  `test/services/client_config_test.dart`, `test/services/api/base_api_client_test.dart`.
+- Docs aligned: `README.md`, `.agents/rules/04-security-and-privacy.md` §2/§5, `ai_service/.env.example`,
+  `docs/runbooks/security-secret-rotation.md`, MOB-23 in `flutter_logic.md`, master report §3/§4/§6.
+
+### BLOCKER 3 — `consume_quota` result shapes
+- **SQL matches the call.** `supabase/migrations/20261019070000_sec07_api_quota_and_rate_limits.sql:30`
+  `consume_quota(p_user_id UUID, p_bucket TEXT, p_limit INT, p_window_seconds INT) RETURNS BOOLEAN`;
+  the only later change (`20261019100000_sec08_round6_hardening.sql:549-550`) restricts EXECUTE to
+  `service_role`. `rate_limiter._consume_db_quota` sends exactly those named parameters.
+- **Shape:** probing supabase-py 2.16.0 and 2.33.0 against a mocked PostgREST, a `true` body gives
+  `res.data is True`, so the current deployment does not 503. But `[true]`, `{"consume_quota": true}`
+  and `[{"consume_quota": true}]` (proxies, a SETOF/TABLE variant, other client versions) reached
+  `allowed is not True` (`rate_limiter.py:206` at `682fdd3`) and would have been 503 in production.
+- **Fix:** `_normalize_quota_result` maps unambiguous allowed shapes (incl. `"true"`/`"t"`) to True and
+  denied shapes to False (→ 429); empty, multi-valued, foreign-keyed, numeric or null values are
+  unknown (→ 503 in production, logged; pass in development).
+- **Tests:** `tests/test_rate_limit_and_env.py` (8 allowed, 7 denied, 10 unknown shapes, each at
+  unit level and through `check_api_quota` in production; SQL signature parsed from the migrations
+  and compared with the RPC parameters).
+
+### HIGH 3 — JWKS fetch
+- **Confirmed:** `auth._get_jwk_for_kid` stamped `last_fetch` before downloading (`auth.py:78` at
+  `682fdd3`), so one transient error rejected every ES256 token for 60 s, and the `urllib` download
+  (`auth.py:60`) ran synchronously on the event loop (via the firewall and `get_current_user_id`
+  inside async routes).
+- **Fix:** the 60 s throttle starts only after a successful download; a failure starts a 2 s back-off
+  (`_JWKS_FAILURE_BACKOFF_SECONDS`), with or without cached keys; known keys survive a failed
+  refresh; a successful refresh replaces the key set (revoked keys stop verifying). The download runs
+  in a worker thread (`asyncio.to_thread`) behind a lock (one fetch per burst) through the new async
+  `auth.decode_token` / `ensure_jwks_for_token`, which the firewall middleware awaits for every
+  protected request. The synchronous `_decode_token` used by `get_current_user_id` only reads the
+  cache, so no route signature changed.
+- **Tests:** `tests/test_jwt_hardening.py` (sync path never fetches; fetch runs off the loop;
+  failure → retry after 2 s, not 60 s; unknown kids throttled 60 s after success; failed refresh with
+  cached keys keeps them and backs off; 5 concurrent requests → 1 fetch; ES256 request through the
+  firewall to a real route → 200).
+
+### HIGH 5 — hard-coded payday 27
+- **Confirmed** in `salary_cycle.py` (`get_cycle_breakdown` 464-466 — which also rolled budgets over
+  with the household payday and so mismatched its own key —, `add_category_and_budget` 691,
+  `archive_category_for_household` 753, `add_sub_category_for_household` 828,
+  `remove_sub_category_for_household` 893, `save_sub_allocations` 960,

+  `recurring_detector.py` (`detect_recurring_bills` 128 plus the `>= 27` due-date heuristic at 307 and
+  383, `toggle_household_recurring_bill` 509, `get_recurring_bill_candidates` 564), and in
+  `pdf_statement_generator.py:41` (which also used the current cycle's dates for any requested key).
+- **Fix:** `salary_cycle.current_household_cycle(household_id)` / `get_household_payday` at every
+  household-scoped call; `detect_recurring_bills(..., payday_day=)` with due dates placed relative to
+  the cycle start day and clamped to the month length; PDF statements use the household payday and

+  activation created instead of inserting a duplicate.
+- **Tests:** `tests/test_household_payday.py` (household paid on the 10th on 2026-10-28 Riyadh:
+  cycle `2026-10`, not `2026-11`, for every function above; due-date cases; payday 1 / February clamp).
+- **Not changed (other stream's files):** `settlement_engine.py:68` and `:456` still call

+### MEDIUM 6 — `raw_sms`
+- **Not a bug.** `transactions.raw_sms` is defined in `supabase/schema.sql:101`, never dropped or
+  renamed by any migration, and `20261020200000_remove_sms_artifacts.sql:28-32` deliberately keeps it
+  as the free-text audit note (installed app builds write it through PostgREST; renaming it would

+  local database from all migrations (`run_tests.py --psql --rebuild --db bt_review_b`, 20/20 passed)

+### Follow-up — zero-row `maybe_single()` lookups (reported by the Nafaqah stream)
+- **Library facts.** postgrest-py 2.x (installed 2.33) returns `None` instead of a response when
+  `maybe_single()` matches no row (`SyncMaybeSingleRequestBuilder.execute`), so `resp.data` raises
+  AttributeError. `supabase>=2.16.0` still allows postgrest-py **0.19.1–1.1.x** (supabase 2.16.0 pins
+  `postgrest>0.19,<1.2`; 2.17–2.18 pin 1.1.1; 2.19+ pin the matching 2.x). Those versions request a
+  single object and map the server's error to `None` only when its details text contains
+  "The result contains 0 rows"; otherwise they raise `APIError("Missing response")`.
+- **`salary_cycle.simulate_affordability` — confirmed live bug.** It read `resp.data` straight from
+  `maybe_single()`, so "Can I afford this?" for a category without a budget row returned 500 with
+  2.33 (reproduced with the real client against a mocked PostgREST). It also looked the budget up by
+  calendar month. Now `first_row` (a `limit(1)` select) on the household's current `cycle_key`, with a
+  legacy by-month fallback.
+- **`auth._get_user_membership` — confirmed for old postgrest.** On postgrest-py ≤ 1.1 a zero-row
+  membership lookup could raise, and the `except` branch then consulted the stale
+  `users.household_id` (the API-13 path), granting access to a removed member. Both lookups now use
+  `first_row`, so "no row" is a definitive no-access on every version. The helper lives in
+  `supabase_client.first_row` (imported by `auth.py`, `salary_cycle.py`); no `postgrest_compat.py` was
+  created, to avoid a file conflict with the other stream.
+- **`supabase_client` household getters** (`get_household_payday`, `get_household_income`,
+  `get_household_rollover_rule`, `add_household_savings_surplus`, `get_household_savings_summary`):
+  a missing row reached the fallback only through a caught AttributeError (behaviour was right, by
+  accident); they now use `first_row` explicitly. `inspect_household_role_invite` already guarded `res`.
+- **Not changed (other stream's files):** `household_permissions.py:193` and `:215` and
+  `nafaqah_service.py:481` guard `res is None` (fine on 2.x) but can still raise on postgrest ≤ 1.1;
+  `household_permissions.py:112` catches it.
+- **Tests:** `tests/test_postgrest_zero_rows.py` (real client + `respx`: library behaviour, `first_row`
+  sends `limit=1`, affordability with and without a budget row and by `cycle_key`, membership with the
+  real client, the old-client raise no longer reaching the stale fallback, getters with and without
+  the row). `tests/fakes.py` now mirrors postgrest-py: `maybe_single()` returns None for zero rows and
+  errors on more than one. Green with supabase 2.33/postgrest 2.33 and with supabase 2.16.0/postgrest 1.1.1.
+
+### Test results (after the zero-row follow-up)
+- `ai_service`: 544 passed (`/opt/venv`, supabase-py 2.33.0) and 544 passed in a scratch venv with
+  supabase-py 2.16.0 / postgrest 1.1.1.
+- `flutter analyze`: no issues; `flutter test`: 497 passed.
+- DB suite (local Postgres 16, rebuilt): 20/20 passed (no SQL changed).
+
+## Owner actions
+1. Rotate `WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `APP_AUTH_TOKEN` (old values remain in git history). With `8c7ab2b` the app no longer needs either for authentication.
+2. Put an `sb_secret_…` key in `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` or `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` (either works; an anon value next to it is ignored with a warning). Deploy with `supabase>=2.16.0`.
+3. Confirm the project's JWT signing: with `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` empty only ES256 (JWKS) user tokens are accepted.
+4. Set `ENV=production` explicitly in deployment and `ENV=development` locally; set `TRUSTED_PROXY_IPS`; provision `REDIS_URL` (shared rate limits + idempotency).

+# Android build verification
+
+Date: 2026-10-20 · Branch: `audit/claude-comprehensive-review` (from `952098d`) · Related: [`flutter_logic.md`](flutter_logic.md) (MOB-02, MOB-18, MOB-19), [`MASTER_AUDIT_REPORT.md`](MASTER_AUDIT_REPORT.md) §4 item 8
+
+Until now this audit had not built the Flutter app for Android, because the sandbox had no Android SDK. Since the last build, the branch has added native plugins (`flutter_secure_storage` 11, `share_plus` 13, `path_provider`) and changed the Android config: backups off, cleartext off, release signing from `key.properties`, minSdk 26. This document records the first real Android build of the branch.
+
+## 1. Verdict
+
+**It builds.** The debug APK, release APK and release App Bundle all build from an unmodified checkout. **No change to `flutter_app/android/`, `pubspec.yaml`, `lib/` or `test/` was needed.**
+
+| Artifact | Command | Result | Size |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Debug APK | `flutter build apk --debug` | ✓ built | 186 MB (194,636,893 B; unstripped engine, Vulkan validation layer, JIT kernel) |
+| Release APK, no `key.properties` | `flutter build apk --release` | ✓ built, **signed with the Android debug key** (intended fallback, §4.4) | 79 MB (82,748,685 B; 3 ABIs) |
+| Release APK, throwaway upload key | `flutter build apk --release` | ✓ built, v2-signed by the upload key | 79 MB |
+| Release App Bundle, throwaway upload key | `flutter build appbundle --release` | ✓ built, jar-signed by the upload key | 70 MB (72,944,161 B) |
+| `flutter analyze` | | No issues found | |
+| `flutter test` | | 511 passed, 0 failed | |
+| Emulator smoke launch | | **Skipped**: no `/dev/kvm` in the sandbox (§6) | |
+
+The merged release manifest matches what the branch intends. It has no SMS permission of any kind, `allowBackup=false`, `fullBackupContent=false`, data-extraction rules that exclude every domain, `usesCleartextTraffic=false`, and is not debuggable. minSdk is 26 and targetSdk is 36. The `flutter_secure_storage` native plugin is compiled in and survives R8. All 64-bit native libraries are 16 KB page-aligned.
+
+## 2. Toolchain
+
+| Component | Version | Source |
+|---|---|---|
+| Flutter / Dart | 3.47.7 stable (`abaf9c5237`) / Dart 3.13.5 | `/opt/flutter` (pre-installed) |
+| JDK | OpenJDK 21.0.12 (Ubuntu) | pre-installed. AGP 9.1 needs JDK 17+ and Gradle 9.3 runs on 17–25, so no extra JDK was needed. Bytecode target stays 17 (`compileOptions` / `jvmTarget`). |
+| Gradle (wrapper) | 9.3.1 | `gradle-wrapper.properties` |
+| Android Gradle Plugin | 9.1.0 | `settings.gradle.kts` |
+| Kotlin Gradle Plugin | 2.4.0 (Flutter's own Gradle plugin compiles with 2.2.21) | `settings.gradle.kts` |
+| Android SDK cmdline-tools | 23.0 (`commandlinetools-linux-16111833_latest.zip`) | dl.google.com. SHA-1 `e025545c…5f60` checked against `repository2-3.xml`. |
+| platform-tools | 37.0.1 | sdkmanager |
+| Platform | android-36 (compileSdk / targetSdk from `flutter.compileSdkVersion` / `flutter.targetSdkVersion` = 36) | sdkmanager |
+| Build-tools | 36.0.0 | sdkmanager |
+| Installed by AGP during the build | NDK 28.2.13676358 (Flutter's default `ndkVersion`), CMake 3.22.1 (builds `jni`'s `libdartjni.so`), platforms android-34 and android-35 (plugin `compileSdk`s) | auto-download (licenses accepted) |
+
+The SDK lives at `/opt/android-sdk`. Commands ran with `ANDROID_HOME=ANDROID_SDK_ROOT=/opt/android-sdk`, after `flutter config --android-sdk /opt/android-sdk`. `flutter doctor` reports "Android toolchain ✓ … All Android licenses accepted". The SDK path is local machine state and is not committed: `local.properties`, `gradlew*` and `gradle-wrapper.jar` are git-ignored and were generated by the Flutter tool.
+
+Plugin versions resolved from `pubspec.lock`: `flutter_secure_storage` 11.2.0, `share_plus` 13.3.1, `path_provider` 2.1.6 (`path_provider_android` 2.3.1 on `jni` 1.0.3), `mobile_scanner` 7.4.2, `sqflite_android` 2.4.4.
+
+## 3. Commands
+
+All builds used obviously fake compile-time configuration. The values pass `validateClientConfig` (https in release; the key is not `sb_secret_`/service-role) and point nowhere real:
+
+```bash
+cd flutter_app
+flutter pub get
+DEFINES="--dart-define=SUPABASE_URL=https://example.invalid \
+         --dart-define=SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY=sb_publishable_FAKE_LOCAL_BUILD_ONLY \
+         --dart-define=FASTAPI_BASE_URL=https://example.invalid"
+flutter build apk --debug   $DEFINES
+flutter build apk --release $DEFINES          # no android/key.properties
+# throwaway upload key, created OUTSIDE the repo (scratch dir), 30-day validity:
+#   keytool -genkeypair -keystore <scratch>/throwaway-upload.jks -storetype PKCS12 \
+#           -alias upload -keyalg RSA -keysize 2048 -validity 30 ...
+# temporary flutter_app/android/key.properties (git-ignored) pointing at it, then:
+flutter build apk --release       $DEFINES
+flutter build appbundle --release $DEFINES
+# key.properties deleted afterwards; the keystore never entered the repo.
+flutter analyze
+flutter test
+```
+
+**Network note (sandbox only, not a project problem).** About 1 in 6 requests to `repo.maven.apache.org` got a random Cloudflare `HTTP 429` from this sandbox, in both curl and Gradle. Gradle makes hundreds of POM/JAR requests, so almost every cold build failed on one of them. The fix was to retry the unchanged `flutter build` command in a loop. Gradle caches each request that succeeded, so every retry got further: the first release build succeeded on its 8th attempt, and the signed APK and the AAB on their 1st. A developer machine or CI runner with normal Maven Central access needs none of this.
+
+The cold debug build spent 431 s in Gradle, including the NDK, CMake and platform downloads. Warm release builds took 5–100 s.
+
+## 4. Release APK inspection
+
+Tools: `aapt2 dump badging` / `dump xmltree` / `dump resources`, `apksigner verify`, `zipalign -c -P 16`, `readelf -lW`, `dexdump`, and the R8 `mapping.txt`.
+
+### 4.1 Identity and SDK levels
+
+- Package `com.budgettracker`, versionCode 3, versionName 1.0.2 (from `pubspec.yaml` `1.0.2+3`).
+- `minSdkVersion` 26, `targetSdkVersion` 36, `compileSdkVersion` 36.
+- ABIs: `arm64-v8a`, `armeabi-v7a`, `x86_64`.
+
+### 4.2 Permissions (merged manifest)
+
+| Permission | Origin |
+|---|---|
+| `INTERNET`, `ACCESS_NETWORK_STATE` | app manifest |
+| `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` | app manifest |
+| `CAMERA` (`android.hardware.camera` declared `required=false` by a plugin) | app manifest (receipt scanner) |
+| `RECORD_AUDIO` | app manifest (voice entry) |
+| `VIBRATE` | `flutter_local_notifications` |
+| `com.budgettracker.DYNAMIC_RECEIVER_NOT_EXPORTED_PERMISSION` (signature-level, self-declared) | AndroidX Core (standard) |
+
+**No SMS permission.** `READ_SMS`, `RECEIVE_SMS`, `SEND_SMS` and the rest are absent. The string `SMS` does not appear anywhere in the merged manifest (0 matches). This satisfies the zero-SMS-interception rule (`.agents/rules/04`). No storage, location, contacts, phone-state or `QUERY_ALL_PACKAGES` permission is merged in by any plugin.
+
+### 4.3 Backup, cleartext, debuggability
+
+| Attribute | Release value | Intended |
+|---|---|---|
+| `android:allowBackup` | `false` | ✓ |
+| `android:fullBackupContent` | `false` | ✓ |
+| `android:dataExtractionRules` | `@xml/data_extraction_rules` (R8-shortened to `res/4j.xml`). Content checked in the APK: `<cloud-backup>` and `<device-transfer>` each exclude `root`, `file`, `database`, `sharedpref`, `external` | ✓ |
+| `android:usesCleartextTraffic` | `false` (no `networkSecurityConfig` overrides it) | ✓ |
+| `android:debuggable` | absent (false). The debug APK has `true`, as expected. | ✓ |
+| `android:extractNativeLibs` | `false` (libraries are loaded from the APK, page-aligned) | ✓ |
+
+Exported components: only `MainActivity` (launcher) and AndroidX `ProfileInstallReceiver`. The receiver is guarded by `android.permission.DUMP`, which only the shell/system holds, and is standard. Every plugin provider, service and receiver (image_picker and share_plus `FileProvider`s, `SharePlusPendingIntent`, ML Kit, CameraX, datatransport) has `exported=false`.
+
+### 4.4 Signing
+
+- **Without `key.properties`:** signed with the Android debug certificate (`CN=Android Debug`, SHA-256 `14061bb8…b8e8`). This is the documented fallback in `android/app/build.gradle.kts`. Gradle logs `android/key.properties not found: release build is signed with the DEBUG key.`, but **`flutter build` hides that warning**, so the build looks like an ordinary success. Such an APK cannot be uploaded to Play or update a store install. See recommendation R1.
+- **With the throwaway `key.properties`:** the APK verifies under APK Signature Scheme v2 with the upload certificate (`CN=Throwaway Local Build`). v1 is not needed at minSdk 26. The AAB verifies with `jarsigner` as signed by the same certificate. This proves the `signingConfigs.release` wiring works end to end.
+
+### 4.5 Native code and plugins
+
+- **`flutter_secure_storage` is present.** The debug dex contains `com.it_nomads.fluttersecurestorage.*` (plugin, storage, `ciphers.*`). In the release build R8 keeps and renames it: `FlutterSecureStoragePlugin -> b20`, `FlutterSecureStorage -> y10`, 21 `com.it_nomads` classes in `mapping.txt`. `GeneratedPluginRegistrant` references the plugin directly, so renaming is safe, and the method channel is looked up by string. Version 11.2.0 does its encryption with `javax.crypto` and the AndroidKeyStore (AES-GCM storage cipher, RSA-OAEP/AES key cipher). It declares `tink-android` but never references it, so R8 legitimately removes Tink from the release dex. No ProGuard rule is needed.
+- **`share_plus`** is present (`SharePlusPlugin -> kz0`, `ShareFileProvider`, `SharePlusPendingIntent`).
+- **`path_provider_android` 2.3.1** runs through `jni`: `com.github.dart_lang.jni.*` is kept unrenamed, and `libdartjni.so` ships for all three ABIs.
+- Release native libraries per ABI: `libapp.so` (AOT), `libflutter.so`, `libdartjni.so`, `libbarhopper_v3.so` (ML Kit barcode, `mobile_scanner`), `libimage_processing_util_jni.so`, `libsurface_util_jni.so` (CameraX), `libdatastore_shared_counter.so`.
+- **16 KB pages:** `zipalign -c -P 16` passes. Every 64-bit `.so` has LOAD alignment of at least `0x4000`, and `libapp.so`/`libflutter.so` have `0x10000`. This meets Play's 16 KB page-size requirement for targetSdk 35+.
+- The debug APK also carries `libsqlite3.so`, from the dev dependency `sqflite_common_ffi` → `sqlite3` native-assets hook. The release build correctly omits it, because the app uses the platform SQLite through `sqflite_android`.
+
+## 5. Build warnings (no action required for this release)
+
+Captured with `./gradlew --offline --warning-mode all :app:help`. None of these fails the build.
+
+- `WARNING: The option setting 'android.newDsl=false' is deprecated` and `... 'android.builtInKotlin=false' is deprecated`. The Flutter template put these in `gradle.properties` because several plugins still apply `org.jetbrains.kotlin.android`, which 15 plugin projects also report as deprecated. They must stay until those plugins and Flutter's Gradle plugin migrate. They will need attention before AGP 10.
+- Groovy `propName value` assignment deprecations (Gradle 10) inside third-party plugin build files: `sqflite_android`, `speech_to_text`, `permission_handler_android`, `flutter_local_notifications`, `jni`, `jni_flutter`. These are upstream, not this repo.
+- `javac` "source/target value 8 is obsolete" from two plugin modules (upstream).
+- The SDK tools print "sdkmanager is deprecated, Android CLI will be used instead" and an "SDK XML version 4" notice. These are cosmetic.
+
+## 6. Emulator smoke test
+
+**Not run.** `/dev/kvm` does not exist in this sandbox. Current Android emulators need hardware acceleration for x86_64 system images and cannot run ARM images on an x86 host, so a headless boot is not possible here. The release APK is fine for a device or emulator test elsewhere. With the fake defines it should start and show the login screen. The config validator passes (https URLs, non-privileged key), and network calls then fail against `example.invalid`. To see the missing-config screen instead, build without `--dart-define`s.
+
+Suggested follow-up on a machine with KVM or a device:
+
+```bash
+flutter build apk --debug $DEFINES
+adb install -r build/app/outputs/flutter-apk/app-debug.apk
+adb shell am start -n com.budgettracker/.MainActivity
+adb logcat -d | grep -E "FATAL|AndroidRuntime|flutter"
+```
+
+## 7. Recommendations
+
+- **R1 (Medium). Make a store build fail without the upload key.** The debug-key fallback is deliberate for local `flutter run --release`. But `flutter build apk|appbundle --release` succeeds silently without `key.properties`, because the Gradle warning is not shown, so a debug-signed artifact can reach a release pipeline unnoticed. Options:
+  - add a CI step that runs `apksigner verify --print-certs` and rejects `CN=Android Debug`;
+  - in `build.gradle.kts`, throw when the task graph contains `bundleRelease` and `key.properties` is missing, keeping the fallback for `assembleRelease`/`flutter run`.
+
+  This audit did not change the signing behaviour, because it is a release-process decision for the owner (MOB-18).
+- **R2 (Low). Declare the microphone optional.** `RECORD_AUDIO` makes Play infer `uses-feature android.hardware.microphone` as *required*, which hides the app from devices without a microphone. Voice entry is optional, so `<uses-feature android:name="android.hardware.microphone" android:required="false" />` in `AndroidManifest.xml` would widen device reach. The camera is already `required=false`.
+- **R3 (Low). Build the release APK/AAB in CI** with the same fake `--dart-define`s, so a plugin or AGP bump cannot silently break the Android build again. The toolchain in §2 is enough.
+
+## 8. Changes made
+
+None to the project. The build passed without changes to `flutter_app/android/`, `pubspec.yaml`, `lib/` or `test/`. The only commit is this document. Local-only artifacts are not committed: the SDK under `/opt/android-sdk`, `local.properties`, `gradlew`, the throwaway keystore (scratch directory, outside the repo), the temporary `key.properties` (deleted after the signed builds), and `build/` outputs.
