+# Database / Supabase Audit (Round 7)
+
+Scope: `supabase/schema.sql`, `supabase/seed.sql`, `supabase/migrations/*`, `supabase/tests/*`, cross-checked against
+the Flutter / ai_service call sites that depend on them. The whole chain was rebuilt from scratch on a local
+PostgreSQL 16 with Supabase platform stubs (`supabase/tests/00_local_supabase_stubs.sql`). The live project
+was not touched: no connection, migration, or query was made against it. "Confirmed" means reproduced on the
+replayed schema. Live may differ (see DB-15), so each fix ships with a catalog check under
+[Owner actions](#owner-actions).
+
+Branch: `worktree-agent-a56ddfb476d55d771` · Base: `f17eb2b`
+
+## Findings
+
+| ID | Severity | Title | Status |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| DB-01 | Critical | `household_invites` has no RLS: anon reads every invite code, any user forges an invite to any household and joins it | Fixed `4fef446`, test 08 |
+| DB-03 | Critical | `reallocate_budget` (SECURITY DEFINER, no checks) is executable by anon: cross-household budget rewrite | Fixed `7e3f326`, test 10 |
+| DB-02 | High | Recursive `memberships_admin_manage` policy: every authenticated read of memberships and every receipts storage policy fails | Fixed `83776af`, test 09 |
+| DB-04 | High | `cost_control_codes` insert/update policies (role PUBLIC) let anon/any user write categories into any household | Fixed `31c6a7b`, test 11 |
+| DB-05 | High | Targeted invites always fail (`claimed_user_id` column does not exist), and the target member is not household-scoped | Fixed `4fef446`, test 08 |
+| DB-06 | Medium | Transfers with a third decimal mint money (1.005 debits 1.00 and credits 1.01); `record_income` accepts negative components and invalid cycle keys | Fixed `729d0d7`, test 12 |
+| DB-07 | Medium | Clients can still INSERT `income_records` directly, which forges the income ledger | Fixed `729d0d7`, test 12 |
+| DB-08 | Medium | Clients can overwrite `transactions.cycle_key` to move spending out of a budget cycle | Fixed `a565bc8`, test 13 |
+| DB-12 | Medium | A sole admin cannot delete their account, and the delete cascade would destroy the household's shared pools | Fixed `070a662`, test 16 |
+| DB-14 | Medium | Existing DB tests masked failures (`ON_ERROR_STOP off`, handlers that swallow their own assertion, test 03 re-creating the policies it tests) | Fixed `c12baba` |
+| DB-15 | Medium | The migration chain cannot be replayed as shipped (dependency order, duplicate version prefix), and live has drifted from it | Partially fixed `c12baba` (local replay). CLI/live baseline: owner action |
+| DB-09 | Low | `sync_user_household_membership()` is SECURITY DEFINER with no pinned `search_path` | Fixed `f17e6c6`, test 14 |
+| DB-10 | Low | Clients can INSERT households directly, which bypasses the quota and gives an invite-code existence oracle | Fixed `f17e6c6`, test 14 |
+| DB-11 | Low | Receipts bucket has no size or MIME limits | Fixed `e1761b4`, test 15 |
+| DB-13 | Low (perf) | RLS helpers run per row; 6 foreign keys and the lockout lookup have no index | Fixed `4271db6`, test 17 |
+| DB-16 | Medium (suspected / design) | Any household member can move the whole shared pool into their own account with `transfer_between_accounts` | Fixed (owner decision: admins only) `59a422d`, test 20 |
+| DB-17 | Low | Non-admin members can read `households.invite_code` directly, which bypasses the SEC-08 masking | Not fixed: released app builds read the column directly (see below) |
+| DB-18 | Low (suspected / design) | `transactions.user_id` is not bound to the caller, and members can edit or delete each other's transactions | Fixed (owner decision: creator bound, owner-or-admin edits) `59a422d`, test 20 |
+
+## Test results
+
+| Run | Command (see [How to run](#how-to-run-the-db-tests-locally)) | Result |
+|---|---|---|
+| Baseline: original suite, shipped schema, plain psql | `run_tests.py --psql --rebuild` at `f17eb2b` + runner | 2 passed / 5 failed. Fixtures assumed the drifted live dump: missing `auth.users` rows, `users.email`, `account_type` 'checking', NOT NULL `keywords` |
+| Baseline after fixture-only adaptation (`c12baba`) | same | **5 passed / 2 failed**. 01 fails: anon reads invites (DB-01). 03 fails: membership policy recursion (DB-02). 07 had been passing only because its errors were ignored (DB-14) |
+| New audit tests on the pre-fix schema | all 17 files against `c12baba` migrations | **5 passed / 12 failed**. Every new test fails for the documented reason |
+| After fixes, fresh database rebuilt from scratch | `run_tests.py --psql --rebuild --db bt_audit_final` | **17 passed / 0 failed** (98 PASSED assertions), and 17/17 again on a second run against the same database |
+| Concurrency stress (not committed; script in the session scratchpad) | 4 parallel sessions, 1,200 transfers A→B and B→A | 0 deadlocks / 0 errors. Money conserved: 200,000.00 − 60.00 fees = 199,940.00 |
+| Admin permissions and co-admins (DB-16 / DB-18), fresh rebuild | `run_tests.py --psql --rebuild --db bt_perms` | **20 passed / 0 failed** (test 20: 10 sections, roommate and family households) |
+| RLS overhead, 50k transactions in one household | `EXPLAIN ANALYZE SELECT count(*) …` as `authenticated` | 55 ms → 11 ms (per-row policy calls became an InitPlan) |
+
+## How to run the DB tests locally
+
+Requires PostgreSQL 16+ and `psql`. Docker is not needed.
+
+```bash
+# Rebuild a throwaway database (stubs + schema.sql + seed.sql + migrations) and run every test
+PGHOST=localhost PGPORT=54329 PGUSER=postgres \
+  python3 supabase/tests/run_tests.py --psql --rebuild --db bt_audit_tests
+
+# Re-run tests against an existing database without rebuilding
+PGHOST=localhost PGPORT=54329 PGUSER=postgres \
+  python3 supabase/tests/run_tests.py --psql --db bt_audit_tests
+
+# Run a subset
+PGHOST=localhost PGPORT=54329 PGUSER=postgres \
+  python3 supabase/tests/run_tests.py --psql --db bt_audit_tests supabase/tests/12_audit_ledger_integrity.sql
+
+# Legacy Docker mode (unchanged default): docker exec budget_tracker_review_pg psql …
+DB_NAME=live_rebuilt_round5 python3 supabase/tests/run_tests.py
+```
+
+`--rebuild` applies `00_local_supabase_stubs.sql` (local stand-ins for `auth.*`, `storage.*`, API roles, the
+`extensions` schema, the realtime publication and Supabase's default `public` grants), then `schema.sql`,
+`seed.sql`, and every migration in replay order. Never point `--rebuild` at a hosted project.
+
+---
+
+## Details
+
+### DB-01: `household_invites` has no RLS (Critical)
+
+- **Where:** `supabase/migrations/20261015_family_nafaqah_and_multi_roommate_settlement.sql:9-18` creates the
+  table and never runs `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY`. The policies in
+  `20261019030000_sec01_sec02_household_takeover_prevention.sql:71-95` are therefore inert.
+- **Root cause:** Supabase grants SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE on `public` tables to `anon` and `authenticated`.
+  Without RLS, those grants decide access.
+- **Reproduction:** As `anon`, `SELECT invite_code FROM household_invites` returns every code. As any
+  authenticated user, `INSERT INTO household_invites (household_id, invite_code, …) VALUES ('<victim hh>', 'X', …)`
+  followed by `join_household_by_code('X')` makes the caller a member of the victim household with full read
+  access. `UPDATE … SET used_by = NULL, expires_at = …` also re-opens used or expired invites. The pre-existing
+  test 01 already failed on this (`Anon user can see 1 household invites`).
+- **Impact:** Anyone can take over member-level access to every household (transactions, receipts, accounts,
+  income).
+- **Fix (`20261020010000_audit_invites_rls_and_targeted_claims.sql`):** enable RLS and revoke `anon`. Also gives
+  `claim_household_role_invite` the same 5-failures/15-minutes lockout and attempt logging as
+  `join_household_by_code`; before this it had none.
+- **Status:** Fixed in `4fef446`. Test: `08_audit_invites_rls_and_targeted_claims.sql`, plus test 01.
+
+### DB-02: Recursive policy on `household_memberships` (High)
+
+- **Where:** `supabase/migrations/20261018_household_memberships_and_switching.sql:27-36`
+  (`memberships_admin_manage`, FOR ALL, role PUBLIC).
+- **Root cause:** The USING clause selects from `household_memberships` inside its own policy, so Postgres
+  raises `infinite recursion detected in policy for relation "household_memberships"` (42P17).
+- **Reproduction:** As `authenticated`, `SELECT count(*) FROM household_memberships` raises 42P17. So does
+  `SELECT … FROM storage.objects`, because every receipts policy (20261019060000) consults the table. The
+  pre-existing test 03 failed with this error.
+- **Impact:** Receipt upload, view and delete through the Storage API fail for every user. The Flutter
+  household-switcher fallback and any client roster read fail too. Had the policy evaluated, admins could also
+  INSERT, UPDATE or DELETE membership rows directly. That would bypass `remove_member`/`leave_household`, which
+  reset `users.household_id`, and leave a removed user with full access.
+- **Fix (`20261020020000_audit_membership_policy_recursion.sql`):**
+  - Drop the policy.
+  - Add a single SELECT policy (`own rows OR is_household_admin(household_id)`). The new helper is
+    SECURITY DEFINER, so the check does not recurse.
+  - Revoke client writes. Membership changes now go only through the RPCs.
+  - Backfill memberships for any `users.household_id` that has none.
+  - `get_auth_user_household_id()` and `get_auth_user_role()` now require a live membership row for the
+    active household, so a stale pointer never grants access.
+- **Status:** Fixed in `83776af`. Test: `09_audit_membership_policies.sql`, plus test 03.
+
+### DB-03: `reallocate_budget` is callable by anon (Critical)
+
+- **Where:** `supabase/schema.sql:181-202`. No later migration redefined or revoked it.
+- **Root cause:** SECURITY DEFINER, no `auth.uid()` or household check, no amount validation, and the default
+  `EXECUTE` grant to PUBLIC.
+- **Reproduction:** As `anon`: `SELECT reallocate_budget('<budget A>', '<budget B>', 900)` moves 900 SAR of
+  allocation between any two budget rows, in any household and across households. Negative amounts are
+  accepted too.
+- **Impact:** Anyone holding the public anon key can tamper with any household's budget by UUID. Budget UUIDs
+  leak through realtime payloads and shared screenshots.
+- **Fix (`20261020030000_audit_reallocate_budget_authz.sql`):**
+  - `EXECUTE` is granted only to `authenticated` and `service_role`.
+  - JWT callers must be admin of the household that owns both rows.
+  - Both rows must be in the same household.
+  - The amount must be > 0, have at most 2 decimals, and be no more than the source allocation.
+  - Rows are locked in id order.
+  - ai_service calls with the service role key and keeps working without a user JWT.
+- **Status:** Fixed in `7e3f326`. Test: `10_audit_reallocate_budget_authz.sql`.
+
+### DB-04: `cost_control_codes` write policies are not household-scoped (High)
+
+- **Where:** `supabase/migrations/20261011_hybrid_category_lifecycle.sql:38-45`. SEC-01/02 replaced only the
+  SELECT policy.
+- **Root cause:** `cost_control_codes_insert` and `_update` apply to role PUBLIC and check only
+  `household_id IS NOT NULL AND is_system = false`.
+- **Reproduction:** As `anon`, `INSERT INTO cost_control_codes (code, …, household_id) VALUES (…, '<victim hh>')`
+  succeeds. An authenticated outsider can do the same, and can also move their own category into another
+  household with UPDATE.
+- **Impact:** An outsider can pollute a victim household's categories, for example with phishing text in names
+  shown in the app. They can also squat on `(household_id, code)` so the household cannot create that code.
+- **Fix (`20261020040000_audit_cost_control_codes_policies.sql`):** writes are allowed only for admins of the
+  caller's active household, on non-system rows of that household. There is no client DELETE path, and anon is
+  revoked. ai_service uses the service role and is unaffected.
+- **Note:** FIX_LOG SEC-02 states "Zero policies with role `{public}` remain". That is not true for the
+  replayed chain: these two policies and DB-02's policy are PUBLIC. Verify on live.
+- **Status:** Fixed in `31c6a7b`. Test: `11_audit_cost_control_codes_policies.sql`.
+
+### DB-05: Targeted (manual-member) invites are broken (High)
+
+- **Where:** `supabase/migrations/20261019100000_sec08_round6_hardening.sql:652-656` (join) and `:738-742`
+  (claim).
+- **Root cause:** Both functions run `UPDATE household_dependents SET claimed_user_id = …`. The column is
+  `linked_user_id` (20261015_manual_members_and_claim_merge.sql:6). PL/pgSQL resolves the name only at run
+  time, so the bug appears only when an invite carries `target_member_id`. In addition,
+  `target_member_id` was never checked against the invite's household.
+- **Reproduction:** Any invite with `target_member_id` fails with
+  `ERROR: column "claimed_user_id" of relation "household_dependents" does not exist`, from both RPCs.
+- **Impact:** The "claim a pre-created family member" flow (ai_service `/households/invites/{code}/claim`) is
+  broken. Once fixed naively, a service-created invite could also link a dependent of another household.
+- **Fix:** Use `linked_user_id`, scoped to the invite's household. Add a BEFORE INSERT/UPDATE trigger that
+  rejects a `target_member_id` from another household; it also binds service-role inserts. Same migration
+  as DB-01.
+- **Status:** Fixed in `4fef446`. Test: `08_audit_invites_rls_and_targeted_claims.sql`.
+
+### DB-06: Ledger precision and income validation (Medium)
+
+- **Where:** `supabase/migrations/20261019100000_sec08_round6_hardening.sql:244-479`
+  (`transfer_between_accounts`, `record_income`).
+- **Root cause:** The parameters are unconstrained `NUMERIC`, while `accounts.balance` and
+  `account_transfers.amount` are `NUMERIC(14,2)` and `fee` is `NUMERIC(10,2)`. Each side of a transfer is
+  rounded on its own. `record_income` accepted negative components (negative deductions inflate net) and any
+  `cycle_key` text.
+- **Reproduction:** Two transfers of `1.005` between your own accounts (A=100, B=0) leave A=100.01 and B=0.01.
+  That is 0.02 SAR created, with each log row saying 1.01. The amount can be repeated without limit.
+- **Impact:** Account balances no longer add up to the transfers and income recorded against them, and
+  households see wrong numbers in their totals.
+- **Fix (`20261020050000_audit_ledger_precision_and_income_append_only.sql`):**
+  - Reject amounts and fees with more than 2 decimals (22023).
+  - Reject negative income components, an empty title, and a `cycle_key` that is not `YYYY-MM`.
+  - When `cycle_key` is NULL, derive it from `received_at` and the household payday.
+  - Lock order was already deterministic and the overdraft check already present; both are verified by the
+    stress run (0 deadlocks in 1,200 opposite-direction transfers).
+- **Status:** Fixed in `729d0d7`. Test: `12_audit_ledger_integrity.sql`.
+
+### DB-07: Clients can INSERT into the income ledger directly (Medium)
+
+- **Where:** `supabase/migrations/20261019090000_sec05_accounts_security_and_transfers.sql:149-154`
+  (`income_insert_household`). SEC-08 dropped only UPDATE and DELETE.
+- **Reproduction:** A member inserts `income_records` with another member's `account_id` and
+  `net_amount = -5000`, and the insert succeeds.
+- **Impact:** Forged income history that budgets, rollover and the payday banner read. It bypasses
+  `record_income`'s account-ownership check, sign check and balance update. A later admin or service-role
+  delete of the forged row would then move the real balance through `adjust_account_balance_on_income_change`.
+- **Fix:** Drop the policy. `income_records` and `account_transfers` become read-only for clients; writes go
+  through the SECURITY DEFINER RPCs only. Flutter already uses `record_income`.
+- **Status:** Fixed in `729d0d7`. Test: `12_audit_ledger_integrity.sql`, plus test 07.
+
+### DB-08: Clients can relabel a transaction's cycle (Medium)
+
+- **Where:** `supabase/migrations/20261019080000_bug02_payday_cycle_parity_and_triggers.sql:131-135`.
+- **Root cause:** `trg_populate_transaction_cycle_key` fires only on `UPDATE OF timestamp, household_id`.
+- **Reproduction:** A member runs `UPDATE transactions SET cycle_key = '1999-01' WHERE id = …`. The value is
+  kept, and `update_budget_on_transaction_update` moves the 200 SAR out of the 2026-11 budget, whose
+  `spent_amount` drops to 0.
+- **Impact:** A member can hide overspending from the household budget.
+- **Fix (`20261020060000_audit_transaction_cycle_key_integrity.sql`):** the trigger also fires on
+  `UPDATE OF cycle_key`, so the server-derived key always wins. The migration does no backfill on purpose: a
+  difference can also come from a legitimate payday change. See the detection query under Owner actions.
+- **Cycle logic review (no defect found):** `get_saudi_cycle_for_timestamp` was checked exhaustively for
+  payday 1..31 on every day of 2026-2029:
+  - Every day falls inside its cycle, with no gaps or overlaps.
+  - Each new cycle starts the day after the previous one ends.
+  - Keys advance exactly one month at a time.
+  - Specific cases pass: 23:59:59 vs 00:00 Riyadh on the 26th/27th, Dec→Jan, payday 31 in February, payday 30
+    on 29 Feb 2028, payday 31 in 30-day months, payday 1 near UTC midnight, and Oct 28 → `2026-11`.
+
+  These checks are committed as a regression in test 13.
+- **Status:** Fixed in `a565bc8`. Test: `13_audit_cycle_key_integrity.sql`.
+
+### DB-09: Unpinned `search_path` on a SECURITY DEFINER trigger function (Low)
+
+- **Where:** `supabase/migrations/20261018_membership_sync_and_shared_account_policies.sql:28`.
+- **Fix:** `ALTER FUNCTION … SET search_path = public, pg_temp`. Test 14 adds a guardrail: every SECURITY
+  DEFINER function in `public` must pin `search_path`.
+- **Status:** Fixed in `f17e6c6`. Test: `14_audit_catalog_guardrails.sql`.
+
+### DB-10: Clients can INSERT households directly (Low)
+
+- **Where:** `supabase/migrations/20261019030000_sec01_sec02_household_takeover_prevention.sql:639-643`.
+- **Impact:**
+  - Bypasses `create_household_and_claim`'s limit of 5 households per user and its server-generated 16-hex
+    invite code.
+  - `INSERT … (invite_code = '<guess>')` returns a UNIQUE violation (23505) when the guess exists, so any
+    user can test whether a static join code exists with no rate limit.
+- **Fix:** Drop the policy and revoke INSERT, DELETE and TRUNCATE from clients. No client inserts households
+  directly.
+- **Status:** Fixed in `f17e6c6`. Test: `14_audit_catalog_guardrails.sql`.
+
+### DB-11: Receipts bucket has no upload limits (Low)
+
+- **Where:** `supabase/migrations/20261008_create_receipts_bucket_and_policies.sql:4-6` and
+  `20261019060000_sec06_private_receipts_bucket.sql`.
+- **Root cause:** `file_size_limit` and `allowed_mime_types` were never set. The storage policy checks only
+  the extension in the file name.
+- **Fix:** 20 MiB limit, and only `image/jpeg`, `image/png` and `image/webp`.
+  - 20 MiB covers ai_service's stitched multi-shot receipts: a 25 MB base64 request body is about 18.75 MB
+    of binary.
+  - Flutter uploads JPEGs of at most 1600 px.
+  - The Storage API enforces these limits.
+- **Status:** Fixed in `e1761b4`. Test: `15_audit_receipts_bucket_limits.sql`.
+
+### DB-12: A sole admin cannot delete their account (Medium)
+
+- **Where:** `supabase/migrations/20261019030000_sec01_sec02_household_takeover_prevention.sql:497-534`
+  (`check_last_admin_membership`), together with
+  `20261018_multi_source_income_and_accounts.sql:11` (`accounts.owner_user_id … ON DELETE CASCADE`).
+- **Reproduction:** `DELETE FROM auth.users WHERE id = <sole admin with members>` fails with
+  `Cannot remove the sole admin while other household members remain`. This is the path used by the Supabase
+  Auth admin API and in-app account deletion.
+- **Impact:** Account-deletion requests cannot be honoured (PDPL and app-store rules require them). If the
+  trigger were simply relaxed, the cascade would also delete every shared-pool account that admin created.
+- **Fix (`20261020090000_audit_sole_admin_account_deletion.sql`):** a BEFORE DELETE trigger on `public.users`
+  hands the household over before the cascade runs:
+  - It promotes the longest-standing member (membership and `users.role`).
+  - It re-owns that user's shared pools to an admin of the household.
+  - Direct demotion or removal of a sole admin stays blocked; BUG-03 is unchanged and re-asserted in test 16.
+- **Status:** Fixed in `070a662`. Test: `16_audit_account_deletion.sql`.
+
+### DB-13: Per-row RLS evaluation and missing indexes (Low, performance)
+
+- **Root cause:**
+  - Policies call `auth.uid()`, `get_auth_user_household_id()` and `get_auth_user_role()` unwrapped, so they
+    run once per row.
+  - `transactions_select_household` also re-parsed the JWT for every row (`auth.uid() IS NOT NULL`).
+  - Six foreign keys had no supporting index: `transactions.reallocated_from_budget_id`,
+    `household_invites.{household_id, created_by, used_by}`, `account_transfers.user_id` and
+    `income_records.user_id`. The two `user_id` columns are scanned by the account-deletion cascade.
+  - The invite lockout count on `invite_attempt_log (user_id, attempted_at)` was unindexed and runs on every
+    join attempt.
+- **Fix (`20261020100000_audit_rls_initplan_and_fk_indexes.sql`):**
+  - Every policy in `public` and the receipts policies in `storage` was re-created with
+    `(SELECT …)`-wrapped calls. Names and semantics are unchanged.
+  - The legacy `household_id IN (SELECT household_id FROM users …)` form now uses the membership-backed
+    helper.
+  - Receipts policies resolve households from memberships only.
+  - Seven indexes were added.
+  - Measured: 55 ms → 11 ms for a 50k-row household scan.
+- **Status:** Fixed in `4271db6`. Test: `17_audit_rls_performance.sql` is a guardrail: no unwrapped helper in
+  any policy, and every foreign key indexed.
+
+### DB-14: Tests that could not fail (Medium, test integrity)
+
+- **Problems:**
+  - `07_sec08_round6_hardening.sql` wrapped every block in `\set ON_ERROR_STOP off`, so `RAISE EXCEPTION
+    'VULNERABILITY…'` never failed the run. Its TEST 3 fixture actually errored (`income_records.cycle_key`
+    NOT NULL), so the income-ledger assertions never ran.
+  - Tests 4, 5 and 7 in that file caught `raise_exception` or `OTHERS` around their own VULNERABILITY raise,
+    so they could not fail even with `ON_ERROR_STOP` on.
+  - `03_sec06_private_receipts.sql` redefined `storage.foldername()` and `storage.extension()` and
+    re-created the three receipts policies inside the test. It tested its own copy, not the migration.
+  - In `06_sec05…sql`, subtest 1 inserted `account_type = 'checking'` (violates the CHECK) under
+    `WHEN OTHERS`, so it passed on the CHECK error rather than on RLS.
+- **Fix:** Remove `ON_ERROR_STOP off`, use flag-based assertions, use the shipped policies and helpers, expect
+  `insufficient_privilege`, and correct the fixtures to the migrated schema. FIX_LOG's SEC-06 and SEC-08
+  "verified" claims should be read in this light: test 03 would have failed on the replayed chain (DB-02).
+- **Status:** Fixed in `c12baba`.
+
+### DB-15: Migration chain is not replayable, and live has drifted (Medium, process)
+
+- **Findings:**
+  - `20261018_membership_sync_and_shared_account_policies.sql` creates a policy on `public.accounts`, which is
+    created only by `20261018_multi_source_income_and_accounts.sql`. Filename (lexical) order applies them the
+    wrong way round, so the chain fails.
+  - Three files each share the version prefixes `20261008` and `20261018`, and two each share `20260925`,
+    `20261002`, `20261005`, `20261009`, `20261011` and `20261015`. The Supabase CLI keys `schema_migrations` on that prefix,
+    so `supabase db reset` / `db push` will reject the duplicates.
+  - The original tests only worked against a dump of live: `users.email`, `account_type` values
+    'checking'/'savings', nullable `cost_control_codes.keywords`, and public `users` rows without `auth.users`
+    (suspected missing FK). Live therefore differs from what the migrations build.
+- **Fix:** `run_tests.py --rebuild` replays with an explicit dependency override and documents why. Shipped
+  migrations were not renamed (rule: never edit shipped migrations).
+- **Status:** Partially fixed in `c12baba`. The live baseline is an owner action.
+
+### DB-16: Shared pool can be drained by any member (resolved by owner decision)
+
+`transfer_between_accounts` let any household member transfer from a shared pool into their own personal
+account (`20261019100000…sql:308-311`). Direct edits and `reconcile_account_balance` on shared pools were
+already admin-only.
+
+- **Owner decision (family and roommate households):** only household admins move money out of a shared
+  pool. Members still move money between their own personal accounts and pay into the pool. Expenses
+  recorded against the pool are not transfers and stay allowed for members (roommates spend from the pool);
+  they are attributed to their creator (DB-18) and visible to everyone.
+- **Fix (`20261020400000_admin_permissions_and_co_admins.sql`):** `transfer_between_accounts` raises
+  `42501` when the source is a shared pool and the caller is not an admin of the household (primary admin or
+  co-admin). The app offers pools as a transfer source to admins only.
+- **Status:** Fixed in `59a422d`. Test: `20_admin_permissions_and_co_admins.sql` §5.
+
+### DB-17: Members can read the static join code (Low, still open)
+
+`households_select_own` exposes `households.invite_code` to every member. SEC-08 hides it only in
+`get_user_households()`. The current app reads the code through that RPC (MOB-25), but:
+
+- Column privileges cannot be limited to non-admins: `REVOKE SELECT (invite_code) ON public.households FROM
+  authenticated` also removes the column from admins' direct reads.
+- Released app builds (`main`) render the whole household settings section from
+  `households.select('name, invite_code')` (`ingestion_settings_screen.dart:129`) and fall back to an
+  embedded `households(name, invite_code)` select in `budget_api_client.dart:594`. With the revoke both
+  queries fail with `42501`, so every user of an older build, admins included, loses the household name,
+  member list, payday, income and rollover settings.
+
+**Decision:** not tightened in this round. Apply `REVOKE SELECT (invite_code) ON public.households FROM
+authenticated` together with a matching column-list `GRANT SELECT` once builds older than this branch are
+retired. Until then a non-admin who reads the table directly still sees the join code.
+
+### DB-18: Transaction attribution bound to the caller (resolved by owner decision)
+
+`transactions_insert_household` and `_update_household` did not bind `user_id` to `auth.uid()`, and any
+member could edit or delete any other member's transaction that had no personal account attached. In
+multi-roommate settlement this allowed attribution spoofing.
+
+- **Owner decision (family and roommate households):** a member creates transactions and edits or deletes
+  only their own. Only household admins edit or delete another member's transactions. The creator is bound
+  at insert.
+- **Fix (`20261020400000_admin_permissions_and_co_admins.sql`):**
+  - `trg_bind_transaction_creator` (BEFORE INSERT): a client insert without `user_id` (older app builds) gets
+    `auth.uid()`; naming anyone else raises `42501`. The insert policy also requires `user_id = auth.uid()`.
+  - `trg_enforce_transaction_write_permission` (BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE): the creator can never change; a
+    non-admin touching someone else's row (or a legacy row with no creator) gets `42501`. It raises instead
+    of hiding the row through RLS so clients, including older builds, report a refusal rather than a silent
+    no-op. Writes issued by other triggers (`pg_trigger_depth() > 1`: foreign-key `SET NULL`/`CASCADE` on
+    account, spouse or household deletion) pass.
+  - `transactions_update_household` keeps household scoping in `USING` and repeats owner-or-admin in
+    `WITH CHECK`; a transaction's personal account must belong to its creator
+    (`transaction_account_matches`, definer because an admin cannot read a member's personal account).
+  - `update_account_balance_on_transaction` lets an admin's edit or delete of a member's own transaction
+    adjust that member's personal account; nobody can attach a transaction to someone else's account.
+  - The service role bypasses all of this; `ai_service` passes the verified JWT user as the creator and
+    checks owner-or-admin itself (enrichment, installment linking, settlements).
+- **Legacy rows:** transactions created before this migration through `ai_service` or most app screens have
+  `user_id IS NULL` (the creator was never recorded). They are admin-only from now on; no creator is guessed. **Owner decision (2026-10-20): keep it this way** — admins edit legacy rows, every new row is attributed to the user who entered it.
+- **Status:** Fixed in `59a422d`. Test: `20_admin_permissions_and_co_admins.sql` §3, §4, §10.
+
+### Household roles: co-admins and the primary admin (owner decision)
+
+- `households.owner_user_id` is the primary admin, backfilled from the longest-standing admin membership and
+  kept by triggers: the first admin of a new household becomes primary; when the primary admin's membership
+  ends (leave, removal by themselves, account deletion), the longest-standing remaining admin takes over
+  (after the DB-12 handover promoted one if needed). Clients cannot write the column (column-list `UPDATE`
+  grant on `households`).
+- `promote_member_to_admin`, `revoke_admin`, `transfer_primary_admin`, `get_household_members`: SECURITY
+  DEFINER, pinned `search_path`, caller resolved from the JWT (the service role passes `p_actor_user_id`;
+  an authenticated caller can never act for someone else), household-scoped.
+  - Any admin promotes members and revokes co-admins (themselves included).
+  - Nobody can demote the primary admin (`trg_protect_primary_admin`), and only the primary admin can end
+    their own membership.
+  - Only the primary admin transfers primary admin; the target becomes an admin if needed and the previous
+    primary stays a co-admin.
+- `set_member_role` / `remove_member` (active household) now go through the same rules.
+  `get_user_households()` also returns `is_primary`.
+- The last-admin protections (BUG-03 trigger, DB-12 account deletion handover) are unchanged.
+- Family Nafaqah: the husband or any household admin (co-admins included, never the wife herself) sets the
+  wife's allowance; `nafaqah_husband_id` now prefers the primary admin among provider members.
+
+## Owner actions
+
+> **2026-10-20 update:** the live catalog and data have been compared read-only with the repo, and the batch
+> was proven on a faithful local replica. Results:
+> - `household_invites` RLS is already on;
+> - `memberships_admin_manage` and the `cost_control_codes` write policies are absent;
+> - `reallocate_budget` is missing on live;
+> - `claimed_user_id` does not exist (so DB-05 is real).
+>
+> The ordered apply plan, the pre-flight migration `20261020005000_preflight_live_alignment.sql`, the
+> check queries and the rollback snapshot are in [`live_db_preflight.md`](live_db_preflight.md); it replaces
+> steps 1–2 below. DB-08 detection on live found 0 mismatching rows.
+
+1. **Before applying, check the live catalog** (read-only, SQL editor):
+   ```sql
+   SELECT relname, relrowsecurity FROM pg_class WHERE oid = 'public.household_invites'::regclass;          -- DB-01
+   SELECT policyname, roles FROM pg_policies WHERE tablename IN ('household_memberships','cost_control_codes'); -- DB-02/04
+   SELECT has_function_privilege('anon','public.reallocate_budget(uuid,uuid,numeric)','EXECUTE');          -- DB-03
+   SELECT count(*) FROM pg_attribute WHERE attrelid='public.household_dependents'::regclass AND attname='claimed_user_id'; -- DB-05
+   ```
+2. Apply `supabase/migrations/20261020010000_*` through `20261020100000_*` in order, each in its own
+   transaction, after review. They are idempotent re-definitions plus one bucket UPDATE. On a hosted project
+   the bucket UPDATE needs the storage schema owner, which is the default for the SQL editor.
+3. **DB-08 detection** (rows whose stored key differs from the derivation, e.g. tampering):
+   ```sql
+   SELECT t.id, t.household_id, t.cycle_key,
+          (SELECT c.cycle_key FROM public.get_saudi_cycle_for_timestamp(t.timestamp, h.payday_day) c) AS expected
+   FROM public.transactions t JOIN public.households h ON h.id = t.household_id
+   WHERE t.cycle_key IS DISTINCT FROM
+         (SELECT c.cycle_key FROM public.get_saudi_cycle_for_timestamp(t.timestamp, h.payday_day) c);
+   ```
+4. **DB-15:** take a fresh baseline from live (`supabase db pull`), squash or rename the duplicate-prefix
+   migrations in a new baseline, and point CI at `run_tests.py --psql --rebuild`.
+5. DB-16 and DB-18 are decided and fixed (`20261020400000_admin_permissions_and_co_admins.sql`; apply after
+   `20261020300000_*`). Before applying, check how many live transactions have no creator
+   (`SELECT count(*) FROM public.transactions WHERE user_id IS NULL;`): those become admin-only.
+   Schedule DB-17 once older app builds are retired.
+
+## Cross-team notes (outside `supabase/`, not changed here)
+
+- **Flutter:** `flutter_app/lib/widgets/dashboard/payday_checkin_banner.dart:42-46` filters
+  `income_records` on `income_type`, but the column is `source_type`. The query errors, the catch swallows
+  it, and the payday check-in banner never shows.
+- **ai_service:** `ai_service/salary_cycle.py:44` (`get_cycle_for_date`) uses
+  `datetime.now(timezone.utc).date()`. Between 00:00 and 03:00 Riyadh on payday it reports the previous
+  cycle, while the DB (Asia/Riyadh) reports the new one.
+- **ai_service:** the invite-claim route should surface the new lockout error from
+  `claim_household_role_invite`, `Too many failed join attempts…`, as HTTP 429.
+- **Informational:** `consume_quota` / `check_quota_status` assign `timezone('utc', now())`, a timestamp
+  without time zone, to a `timestamptz` variable. Window boundaries therefore depend on the session
+  `TimeZone`. That is harmless while PostgREST sessions stay on UTC, the Supabase default.

+# Dependency and Supply-Chain Audit
+
+Date: 2026-10-20. Base commit: `952098d`. This is a report only. No dependency file was changed.
+
+Scope:
+- `ai_service/requirements.txt`, `Dockerfile`, `docker-compose.yml`
+- `web_app/package.json` and `package-lock.json`
+- `flutter_app/pubspec.yaml` and `pubspec.lock`
+- CDN-loaded scripts in `landing_page/*.html`, `ai_service/static/index.html` and `ai_service/_landing_impl.py`
+
+## Method and tool versions
+
+| Stack | What was run | Tools |
+|---|---|---|
+| Python | Installed `requirements.txt` into fresh scratch venvs on Python 3.11.17 (the Dockerfile version) and on 3.13.16. Ran `pip-audit -l` and `pip-audit -r requirements.txt`. Checked the version floors (`>=` lower bounds) against the OSV API. Ran the hermetic test suite against the latest resolved versions. Built a hashed lock as a preview (`uv pip compile --generate-hashes`), not committed. | pip 26.2.2, pip-audit 2.10.1, uv 0.11.32, pipdeptree |
+| Node | `npm ci`, `npm audit --omit=dev`, `npm audit`, `npm outdated`, `npm audit signatures`, plus a check of lockfile integrity and hosts | node 22.22.0, npm 10.9.4 |
+| Flutter | `flutter pub get --enforce-lockfile` (the lock was not changed), `flutter pub outdated` and `--json --show-all` (discontinued, retracted and advisory flags), then all 152 hosted `pubspec.lock` packages through `https://api.osv.dev/v1/querybatch` with ecosystem `Pub`. The OSV query was checked against a known-vulnerable control (`http 0.12.2` correctly returns GHSA-4rgh-jx4f-qfcq). | Flutter 3.47.7, Dart 3.13.5 |
+
+Resolved Python set: 95 packages, the same on 3.11 and 3.13. Main versions: fastapi 0.156.3, starlette 1.9.0, pydantic 2.14.1, litellm 1.106.1, supabase 2.33.0 (postgrest, realtime, storage3 and supabase-auth also 2.33.0), uvicorn 0.54.0, httpx 0.28.1, redis 8.1.0, reportlab 5.0.1, python-jose 3.5.0, PyJWT 2.15.1 (transitive), cryptography 50.0.2.
+
+Test results with the latest-resolved set: **584 passed on Python 3.11 and 584 passed on Python 3.13**. The current floating resolution therefore works today.
+
+---
+
+## Findings by severity
+
+| ID | Severity | Stack | Finding | Reachable? | Action |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| DEP-01 | **High** (supply chain) | Python | No lock, constraints or hashes. Every requirement is `>=` with no upper bound. The `litellm>=1.40.0` range includes **litellm 1.82.7 and 1.82.8, which contained credential-stealing malware** (MAL-2026-2144 / PYSEC-2026-2), and 1.40.0 itself, which has 59 OSV records (several Critical). | The malware runs on `import litellm`, so it is fully reachable for any build that resolved to those versions. Today's resolution (1.106.1) is clean. | Add a hashed lock and install with `--require-hashes`. Raise the floors. Check the deployed image (see below). |
+| DEP-02 | **Medium** | Python | `python-jose 3.5.0`: **CVE-2026-85394 / GHSA-3qf3-8w2g-rqmx / PYSEC-2026-4298** (an incomplete fix for CVE-2024-33663, an HMAC/asymmetric algorithm-confusion bypass using DER public keys). Rated Critical by OSV. **No fixed version exists.** The library is minimally maintained. | **Not reachable in the current `auth.py`** (reasoning below) | Migrate `auth.py` to PyJWT, which is already installed through `supabase-auth`. Then drop `python-jose[cryptography]`. |
+| DEP-03 | **Medium** (if deployed) | Web | `landing_page/index.html:108` and `landing_page/mobile.html:11` load `https://cdn.tailwindcss.com?plugins=forms,container-queries`: no version, no SRI, and the script runs at runtime with full DOM access. `index.html` contains the VIP form that posts to the API. | Yes, if these pages are served. They are listed as prototypes in WEB-13. | Precompile the CSS with the `web_app` Tailwind toolchain. A versioned CDN URL is only a stop-gap. |
+| DEP-04 | Low | Python | `ecdsa 0.19.2`: **CVE-2024-23342 / GHSA-wj6h-64fc-37mp** (Minerva timing attack on P-256 signing). No fix is planned upstream. | No. python-jose selects the `cryptography` backend when it is installed (confirmed: `jose.backends.ECKey` is `CryptographyECKey`), and the service only verifies signatures. The advisory covers signing and ECDH. | The package goes away with the DEP-02 migration (`ecdsa` is pulled in only by python-jose). |
+| DEP-05 | Low | Node | 7 dev-only advisories (5 high, 2 moderate), all from the `tailwindcss@3.4.19` build chain: `braces 3.0.3`, **GHSA-vfj7-8cjw-p6xm** (CVSS 7.5, no fixed `braces` release, so chokidar, micromatch and fast-glob are also flagged), and `postcss-selector-parser 6.1.4`, **GHSA-rj75-hqrm-r3gf** (CVSS 5.9, fixed in 7.1.6). `npm audit --omit=dev` finds **0**. | No. These only run at build time, on developer-controlled content globs and CSS. Nothing ends up in the shipped bundle. | Plan a Tailwind 4 migration. Do not run `npm audit fix --force` blindly (see below). |
+| DEP-06 | Low | Docker | Floating base tag `python:3.11-slim` with no digest. `pip install --upgrade pip` is unpinned. No hash checking. Test-only packages (pytest, respx, fakeredis, pytest-asyncio) ship in the production image. The "~200MB" comment is wrong: site-packages alone is about 440 MB, and litellm accounts for 170 MB of it. | Partly. The test tools are dead weight in production, and pytest CVE-2025-71176 is local-only. | Pin the base image by digest. Split the requirements. Install from the lock with `--require-hashes`. |
+| DEP-07 | Low | Flutter | Declared but never imported: `flutter_local_notifications` (also the most outdated package, 17.2.4 against 22.3.2) and `timeago`. `intl: any` is unconstrained. The SDK constraint `>=3.3.0` does not match the lock, which needs Dart `>=3.12.0` and Flutter `>=3.44.0`. | Unused plugins still add native code and manifest entries. | Remove the two unused packages. Set `intl: ^0.20.2` and `sdk: ^3.12.0`. |
+| DEP-08 | Low | Flutter | 14 packages are held back by major-version constraints, and 36 more can move to newer versions without any `pubspec.yaml` change. **0 OSV advisories, 0 discontinued, 0 retracted** among 152 hosted packages. | No known vulnerabilities | Run `flutter pub upgrade` for the lock-only updates (supabase_flutter 2.17.2 to 2.18.3 and others). Schedule the majors (table below). |

+
+## Python details (`ai_service`)
+
+### DEP-01: no lock, floors only, and the litellm malware release
+
+`requirements.txt` has 14 direct requirements, all of the form `>=X`. Each build resolves to whatever is newest on PyPI that day. Concretely:
+
+- The **litellm** floor `>=1.40.0` allows:
+  - **1.82.7 and 1.82.8 (MAL-2026-2144 / PYSEC-2026-2)**, published on 2026-03-24 with a stolen PyPI token after the Trivy compromise. The payload runs on import. It harvests environment variables, `.env` files, SSH keys and cloud metadata tokens, sends them to `models.litellm[.]cloud`, and installs a systemd persistence unit.
+  - **1.40.0 itself**, which has 59 OSV records, including:
+    - GHSA-gppg-gqw8-wh9g / CVE-2024-5751 (eval RCE, Critical, fixed in 1.40.16)
+    - GHSA-4xpc-pv4p-pm3w / CVE-2026-49468 (host-header authentication bypass, Critical, fixed in 1.84.0)
+    - GHSA-6wvf-77m9-58rm / CVE-2026-37004 (SSTI, Critical, fixed in 1.83.7)
+    - GHSA-3cv6-jpf6-8222 / CVE-2026-84377 (SSRF and credential exfiltration, fixed in 1.96.2)
+
+  Reachability: almost all of these records concern the **LiteLLM Proxy server**: its admin UI, SSO, MCP, guardrails and `/prompts` endpoints. This service uses only the SDK (`litellm.completion` in `chat_parser.py`, `receipt_scanner.py` and `support_agent.py`). It does not install the `[proxy]` extra and never starts the proxy. So the CVEs are **not reachable** at any version. **The malware is reachable at any version that contains it.**
+- The git history begins on 2026-10-19 (it was squashed), so this repository cannot show whether any environment was built during the malware window.
+  - **Owner check:** run `pip show litellm` in the running Railway container, or look at old build logs and any developer `.venv` created in late March 2026.
+  - If 1.82.7 or 1.82.8 ever appears, treat the host as compromised and rotate every secret it held: `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` / service role key, `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET`, `GOOGLE_API_KEY`, `WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `RESEND_API_KEY` and any Railway token.
+- Range of packages that could move to a breaking new major version through these unbounded floors:
+
+| Requirement | Floor | Resolves today | Major-version exposure |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `fastapi>=0.111.0` | 0.111.0 | 0.156.3 | FastAPI is still 0.x, so any minor release may break. It now pulls in **starlette 1.9** (a starlette major), which already warns "Using `httpx` with `starlette.testclient` is deprecated; install `httpx2`". A future starlette release could break the test suite. |
+| `pydantic>=2.7.0` | 2.7.0 | 2.14.1 | No upper bound, so a future pydantic 3 would be installed automatically. FastAPI and litellm cap at `<3`, which would make the resolver fail or backtrack instead. |
+| `supabase>=2.16.0` | 2.16.0 | 2.33.0 | supabase-py 3.x would arrive automatically. `postgrest_compat.py` exists only because postgrest behaviour already changed between minors. Deprecation warnings for `timeout` and `verify` already show up in tests. |
+| `litellm>=1.40.0` | 1.40.0 | 1.106.1 | Releases almost daily with a large transitive tree (boto3, openai 2.x, huggingface_hub 1.x, tokenizers, tiktoken, jinja2, aiohttp). It is the highest-risk dependency, as the malware above shows. |
+| `redis>=5.0.0` | 5.0.0 | **8.1.0** | Already three majors past the floor. Tests pass with fakeredis 2.40, but nothing pins this. |
+| `reportlab>=4.0.0` | 4.0.0 | **5.0.1** | Major already crossed. `tests/test_pdf_statement.py` passes. Pulls in pillow 13, which requires Python 3.11+. |
+| `pytest-asyncio>=0.23.0` | 0.23.0 | **1.4.0** | Major already crossed (strict mode by default). Tests pass. |
+| `uvicorn[standard]>=0.30.0`, `httpx>=0.27.0` | | 0.54.0, 0.28.1 | Both are 0.x and may break on any minor. |
+
+**Would a lock or constraints file help? Yes.** It is the main fix for DEP-01 and DEP-09. Recommended approach:
+
+1. Keep `requirements.in` (or the current `requirements.txt`) with the direct dependencies. Raise these floors:
+   - `litellm>=1.96.2,<2`: covers the newest fixed advisory and is past the malicious versions.
+   - `python-dotenv>=1.2.2`
+   - `pytest>=9.0.3`
+   - `supabase>=2.16.0,<3`
+   - `pydantic>=2.7,<3`
+2. Generate the lock: `uv pip compile requirements.in --python-version 3.11 --generate-hashes -o requirements.lock`. This works today: it produced 95 pins in the dry run, and the preview was not committed.
+3. In the Dockerfile, use `pip install --require-hashes --no-deps -r requirements.lock`.
+4. Move pytest, pytest-asyncio, respx and fakeredis to `requirements-dev.txt` so they stay out of the production image.
+
+Upgrade risk: low. The resolved set already passes all 584 tests. A lock freezes that set; it does not change it.
+
+### DEP-02: python-jose (CVE-2026-85394)
+
+The advisory works like this: python-jose's HMAC key wrapper accepts an asymmetric public key in DER form as if it were an HMAC secret. An attacker who knows the public key can then forge an HS256 token, but only when the verifier passes the public key to `jwt.decode` without restricting `algorithms`.
+
+Why the current code is not exposed (`ai_service/auth.py`, `_decode_token`):
+- It reads the header `alg` and branches on it explicitly.
+- `ES256` uses a JWKS key filtered to `kty == "EC"`, `crv == "P-256"` and `alg == "ES256"`, with `algorithms=["ES256"]`.
+- `HS256` uses `SUPABASE_JWT_SECRET` (a shared secret, never a public key), with `algorithms=["HS256"]`.
+- Any other `alg` is rejected before verification.
+- The public key is therefore never handed to the HMAC path.
+
+Remaining risk: a future refactor could pass a single key object with both algorithms, or `alg` could be read from the token. There is also no upstream fix, so any later variant will not be patched.
+
+Recommendation: migrate `auth.py` to **PyJWT**. It is already installed (PyJWT 2.15.1, required by `supabase-auth>=2.12`).
+- `jwt.PyJWK(jwk_dict)` replaces `jose.jwk.construct`.
+- `jwt.decode(..., algorithms=[...], audience=..., issuer=..., options={"require": ["exp", "iat", "sub"]}, leeway=30)` replaces the jose call.
+- `jwt.get_unverified_header` has the same name.
+
+Then remove `python-jose[cryptography]`. That also removes `ecdsa`, `rsa` and `pyasn1` (closing DEP-04).
+
+Upgrade risk: medium-low. About 60 lines change in one module, and `tests/test_jwt_hardening.py` covers the alg allow-list, `kid` handling, JWKS throttling and the exp, iat, sub, aud, iss and role checks. Watch for small differences in exception types: PyJWT raises `jwt.PyJWTError` subclasses, not `JWTError`.
+
+### Python version
+
+- The Dockerfile uses 3.11, which receives security fixes until 2027-10. The resolved set and the test suite also work unchanged on **3.13**, so moving the base image to `python:3.12-slim` or `python:3.13-slim` is low risk.
+- The comment `# Compatible with Python 3.10+` in `requirements.txt` is out of date. starlette 1.9 and pillow 13 require Python >=3.11, so on 3.10 pip would resolve to a different, untested set of older versions. Change the comment to 3.11+, or add `python_requires` / `.python-version`.

An `overrides` entry forcing `postcss-selector-parser@^7.1.6` under `postcss-nested@6` is not recommended: it crosses a major of the parser API.

+
+| File | External resource | Pinned? | SRI? |
+|---|---|---|---|

+
+`ai_service/static/index.html` loads only self-hosted, hashed bundles (`/assets/index-*.js`), and `_landing_impl.py` loads no third-party JavaScript. Both are fine.
+
+Tailwind documents the Play CDN as development-only. If the CDN or that URL were compromised, the attacker would get script execution on the landing page and could read or redirect the VIP form submission. Fix: compile the CSS at build time. The `web_app` toolchain already exists. At minimum, pin a version path such as `cdn.tailwindcss.com/3.4.17`. This is already tracked as WEB-13 (Low) in `ui_web.md`. It should become Medium if `landing_page/` is deployed publicly.

+
+Already in good shape:

+- `.dockerignore` excludes `.env*`, tests and dev scripts (the API-25 fix)

+2. `pip install --upgrade pip` installs whatever pip is current. Pin it, or skip the upgrade when installing from a hashed lock.
+3. `pip install -r requirements.txt` has no hashes (see DEP-01). Use `--require-hashes` with a lock file.
+4. Test dependencies are installed into the runtime image. Split them into `requirements-dev.txt`.
+5. The image-size comment (~200MB) is inaccurate: about 440 MB of site-packages, of which litellm is 170 MB, botocore 31 MB and cryptography 16 MB. A smaller LLM client (calling the Gemini REST API directly with the httpx already present) would remove most of the tree and most of the supply-chain risk. That is an architecture decision and is listed here as an option only.

+# End-to-end results: ai_service + real PostgREST + local Postgres
+
+Date: 2026-10-20. Branch `audit/claude-comprehensive-review`, base commit `952098d`.
+Suite: `tests/e2e/` (how to run: `tests/e2e/README.md`).
+
+## Environment achieved
+
+| Component | What ran | Real or faked |
+|---|---|---|
+| Database | PostgreSQL 16.15, database `bt_e2e` rebuilt from `00_local_supabase_stubs.sql` + `schema.sql` + `seed.sql` + all 41 migrations (`run_tests.py --psql --rebuild --no-tests`) | Real |
+| REST layer | PostgREST **12.2.3** official static binary (`jwt-secret` = HS256 test secret, `db-anon-role=anon`, `db-schemas=public`, connects as login role `bt_e2e_authenticator` granted `anon`/`authenticated`/`service_role`) | **Real** |
+| Supabase URL layout | Python gateway proxying `/rest/v1/*` byte-for-byte to PostgREST (Kong stand-in) | Real traffic, thin proxy |
+| Auth (GoTrue) | Not run. Users are rows inserted into `auth.users` (the real `handle_new_auth_user` trigger creates `public.users`); access tokens are GoTrue-shaped HS256 JWTs (`aud=authenticated`, `iss={SUPABASE_URL}/auth/v1`, `role=authenticated`) signed with the test secret. `auth.uid()`/`auth.jwt()` read `request.jwt.claims`, which PostgREST sets from the verified token. | Simulated |
+| ai_service | The real FastAPI app (`main.app`) served by uvicorn 0.54 on a loopback port; supabase-py 2.33.0 / postgrest-py 2.33.0 with a locally signed `service_role` JWT as `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY`; `ENV=development`; no Redis (in-memory limiter + DB quota) | Real |
+| LLM | `litellm.completion`/`acompletion` replaced by a queue of canned JSON responses; empty queue raises (exercises the heuristic fallback) | Faked |
+| E-mail | `mail_service.RESEND_ENDPOINT` pointed at a local capture endpoint; `RESEND_API_KEY` unset for the "absent" case | Faked provider endpoint only |
+| Storage | `/storage/v1` in-memory stub (no scenario uploads; QR receipts need none) | Stubbed |
+| Network | Socket guard: any non-loopback connect fails the run. One hit was caught during bring-up (litellm fetching its price map from GitHub at import) and is now disabled with `LITELLM_LOCAL_MODEL_COST_MAP=True`. Final runs: zero outbound attempts. | Enforced |
+
+Not covered: GoTrue itself (signup/refresh/ES256 JWKS path), Supabase storage-api and image
+receipts (Gemini vision), Redis-backed limiter/idempotency, Realtime, the Flutter and web clients.
+The live Supabase project, Railway and every LLM/e-mail provider were never contacted.
+
+Python 3.13.16, FastAPI 0.156.3, httpx 0.28.1, litellm 1.106.1, python-jose 3.5.0, psycopg 3.3.6,
+pytest 9.1.1.
+
+## Results
+
+Full run with rebuild: **30 passed, 8 xfailed (strict), 0 failed** in ~2 min.
+
+| # | Scenario | Tests | Result |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 1 | Households: family (husband admin + wife member via spouse invite) and roommates (admin + 2 via peer invites); invite single use; admin-only invites; brute-force lockout → 429 with `Retry-After: 900` (correct code refused while locked; direct `join_household_by_code` RPC also refused); forged / expired / wrong-issuer / service-role tokens → 401 on API and PostgREST | 5 | Pass |
+| 2 | Chat commit by every member of both households (creator = JWT subject, 1 LLM call each); heuristic fallback without LLM; ZATCA QR receipt (no LLM) preview + commit with `wife_personal`, fingerprint de-dup on rescan, contradicting class → 422; `cycle_key` for payday 27 and payday 10 at Riyadh 23:59/00:00 boundaries and month boundaries where the UTC date differs, with each cycle's budget charged exactly its own rows; `client_occurred_at` window | 7 + 1 xfail | Pass; **E2E-03** |
+| 3 | Nafaqah: wife-paid shared expenses → husband owes 345.50; partial 100.25; overpayment 409 with `outstanding` (API) and refused by `record_spouse_reimbursement` directly; full repayment through `/households/{id}/reimbursements` routed to the ledger; reverse direction 409; allowance 500 → spent 150.75 / remaining 349.25, overspend reported (−50.75); wife cannot set her allowance (API 403, RPC refused); `/settlement` (any `split_ratio`) and `/settlement-v2` equal the ledger outstanding, no 50/50 | 4 + 2 xfail | Pass; **E2E-01, E2E-02** (roommate settlement) |
+| 4 | Member edits own tx via PostgREST; other's tx edit/delete/creator change → 403 from the DB; via API: installment linking and chat enrichment of other's tx → 403, own → 200; admin edits/deletes anyone's; shared pool created by admin only; member pool withdrawal → 403, admin → OK (fee booked); co-admin promotion (DB role synced, co-admin edits others' tx via PostgREST); co-admin cannot demote primary (API 403, RPC refused, raw membership PATCH refused) nor transfer primary; primary transfer; former primary demotable; last admin protected | 3 + 2 xfail | Pass; **E2E-06, E2E-07** |
+| 5 | IDOR sweep: 55 API calls (every household-scoped route plus B-object ids under A's household) by A's admin and by A's member → all 403/404, no B data in any body, B's rows byte-identical before/after; cross-household enrich/dependent-delete/receipt path → B untouched; PostgREST: 13 tables return `[]` for B, inserts/updates/deletes into B refused, 12 household-scoped RPCs with B's id and spoofed `p_actor_user_id` refused | 4 + 3 xfail | Pass; **E2E-04, E2E-05** |
+| 6 | DB quota without Redis: 30 chat calls OK, 31st 429, `api_quota.count` = 31, still 429 after resetting the in-memory limiter (DB authoritative), other user unaffected, `consume_quota` not client-callable; receipt quota 10 → 429; inquiries: no provider → 503 (public and in-app), fake Resend → 200 with correct To/Reply-To/Authorization, honeypot silent, in-app identity from JWT only, provider 500 → 502, per-IP limit 5 → 429 | 5 | Pass |
+| 7 | DB-06: transfers of 1.005 / fee 0.001 / 0.001 and income 1.005 or negative parts → 400, balances and transfer table unchanged, 1.01 + 0.25 fee conserves money; chat 10.005 stored = returned amount (2 dp); 3-dp allowance → 422. Mixed multi-step sequence (API budgets, income, transfers, chat, QR receipt, PostgREST inserts with accounts, edits of amount/category/account/timestamp across cycles, admin edit + delete, `/budgets/recalculate`): `budgets.spent_amount == Σ transactions` per (category, cycle) and every account balance == income − debits − transfers out − fees + transfers in after every step | 3 | Pass |
+
+## Bugs found (each is a strict xfail in the suite)
+
+Reproduce any of them with `BT_E2E=1 python -m pytest tests/e2e/<file>::<test> --runxfail`.
+
+### E2E-01 (High): roommate settlements can never be recorded
+`POST /households/{id}/reimbursements` in a non-family household always answers 500.
+`supabase_client.record_household_reimbursement` inserts `paid_by` and `notes`, which do not exist
+on `public.transactions`; PostgREST answers `PGRST204 Could not find the 'notes' column`.
+Repro: roommate member A → `POST /households/{hh}/reimbursements {"household_id": hh, "payer_id": A,
+"recipient_id": B, "amount": 75}` → 500, no row. Test:
+`test_03_nafaqah_and_settlement.py::test_roommate_settlement_reimbursement_is_recorded`.
+
+### E2E-02 (High): multi-roommate settlement never reports any debt
+`GET /households/{id}/settlement-v2` (mode `multi_roommate`) selects `transactions.paid_by` (no such
+column: `42703`); the error is caught and `txs = []`, so `pairwise_debts`/`simplified_debts` are
+always empty. Independently, chat/receipt commits never persist the payer: `insert_transaction`
+first sends `paid_by`/`beneficiary` (PGRST204) and retries without them, so even a fixed query
+would have no payer to read. Repro: roommate pays 300 shared by chat → settlement-v2 shows nothing
+owed (expected 200 owed to the payer). Test:
+`test_03_nafaqah_and_settlement.py::test_roommate_multi_party_settlement_reports_debts`.
+(Side effect: every chat/receipt commit costs a failed insert and a warning log; `/settlement`
+v1 also fails its first query and falls back.)
+
+### E2E-03 (Low): unknown category override → 500
+`POST /agent/chat-transaction` with `category_code` not in the taxonomy: the DB trigger's `23503`
+propagates through `insert_transaction`'s fallback chain as an unhandled `APIError` → 500 instead
+of a 4xx. Test: `test_02_expense_commits_and_cycles.py::test_unknown_category_override_is_a_client_error`.
+
+### E2E-04 (Low): helper RPCs leak another household's admin / husband id
+`household_primary_admin_id(uuid)` and `nafaqah_husband_id(uuid)` are SECURITY DEFINER, EXECUTE-able
+by `authenticated`, and return the user id for any household id without a membership check;
+`nafaqah_is_spouse_member(uuid, uuid)` is a membership oracle. Repro (any signed-in user):
+`POST /rest/v1/rpc/household_primary_admin_id {"p_household_id": "<other household>"}` → the
+owner's UUID. Test: `test_05_idor_sweep.py::test_postgrest_helper_rpcs_do_not_leak_other_household_members`.
+
+### E2E-05 (Medium): sub-category definitions are global and writable by any member
+`cost_control_sub_categories` has no `household_id`. `GET /budgets/sub-categories?parent_code=X`
+lists another household's custom sub-categories (custom codes are guessable `CUSTOM-…`), and
+`POST /budgets/sub-categories` (membership of the body's household only; no admin, no ownership of
+`parent_code`) inserts a definition under any parent — a system category or another household's
+custom category — which every household then sees (`GET /budgets/sub-categories`, chat preview
+`available_sub_categories`). Repro: member of A posts `{"household_id": A, "parent_code":
+"OPEX-DINING", "name_en": "Planted by A"}` → B's `GET /budgets/sub-categories?parent_code=OPEX-DINING`
+includes it. Tests: `test_05_idor_sweep.py::test_sub_categories_of_other_household_are_not_listed`,
+`::test_sub_category_cannot_be_planted_into_other_households`.
+
+### E2E-06 (Medium): members administer budgets through the API
+The database reserves budget writes for admins (`budgets_insert_admin`/`budgets_update_admin`) and
+`POST /households/{id}/categories/toggle` requires an admin, but `POST /budgets/categories`,
+`DELETE /budgets/categories/{code}`, `POST /budgets/sub-allocations` and
+`POST /budgets/sub-categories` use only `verify_household_access` with the service role. Repro: plain
+member → `POST /budgets/categories {"household_id", "code": "OPEX-DINING", "allocated_amount": 1}`
+→ 200 (allocation 900 → 1) and `DELETE /budgets/categories/OPEX-DINING?household_id=…` → 200
+(category deactivated); the same member is refused by RLS when patching `budgets` directly. Test:
+`test_04_permissions.py::test_member_cannot_administer_budgets_through_the_api`.
+
+### E2E-07 (High): self-assignable `financial_role` rewrites who owes whom
+`authenticated` has UPDATE on `users.financial_role` (`users_update_own_profile`), and that column
+alone decides Nafaqah mode, the husband/wife and the debt direction. Repro: roommate →
+`PATCH /rest/v1/users?id=eq.<self> {"financial_role": "spouse"}` → 200; the flat becomes
+`family_nafaqah` (`/nafaqah` mode, `/settlement` mode), the roommate's next chat expense is stored
+`wife_reimbursable` and the primary admin is shown as owing it. A wife can likewise set herself to
+`provider` and drop the family out of Nafaqah mode. Test:
+`test_04_permissions.py::test_member_cannot_self_assign_financial_role`.
+
+## Observations (not marked as bugs)
+
+- `accounts.balance` is client-settable on INSERT of a personal account and `reconcile_account_balance`
+  sets an arbitrary balance; neither leaves a ledger entry, so "balance == ledger" holds only for
+  accounts opened at 0 and never reconciled (the money tests do exactly that).
+- Chat amounts with a third decimal are rounded by Python `round()` on a float (1.005 → 1.0,
+  2.675 → 2.67) while Postgres rounds `numeric` half away from zero (1.005 → 1.01, 2.675 → 2.68, what
+  a direct PostgREST insert stores). Stored and returned values agree on each path, so nothing is
+  minted, but the API and the app's direct writes can round the same input differently.
+- The fixed-window `consume_quota` resets at epoch-aligned 600 s boundaries, so a burst straddling a
+  boundary can get up to 2× the limit; the in-memory sliding window still caps a single instance.
+
+
+## Re-run on the merged branch (2026-10-20)
+
+After merging the final backend review (FR-B-01/02/04/05), the suite was re-run on the fully merged branch: **35 passed, 3 xfailed**. E2E-01, E2E-02, E2E-06, E2E-07 and the planting half of E2E-05 now pass (they were fixed independently by FR-B-01, FR-B-02, FR-B-05 and FR-B-04), so their `xfail` marks were removed. Still open: E2E-03 (Low), E2E-04 (Low), E2E-05 listing (Medium).
+

+
+Full run with rebuild: **39 passed, 0 xfailed, 0 failed**.
+

+|---|---|---|---|

+| E2E-04 (Low) | **Fixed in the repo** (`d08dc07`); live needs migration `20261020600000` | EXECUTE on the three helpers revoked from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated (service_role keeps it). Callers: `household_primary_admin_id` ← `protect_primary_admin_membership` (trigger), `get_household_members`, `promote_member_to_admin`, `revoke_admin`, `remove_member`; `nafaqah_husband_id` ← `set_member_allowance`, `get_spouse_reimbursement_balance`, `record_spouse_reimbursement`; `nafaqah_is_spouse_member` ← `validate_transaction_nafaqah_class` (trigger), `get_member_allowance_status`, `set_member_allowance`, `get_spouse_reimbursement_balance`, `record_spouse_reimbursement`. All SECURITY DEFINER, owned by postgres; no RLS policy, view or constraint uses them; no `.rpc()` in ai_service, Flutter or web (branch and `origin/main`). | e2e `test_postgrest_helper_rpcs_do_not_leak_other_household_members` (now regular); `supabase/tests/22_*.sql` |
+| E2E-05 (Medium, listing) | **Fixed** (`06fc7ed`); live needs migration `20261020600000` for direct PostgREST reads | API lists and creates sub-categories only under a system category or a custom category of the caller's household (foreign/unknown parent: empty list on GET, 403 on POST); chat preview scoped. DB: `cost_control_sub_categories` rows readable only with their parent category (global or caller's active household), client writes and anon revoked. Residual by design: definitions under system categories remain shared (needs a `household_id` column to change). | e2e `test_sub_categories_of_other_household_are_not_listed` (now regular, also checks PostgREST and that the owner still sees them), new `test_admin_cannot_add_sub_categories_under_another_households_category`; `ai_service/tests/test_sub_category_scoping.py`; `supabase/tests/22_*.sql` |

+# Independent review (Fable) — 2026-10-21
+
+Three independent reviewers (a different model from the team that wrote the code) reviewed branch
+`audit/claude-comprehensive-review` @ `bcd2baf`, report-only. Every finding was reproduced (SQL as
+`SET ROLE authenticated` with `request.jwt.claims`, FastAPI `TestClient` with real JWT verification,
+or the real-stack e2e harness) unless marked *suspected*. Reproduction files are in the session
+scratchpad (`fable_db/`, `fable_api/`, `fable_logic/`).
+
+Owner decisions taken on 2026-10-21 for this round:
+- **Nafaqah provider:** the household's primary admin is the provider (husband) by default; an admin
+  can change it. Stored explicitly per household — never inferred.
+- **Wife personal purchases** are charged to her allowance **only**; they do not count against the
+  household category budgets.
+
+Status of each item is tracked in `FIX_LOG.md`.
+
+## A. Nafaqah / money logic
+
+| ID | Sev | Finding | Where | Fix direction |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| FABLE-LOGIC-01 | High | Family vs roommate mode is decided by the per-**user** `users.financial_role`, but users can belong to several households. A wife who claims a `peer` invite elsewhere flips her family to `shared_split` (husband shown as owing 150 of a 300 debt, ledger unreadable: `22023 Reimbursements apply to a spouse member`); a spouse joining roommates by code turns the flat into `family_nafaqah` and the rent split disappears. | `20261020010000:118-122,216-223`; `20261020300000:61-76`; `20261020400000:977-998`; `nafaqah_service.py:182-184,210-262`; `settlement_engine.py:137-139,266-277,545-560` | Financial role per membership (`household_memberships.financial_role`); invite claims write the membership row; helpers, `load_family_context` and settlement read it; `users.financial_role` only a cache of the active household; refuse `nafaqah_class` writes when the household has no provider. |
+| FABLE-LOGIC-02 | High | Editing/deleting/declassifying a `wife_reimbursable` advance after a partial repayment silently corrupts the ledger: 300 advance, 200 repaid, amount edited to 100 → outstanding 0, hidden overpaid 100; the wife's next 50 advance is swallowed (`exceeds the outstanding balance of 0.00`). `overpaid` is never shown in the app. | `20261020300000:396-414`; no trigger on UPDATE/DELETE; `edit_transaction_sheet.dart:290-318`; `installment_service.py:222-249`; `nafaqah.dart:154-167`; `family_reimbursement_card.dart:189,283` | `BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE` guard (same advisory lock as repayments) refusing changes that make advances < repayments; expose `overpaid` in API and card; installments refuse classified rows. |
+| FABLE-LOGIC-03 | Medium | Settlement v2 splits chat/receipt **personal** expenses among all roommates: `insert_transaction` never writes `beneficiary_type/beneficiary_id` (default `household`), so "قهوتي 15" makes the others owe 5 each; `/settlement` and `/settlement-v2` disagree. The edit sheet never updates those columns either. | `supabase_client.py:443-478`; `settlement_engine.py:46-49,469-474`; `multi_roommate_settlement_card.dart:122`; `edit_transaction_sheet.dart` | Map `beneficiary` → `beneficiary_type/beneficiary_id` on insert and edit; v2 reads structured columns. |
+| FABLE-LOGIC-04 | Medium | The husband is inferred (any `provider`, preferring the primary admin) and `financial_role` defaults to `provider`, so an adult son who created the household becomes the Nafaqah provider. | `20261020400000:977-998`; `nafaqah_service.py:255-261`; `20261015_…:5-6` | Explicit `households.nafaqah_provider_user_id` (default primary admin, admin-changeable); `family_member` default for non-spouse joiners. |
+| FABLE-LOGIC-05 | Medium | Changing payday mid-cycle leaves stale `cycle_key`s: allowance and category budgets of a cycle include purchases outside its dates (Nov 5 rows stay `2026-11` after payday 27→10). | `supabase_client.py:657-687`; `20261020300000:249-261,302-307` | On payday change re-stamp `cycle_key` for the open cycle onward and move current `member_allowances`/`budgets` rows. |
+| FABLE-LOGIC-06 | Medium | `wife_personal` purchases also raise the household category budget (counted twice). Owner decision: allowance only. | `20261019080000:138-156` | Exclude `wife_personal` from budget triggers/recalculation/forecasts. |
+| FABLE-LOGIC-07 | Medium | LLM-fallback classifier misreads common Saudi phrasing ("دفعت فاتورة الكهرباء" → wife_personal; "زوجتي دفعت المقاضي" → no class; "paid by my husband…" → wife_reimbursable; pronoun suffixes captured as child names). 7 of 15 phrases wrong. Mitigated by the confirmation card. | `chat_parser.py:201-224,414-419` | Extend phrase/keyword lists, exclude pronoun suffixes, ask when undetermined. |
+| FABLE-LOGIC-08 | Low | Roommate pairwise ledger drops the un-itemised part of a receipt (VAT/discount): 115 receipt with one 100 item → 50 owed instead of 57.50. | `settlement_engine.py:459-467` | Attribute `amount − Σitems` pro-rata. |
+| FABLE-LOGIC-09 | Low | Dart money parsing rounds with binary floats ("1.005" → 1.00, "0.285" → 0.28). | `flutter_app/lib/models/money.dart:45` | Parse to integer halalas from the string, half-up. |
+
+Verified correct: salary-cycle parity SQL/Python/Dart (0 mismatches over 60,388 date×payday pairs incl. Riyadh midnight, Dec→Jan, Feb 29, payday 29–31); no spousal split in family paths; overpayment rejected under advisory lock; wife cannot set her own allowance; Decimal/halala exactness; roommate debt simplification optimal; DB-18 legacy rows admin-only; offline replay carries Nafaqah fields.
+
+## B. Database security (migrations applied to live)
+
+| ID | Sev | Finding | Where | Fix direction |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| FABLE-DB-01 | High | Any member reads open invite codes (`invites_select_household` for all members) and can claim the spouse/provider invite meant for someone else: becomes "the wife", links the manual member record, creates Nafaqah debt, real invitee gets "already used". Same via `join_household_by_code`. | `20261020100000:177-181`; `20261020010000:79-128,195-228` | Invites readable by admins only; a trigger refusing a claim by an existing member of the invite's household. |
+| FABLE-DB-02 | Medium | Account deletion still fails for anyone who created or claimed an invite: `household_invites.created_by/used_by` are `ON DELETE NO ACTION` (the SEC-01 `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS … SET NULL` was a no-op). **Confirmed on live.** | `20261019030000:66-67`; `20261015_…:262-264` | `created_by` → SET NULL, `used_by` → CASCADE; extend test 16. |
+| FABLE-DB-03 | Low | A co-admin re-joining by code / claiming an invite of their own household is silently demoted (sync trigger copies `users.role`); the primary admin gets a hard error. | `20261020010000:115-144,216-223`; `20261018_membership_sync…:128-144` | RPCs no-op for existing members; sync trigger never downgrades. |
