+# Final Fresh-Eyes Review: Flutter App and Web
+
+Branch `audit/claude-comprehensive-review`, reviewed from `952098d` (base `4ab1534`). Date: 2026-10-20.
+Scope: `git diff 4ab1534...HEAD -- flutter_app/lib web_app/src landing_page`, the API clients in
+`flutter_app/lib/services` checked against `ai_service/routes` + `models.py`, and every Supabase table/RPC call
+checked against `supabase/migrations`. Backend and SQL were read only; nothing was changed there.
+
+## Summary
+
+The merged parallel work is mostly coherent: the API clients match the FastAPI routes and Pydantic models
+(Nafaqah, household roles, support/VIP inquiries, chat/receipt Nafaqah and idempotency fields), the RPC
+parameters match the SQL signatures (`transfer_between_accounts`, `record_income`, `reconcile_account_balance`,
+`get_user_households`, `switch_active_household`), and the l10n guard keeps en/ar/ur in sync.
+
+The real defects sat where streams met: the Nafaqah class was read from recorder-relative fields in the edit
+sheet, the offline queue had three different ways to block itself forever, the manual sheet still offered the
+roommate split between spouses and used a different family source than the other flows, and several paths still
+reported success (BNPL plan, installment payment, invite code, "saved offline") for things the server refused.
+
+| Severity | Found | Fixed | Open |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| High | 4 | 4 | 0 |
+| Medium | 7 | 7 | 0 |
+| Low | 14 | 3 | 11 |
+
+Gates after the last commit: `flutter analyze` 0 issues; `flutter test` **531 passed** (511 at the start, +20 new);
+`web_app`: `npm ci && npm run build && npm run lint` pass with 0 warnings.
+
+## Findings
+
+| ID | Sev | File:line | What / why | Verified how | Status |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| FR-A-01 | High | `flutter_app/lib/screens/home/edit_transaction_sheet.dart:183` | The Nafaqah class was derived from `paid_by`/`beneficiary`, which are relative to whoever recorded the row ('me' = recorder). A stored NULL class was not applied, so the wife opening the husband's ordinary expense saw "the husband owes the wife SAR X", and any save (e.g. fixing the amount) wrote `nafaqah_class = wife_reimbursable`: a false debt. Same in reverse for a wife-recorded "husband paid" row on the husband's phone. | 2 widget tests (failed before the fix) in `test/widgets/edit_transaction_sheet_test.dart`. | Fixed `f7f024b`: the stored class is authoritative (NULL = husband paid); class columns are not written until it is loaded. |
+| FR-A-02 | High | `flutter_app/lib/services/api/budget_api_client.dart:498`, `edit_transaction_sheet.dart:~700` | `createInstallmentPlan` parsed the normalised error map into an empty plan instead of failing. A refused BNPL conversion (403 for another member's transaction, 400, 5xx, offline) still rewrote the transaction to the monthly amount and showed "plan active": the budget dropped to 1/N with no plan behind it. | Unit tests in `test/services/budget_api_client_test.dart` (403 must throw). | Fixed `075333a` (`ApiRequestException`). |
+| FR-A-03 | Medium | `budget_api_client.dart:503`, `providers/installment_provider.dart:120`, `widgets/dashboard/installment_plans_card.dart:~630` | `payInstallment` returned a bogus plan for an error answer and `recordPayment` always returned true; the card refreshed silently (and called `setState` after an await without a mounted check). | Unit test (error answer → null). | Fixed `075333a`: null on error, card shows `rb_payment_failed`, mounted guard. |
+| FR-A-04 | Medium | `flutter_app/lib/screens/scanner/multi_page_receipt_scanner_screen.dart:~150` | The multi-page scanner committed without an `Idempotency-Key`, then queued the shots under a fresh key with `allow_duplicate=true`; a request that timed out after the server stored it was booked twice on replay. Every non-422 error (403, 409, 400) was also parked as "queued offline". | Code trace + `SyncWorker.shouldQueueAfterOnlineFailure` unit test + replay-key test in `test/services/sync_worker_test.dart`. | Fixed `f319930`: one key for the online attempt and the queue item; refusals are shown. |
+| FR-A-05 | Medium | `flutter_app/lib/widgets/transactions/manual_expense_sheet.dart:~540` | In a family household the manual sheet still offered the Family/Roommates toggle; choosing Roommates stored an equal `all_peers` split between the spouses (rule 02: never a split in family mode). | Widget test `family household: Nafaqah choice only, no roommate split toggle`. | Fixed `f43c19b`: toggle hidden when the household has a wife. |
+| FR-A-06 | Low | same file | The Nafaqah selector was shown in households without a wife; a chosen class was silently dropped (no spouse id). | Widget test (roommate household has no selector). | Fixed `f43c19b`. |
+| FR-A-07 | Medium | same file, `_loadHouseholdMembers` | Family detection used `users.household_id` (each member's *active* household) while the DB trigger, chat, receipt, edit and multi-page flows use household memberships. A wife active in another household was invisible to the husband's manual sheet, and a non-spouse family member could record a class the other flows never offer. | Widget tests `the wife is found even when her active household is another one` and `another family member ... without a Nafaqah class`. | Fixed `762d747`: context from `GET /households/{id}/nafaqah`, member list as offline fallback. |
+| FR-A-08 | Medium | same file, `_saveExpense` | Any insert error (including permanent DB rejections: 42501, the Nafaqah trigger 23503/23514, PGRST204) was queued and reported "saved offline"; the row then failed on every replay. A provider-refresh exception after a successful insert also queued the row a second time. | Widget tests (rejection is shown and not queued; network failure queues the same row id); `isPermanentInsertError` unit test. | Fixed `f43c19b`. |
+| FR-A-09 | High | `flutter_app/lib/services/sync_worker.dart:~290` | The queue drains FIFO and halts at the first transient failure. Every 403 was transient, but the current backend answers 401 for expired credentials and 403 only for "not a member / not allowed". One refused item (a household the user left; another account's queued entry after an account switch on the same device) sat at the head forever and nothing queued after it ever synced. Items of a previous account were also replayed with the current user's JWT. | Tests `a 403 refusal does not block later items`, `another account's queued items wait for that account`, legacy-firewall 403 stays transient. | Fixed `59b8e6b`: 403 = rejection with retry budget (except the legacy `Untrusted endpoint access` 403); items whose `user_id` is another account wait; multi-page and batch drafts now record `user_id`. |
+| FR-A-10 | Medium | `flutter_app/lib/screens/scanner/receipt_scanner_sheet.dart:~500` | When `/agent/scan-receipt` refused the commit (403 enriching another member's transaction, 409 Nafaqah state, 400) the sheet inserted the receipt directly into `transactions`, bypassing the server check; for a refused enrichment this created a second transaction. | Code trace; decision function unit-tested. | Fixed `f453087` (refined in `833526d`). |
+| FR-A-11 | Medium | `budget_api_client.dart:createRoleInvite`, `widgets/settings/role_invite_dialog.dart:76` | Both the client and the dialog fabricated a local `INVxxxxx` code when invite creation failed (403 for non-admins, offline) and presented it as generated; nobody can join with it. The existing widget test depended on the fake code. | Client test (403 throws) and widget test (no code, error, retry possible). | Fixed `95ba2e5` (+ `rid_generate_failed` / `rid_admin_only` in en/ar/ur). |
+| FR-A-12 | High | `flutter_app/lib/services/api/base_api_client.dart:_send`, `sync_worker.dart:classifyResponse` | `/agent/scan-receipt` answers HTTP 200 `{"status":"error"}` when it cannot read the images or the total is 0. The client map had no status code, identical to a lost connection, so the worker classified it transient: an unreadable queued receipt stalled the whole queue forever. | Regression test `a 200 {"status": "error"} answer is a rejection` in `test/services/offline_sync_regression_test.dart` (failed before). | Fixed `833526d`: transport failures carry `network_error`; other code-less error answers are rejections. Backend follow-up below. |
+| FR-A-13 | Low | `web_app/src/components/Simulator.tsx:58`, `App.tsx:46` | The AI demo sentence was captured once from the initial language and stayed Arabic after switching to English. | `npm run build` + reasoning (no web test runner in the repo). | Fixed `1988ed1` (`key={lang}`). |
+| FR-A-14 | Low | `web_app/src/components/Simulator.tsx:16-36` | Payday demo started on the 28th although it highlights the 27th standard; a payday after the end of a short month gave a wrong countdown. | Build + reasoning. | Fixed `1988ed1`. |
+| FR-A-15 | Low | `edit_transaction_sheet.dart:212` | Husband with several wives: switching an unclassified expense to a wife class silently uses the first wife (no chooser, unlike chat/receipt/manual). | Code trace. | Open: needs a wife chooser in the edit sheet; rare (multiple wives and a retroactive class). |
+| FR-A-16 | Low | `edit_transaction_sheet.dart:293`, `providers/transaction_provider.dart:352` | Every edit first sends `paid_by`/`beneficiary`, columns `transactions` does not have (confirmed in `live_db_preflight.md`), and only then the `raw_sms` fallback: two requests per save. `TransactionProvider.updateTransaction` (unused) writes the same columns and would always fail. | Code + migrations grep. | Open: harmless; remove the first attempt and the dead method in a cleanup. |

+| FR-A-20 | Low | `widgets/scanner/batch_item_review_sheet.dart:253,293` | Batch offline drafts store `image_local_path`, which replay ignores; the receipt image is never uploaded and a draft with amount 0 can only fail. Pre-existing. | Code trace (`OfflineQueueManager.loadImages`). | Open. |

+| FR-A-22 | Low | `web_app/src/i18n/translations.ts:369,711` | Family demo row shows the wife paying the groceries as "Budget 100% reconciled"; under rule 02 that is a debt the husband owes her. | Read. | Open: marketing copy, owner wording. |
+| FR-A-23 | Low | `screens/settings/ingestion_settings_screen.dart:986` | `setState` after `await Permission.notification.request()` without a mounted check. | Mounted-gap scan. | Open: trivial. |
+| FR-A-24 | Low | `flutter_app/lib/main.dart:181` | Sign-out resets transaction, budget and role providers but not `RecurringBillsProvider` / `InstallmentProvider`; a second account briefly sees the previous account's bills/plans until they refetch. | Code trace. | Open. |
+| FR-A-25 | Low | `flutter_app/lib/services/household_permissions.dart:27` | The app treats `account_type = shared_pool` as a pool even when `is_shared_pool` is false; the DB checks only the flag, so such an owner is hidden an allowed transfer. | Code vs `transfer_between_accounts` SQL. | Open: align once the data model guarantees both are set together. |
+
+## Contract checks that passed
+
+- Nafaqah: `GET/POST /households/{id}/nafaqah[/reimbursements|/allowance]` paths, methods, bodies
+  (`amount`, `payment_method` enum, `wife_user_id`, `cycle_key` pattern) and response fields match
+  `routes/nafaqah.py` and `nafaqah_service.py`; 409 `detail.code` (`overpayment`, `not_family`) is read from the
+  spread error map.
+- Roles: `/households/{id}/members`, `/members/{uid}/admin` (POST/DELETE), `/primary-admin` and `HouseholdRoster`
+  fields match `household_permissions.list_members`; 403/404/409 mapping matches `_permission_http_error`.
+- Chat/receipt: `paid_by`, `beneficiary`, `nafaqah_class` (`wife_reimbursable|wife_personal|none`),
+  `nafaqah_spouse_id`, `client_occurred_at`, `Idempotency-Key` are all read by `routes/chat.py` / `routes/receipts.py`.
+- Support/VIP: `POST /support/inquiries` and `/public/inquiries` bodies satisfy `extra="forbid"`, the locale regex
+  (`ar|en|ur`) and the honeypot; web/landing show success only on 2xx.
+- Direct inserts use only existing columns and allowed `source` values (`chat|receipt_scan|manual`); the
+  manual/batch/receipt rows set `nafaqah_class` and `nafaqah_spouse_id` together, as the trigger requires.
+
+## Backend issues to hand off (not changed here)
+
+1. **`/agent/scan-receipt` and `/agent/chat-transaction` answer HTTP 200 with `{"status": "error"}`**: the
+   receipt route for invalid images, unreadable receipts, total <= 0 and failed enrichment
+   (`receipt_scanner.py` ~L475-615), the chat route for failed enrichment (`chat_parser.py` ~L540). They should be 4xx
+   (422) so every client can tell a refusal from success by status code. FR-A-12 works around it on the client.
+2. **Idempotency is per process** without `REDIS_URL` (known MOB-06/12): FR-A-04's shared key only prevents the
+   duplicate when the replay reaches the same instance, or Redis is configured.
+3. Optional: `transfer_between_accounts` decides "pool" by `is_shared_pool` only (see FR-A-25); consider a CHECK
+   that `account_type = 'shared_pool'` implies `is_shared_pool`.

+# Final review: backend and database
+
+Base `4ab1534` (origin main), reviewed head `952098d` (`audit/claude-comprehensive-review`), 2026-10-20.
+Scope: `git diff 4ab1534...HEAD -- ai_service supabase`, excluding `ai_service/static` and `_landing_impl.py`.
+This was a fresh-eyes pass after many agents' work was merged. It looked for cross-module drift, wrong column, RPC and error contracts, authorization gaps, Nafaqah, permission and settlement interactions, cycle consistency, money types and dead code.
+
+## How findings were verified
+
+- **Real schema.** The column lists of `public.transactions`, `users`, `households`, `budgets` and other tables were read from the local rebuild (PG16, all migrations). `live_db_preflight.md` (D13 and MOB-03) says live has the same columns: there is **no `paid_by`, `beneficiary` or `notes` column** on `transactions`.
+- **Schema-aware fake.** The test fake (`ai_service/tests/fakes.py`) can now enforce a table's real column list (`client.schemas[...]`), rejecting unknown columns and returning only the selected ones, the way PostgREST does. The new tests in `ai_service/tests/test_final_review_backend.py` run with the live `transactions` columns. Before this, the fake accepted any column, so the suites stayed green while these code paths failed in production.
+- **Database-side proof.** `supabase/tests/21_review_backend_contracts.sql` runs on a fresh local rebuild. It proves the `financial_role` fix and the settlement-row contract. The old settlement payload fails there with 42703 and 23503.
+- Every fix was test-first: each new test was run and seen to fail before the code change.
+
+## Findings
+
+| ID | Sev | Where (at `952098d`) | What and why | Verified how | Status |
+|---|---|---|---|---|---|
+| FR-B-01 | High | `ai_service/supabase_client.py:1089-1128` (`record_household_reimbursement`), `routes/households.py:305-377` | **Recording a roommate settlement failed on every call.** The insert named the columns `paid_by` and `notes`, which do not exist, and the category `OPEX-SETTLEMENT`, which does not exist either (the category trigger raises 23503). `POST /households/{id}/reimbursements` therefore always returned 500. Before the branch the error was swallowed and the endpoint reported success. The payer and recipient were also never checked against household membership. When the family lookup failed, the route fell through to the roommate path, which would record a split in a family household. | Strict-fake API tests. SQL test 21: the old payload gives 42703 and 23503; the new row inserts as service role, gets a `cycle_key` and leaves budgets unchanged. | Fixed `65a244a` (DB proof `6f34dfc`). The row now uses only existing columns: payer in the `PaidBy:` audit tag, recipient in `beneficiary_id` / `settlement_target_id`, `category_code` NULL, `source` manual, exact decimal amount, creator = caller. Both parties must be members. A failed family lookup is now an error. |
+| FR-B-02 | High | `ai_service/settlement_engine.py:490-502` (`calculate_settlement_v2`) | **Roommate debts were always empty.** The query selected `paid_by`, so it failed. The `except` replaced the result with `txs = []`, so every roommate household showed no debts and the family spending breakdown showed zeros. | Strict-fake test (`test_settlement_v2_roommate_debts_use_creator_as_payer`, `..._appears_in_settlement_v2`). | Fixed `65a244a`. Only existing columns are selected. The payer is the `PaidBy:` member id, or the creator for "me" or no tag, or the other member for "partner" in a two-person household. Otherwise the transaction is not attributed (never guessed). Query errors now propagate instead of reporting "settled". |
+| FR-B-03 | Medium | `settlement_engine.py:82-106` (`calculate_partner_settlement`) | **`/settlement` never applied the Nafaqah class (API-16).** The primary query selected `paid_by` and `beneficiary`, always failed, and fell back to a query without `nafaqah_class`. In family mode, shared totals came from text heuristics; for example, a wife-paid advance appeared as paid by the husband. | Strict-fake test `test_partner_settlement_reads_nafaqah_class`. | Fixed `65a244a` |
+| FR-B-08 | Medium | `settlement_engine.py:117-163` | **Both partners saw themselves as the payer, and settlements were ignored in `/settlement`.** The `PaidBy: me` / `Beneficiary:` tags are relative to the transaction's creator, but `/settlement` read them as relative to the caller. Recorded settlements were not counted, and once they could be stored they would have counted as "shared paid by me". | `test_partner_settlement_tags_are_relative_to_the_creator`, `test_partner_settlement_counts_recorded_roommate_settlements` | Fixed `65a244a`. Tags are swapped when the creator is not the caller. Settlement rows adjust roommate balances only; family debts stay in the Nafaqah ledger. Settlements are also excluded from `recalculate_budgets` and the cycle breakdown, which used to add them to OPEX-MISC spending. |
+| FR-B-04 | High | `supabase/migrations/20261019030000_...:32` (still in effect after `20261020300000` / `400000`) | **Any member could change their own Nafaqah role.** `users.financial_role` stayed in the client-writable column list. Since the Nafaqah and permissions migrations, it decides who the wife is (creditor of the reimbursement debt), who the husband is, and whether a household is a family at all (settlement mode, `/reimbursements` routing). Any member could therefore set their own row to `spouse`: a roommate could turn the flat into a "family" and raise debts against the provider, and a wife could drop out of her own ledger. No app build or the web app writes this column (checked old and new builds). | SQL test 21 (before the fix the UPDATE returned 00000). | Fixed `6f34dfc`: **new migration `20261020500000_review_lock_financial_role.sql`**. It revokes the column privilege, is idempotent and changes no data. Live has no family household (preflight §4). **Owner: apply to live** (one statement). |
+| FR-B-05 | High | `ai_service/routes/budgets.py:294, 310, 332, 418, 443` | **Members could do admin-only budget work through the API.** RLS allows only admins to insert or update budgets and household categories (`budgets_*_admin`, `cost_control_codes_insert/update`), and the app shows those controls to admins only. The service-role routes checked membership only, so any member could add or edit categories, change allocations and sub-allocations, add or remove sub-categories and archive categories. | Real-JWT tests: a member gets 403 and the worker is never called; an admin gets 200. | Fixed `1929e98` |
+| FR-B-06 | Medium | `ai_service/supabase_client.py:298-322`, `chat_parser.py:678-684`, `receipt_scanner.py:745-751` | **Budget reallocation bypassed every check of the hardened RPC.** The deficit was a float (50.3 - 20.1 = 30.199999999999996). The DB-03 `reallocate_budget` RPC rejects amounts with more than 2 decimals, and any refusal (including insufficient allocation) fell back to two unlocked read-modify-write updates without those checks. The transaction was still flagged as reallocated. | Tests: the RPC receives `"30.20"`; a refused RPC leaves budgets untouched and returns False; chat sets `is_reallocated=False`. | Fixed `983b3b1`. The unused `deduct_from_budget` was removed: it would double-count spending next to the insert trigger. |
+| FR-B-07 | Medium | `ai_service/nafaqah_service.py:325-329` | **A database hiccup could silently erase a wife's debt.** `resolve_expense_nafaqah` treated any failure to load the household's members as "not a family". A chat or receipt commit during an outage stored a wife-paid expense without its class, so her reimbursement debt was lost without a trace. The settlement code already refuses this guess. | `test_commit_fails_instead_of_storing_an_unclassified_family_expense` | Fixed `1ad15b5`. Commits raise, so the client keeps the entry queued and retries. Previews still degrade. |
+| FR-B-11 | Medium | `supabase_client.py:431-434` (insert payload), `receipt_scanner.py:756` | **Receipt scans lost who paid.** Every chat and receipt insert first sent `paid_by` and `beneficiary`, failed, and was retried with a warning. Chat keeps the attribution in its `raw_sms` tags; receipts did not, so a receipt paid by the partner lost that information. | Strict-fake tests (one insert, no warning; receipt row carries `PaidBy: partner`). | Fixed `9715104` |
+| FR-B-09 | Low | `chat_parser.py:438`, `receipt_scanner.py:312`, `support_agent.py:132`, `docker-compose.yml:19`, `.env.example:24` | **Four different default models.** With `LITELLM_MODEL` unset, chat, receipts, support and Docker each fell back to a different model, and `.env.example` documents a fifth value. (Raised by the coordinator.) | `test_every_llm_call_uses_the_same_default_model` | Fixed `b95bc69`: `utils.DEFAULT_LITELLM_MODEL` (`gemini/gemini-3.6-flash-lite`, the documented value) and `utils.litellm_model()`, mirrored in `.env.example` and compose. `requirements.txt` was not touched. |
+| FR-B-10 | Low | `main.py:153`, `auth.py:25` | **Dead `IS_PRODUCTION` constants.** They were unused and defaulted to development, the opposite of `utils.is_production()`, which fails closed. The DB runner docstring also still mentioned CI. | grep (no references) | Fixed `b95bc69` |
+| FR-B-12 | Medium (design) | `users.financial_role` vs per-household Nafaqah | **A wife's role is global, but Nafaqah is per household.** `financial_role` is stored once per user, while the Nafaqah ledger and household mode are per household. Joining a second household by a role invite rewrites it: for example, a wife who joins a roommate flat as `peer` disappears from her family's ledger, and `get_spouse_reimbursement_balance` raises 22023. | Code reading (`claim_household_role_invite` / `join_household_by_code` in `20261020010000`) | Open: needs a per-membership financial role (schema and product change). |
+| FR-B-13 | Low | `20261020300000`, `20261020400000` | **The database lets any member classify a family expense.** A direct client insert can set `nafaqah_class` to `wife_reimbursable` while naming the wife, whoever the creator is. The API allows only the husband or that wife to classify. Impact is limited: admins see and can delete such rows. | Code reading | Open: needs a decision on who may classify by direct insert. Old app builds insert directly. |
+| FR-B-14 | Low | `household_primary_admin_id`, `nafaqah_husband_id`, `nafaqah_is_spouse_member`, `transaction_account_matches` | **Some database helpers answer questions about other households.** These SECURITY DEFINER helpers are executable by any authenticated user and answer for any household UUID (owner, husband, spouse membership, account ownership). Callers need the UUIDs. | ACL listing on the rebuild | Open: low value. Fix later by scoping them to the caller's households. |
+| FR-B-15 | Low | `routes/budgets.py:124-145` (`/budgets/recurring-bills/toggle`) | **Members can edit recurring-bill settings that RLS reserves for admins.** Any member can rewrite `budgets.sub_allocations` metadata (recurring flag, due day, name). The app's recurring-bills card is not admin-gated. | Code reading | Open: changing it would break a member-visible control (product decision). |
+| FR-B-16 | Low | `household_permissions.load_roster` vs `nafaqah_service.load_family_context` | **Two copies of the member loader.** Both run the same queries with slightly different role normalisation, so they can drift. | Code reading | Open: refactor only. |
+| FR-B-17 | Low | `idempotency.py` | **A replayed key can return a different request's result.** Idempotency keys are scoped to (user, endpoint) but not to the request body, so a reused key with a different body returns the first result. Keys are per process unless `REDIS_URL` is set (already MOB-06/12). | Code reading | Open |
+
+Checked and consistent: Nafaqah RPC names and parameters against SQL; SQLSTATE mappings (42501, 22023, 23514, 23503, P0002, HINT overpayment) against every `RAISE`; role RPC refusals; the husband resolution in Python and in `nafaqah_husband_id` (primary admin, then admin, then seniority); allowance and reimbursement permission rules in Python and SQL; cycle keys (`get_cycle_for_date` matches `get_saudi_cycle_for_timestamp`, Riyadh date, household payday); and EXECUTE grants: no SECURITY DEFINER function is executable by anon, and every one that takes `p_actor_user_id` rejects a JWT caller acting for someone else.
+
+## Remaining caveats
+
+- Settlement payments are still stored as `transactions` rows (`is_settlement = true`, category NULL). The Python aggregations now skip them. Client-side totals that sum every transaction (the Flutter feed and PDF statement) still list them; they are clearly labelled "Settlement Reimbursement".
+- The fixes to the settlement engines read who paid from the `PaidBy:` audit tags. Rows with no tag and no creator (the 14 legacy live rows) are not attributed in roommate debts. That is deliberate: guessing would assign money to the wrong person.
+
+## Test gates (final head)
+
+- `cd ai_service && /opt/venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider`: **610 passed** (584 at `952098d`).
+- `PGHOST=localhost PGPORT=54329 PGUSER=postgres python3 supabase/tests/run_tests.py --psql --rebuild --db bt_rev_backend`: **21/21 passed** (20 plus new test 21).

+# Flutter Logic & Security Audit (mobile app)
+
+Scope: `flutter_app/lib/services`, `lib/providers`, `lib/models`, `lib/main.dart`,
+`lib/supabase_config.dart`, `flutter_app/test`, `pubspec.yaml`, Android config. I made
+logic-only edits in screens and widgets where a fix needed them. Every changed screen or
+widget file is listed under "Files outside the mobile-logic ownership touched" at the end.
+Base commit: `f17eb2b`. File:line references point to the base commit unless noted.
+
+## Gates: baseline vs final
+
+| Gate | Baseline (`f17eb2b`) | Final |
+|---|---|---|
+| `flutter analyze` | No issues found | No issues found |
+| `flutter test` | 141 passed, 0 failed | 340 passed, 0 failed |
+
+After the follow-up fixes (MOB-19, MOB-26..28, UI-20, UI-25; commits `b73c865`..`29b83f6`), on base `820a6a3`: `flutter analyze` reports no issues and `flutter test` passes 410, fails 0.
+
+Toolchain: Flutter 3.47.7 stable / Dart 3.13.5. There is no Android SDK in the sandbox, so
+I could not build the APK or AAB. The Android manifest and Gradle changes are covered only
+by tests that check the source files.
+
+Two existing tests asserted the buggy behaviour and were rewritten:
+- `offline_queue_manager_test` "Prevents duplicate enqueue with identical payload" (MOB-05).
+- `sync_worker_test` expected a network error to consume a retry (MOB-09).
+
+The other new tests use injection points added by the fixes (`api:`, `transactionInserter:`,
+`blobDirectoryProvider:`, `AuthGate` builders). For those, the reproduction steps below show
+how each bug was observed.
+
+## Findings
+
+| ID | Sev | Title | Location (base) | Status |
+|---|---|---|---|---|
+| MOB-01 | Critical | Offline chat replay only *previews* (never stores); the offline "preview" fallback counts as synced | `services/sync_worker.dart:115-125`, `services/api_service.dart:63` | Fixed `b875e71` + test |
+| MOB-02 | High | Production URLs/keys hard-coded as defaults; the static `APP_AUTH_TOKEN` is sent from the client; no config validation | `supabase_config.dart:6-35`, `services/api/base_api_client.dart:11-14,68` | Fixed `b875e71`, `4e329a5` + tests |
+| MOB-03 | High | Manual expenses: the online insert names a non-existent `paid_by` column, so every save goes offline. The replay goes through the AI chat endpoint, which drops or coerces payer, beneficiary, account and time (the wife's reimbursable debt is lost) | `widgets/transactions/manual_expense_sheet.dart:221-266`, `sync_worker.dart:115-121` | Fixed `b875e71` + tests |
+| MOB-04 | High | Rows left in `syncing` after an app kill are never replayed again | `services/offline_queue_manager.dart:134-157` | Fixed `b875e71` + test |
+| MOB-05 | High | Two identical offline purchases are silently merged into one (content-hash dedup) | `offline_queue_manager.dart:88-117` | Fixed `b875e71` + test |
+| MOB-06 | High | Replays are not idempotent: no key is sent and `allow_duplicate=true`, so a request that timed out after the server committed gets booked twice | `sync_worker.dart:115-158` | Partly fixed `b875e71` (client) + test; backend must honour `Idempotency-Key` |
+| MOB-07 | Medium | FastAPI JSON error bodies (`{"detail":..}`) come back without `status:'error'`, so callers treat 4xx responses as success | `base_api_client.dart:109-123` (and in get/put/delete) | Fixed `b875e71` + tests |
+| MOB-08 | Medium | An expired JWT gets 403 from the firewall, not 401, so refresh-and-retry never fires; there is no proactive refresh | `base_api_client.dart:100-107`; `ai_service/main.py:186-192` | Fixed `b875e71` + tests |
+| MOB-09 | Medium | Transient failures use up the 5-try budget, so expenses end up `failed` with no visibility or retry. No FIFO guarantee | `offline_queue_manager.dart:167-186`, `sync_worker.dart:79-92` | Fixed `b875e71` + tests |
+| MOB-10 | Low | A concurrent flush returns 0 instead of awaiting the drain; only 50 items are processed per drain | `sync_worker.dart:59`, `offline_queue_manager.dart:135` | Fixed `b875e71` + tests |
+| MOB-11 | High (suspected) | Base64 receipt images are stored inline in SQLite. Rows over Android's ~2 MB CursorWindow make `getPendingItems` throw, which blocks the whole queue | `offline_queue_manager.dart:135-146`; enqueuers in scanner screens | Fixed defensively `b875e71` + test (not reproduced on a device) |
+| MOB-12 | Medium | Replayed expenses are stamped with the server's "now", so an expense made offline on the 26th lands in the next cycle | `ai_service/chat_parser.py:615` (`now_iso`) | Partly fixed `b875e71` (client sends `client_occurred_at`; manual expenses keep their own timestamp); backend must read it |
+| MOB-13 | High | Dart cycle keys use device-local time, a hard-coded 27, and ignore the payday clamping and labelling rules, so they diverge from `get_saudi_cycle_for_timestamp` | `screens/home/dashboard_screen.dart:347-353`, `budget_management_screen.dart:166-171`, `accounts_overview_screen.dart:37-43`, `widgets/accounts/record_income_sheet.dart:109-115`, `widgets/salary/payday_income_sheet.dart:131-134`, `widgets/dashboard/budget_hero_card.dart:24-53`, `models/models.dart:365-384` | Fixed `4e329a5` + 123 parity/invariant tests |
+| MOB-14 | High | Arabic-Indic and Urdu digits in amount fields parse to null, so an amount typed as "١٥٠" becomes 0 | 39 `double.tryParse(...text)` sites (screens/widgets) | Fixed `867a2e3` + tests |
+| MOB-15 | Medium | `_AuthGate` re-queries the profile on every auth event (hourly token refresh), which tears down and rebuilds the Dashboard. Offline start shows the onboarding screen to existing users | `main.dart:125-170` | Fixed `4e329a5` + widget tests |
+| MOB-16 | Medium | Providers keep the previous household's data (and Realtime channel) across a sign-out or household switch | `providers/transaction_provider.dart:93-98`, `budget_provider.dart:36-40` (init) | Fixed `4e329a5` + tests |
+| MOB-17 | Low | `selectCycle` race: a stale breakdown response overwrites the newer cycle | `providers/budget_provider.dart:42-47,98-115` | Fixed `4e329a5` + test |
+| MOB-18 | Medium | Android `allowBackup` is on by default (session tokens, offline queue and receipts end up in backups); release builds are signed with the debug key (plus a TODO) | `android/app/src/main/AndroidManifest.xml:24-27`, `android/app/build.gradle.kts:30-35` | Fixed `4e329a5` + source tests (build not verified) |
+| MOB-19 | Medium | The Supabase session (refresh token) sits in plaintext SharedPreferences | `supabase_flutter` default storage | Fixed `b73c865` + tests (`flutter_secure_storage` LocalStorage with one-time migration; APK build not verified, no Android SDK) |
+| MOB-20 | Low | The Dashboard `onItemsFlushed` listener is never cancelled (leak plus dead context) | `screens/home/dashboard_screen.dart:63` | Fixed `ef203c1` (no automated test: the screen needs an initialised Supabase) |

+| MOB-22 | Low | Stored signed receipt URLs are returned verbatim (they break after expiry); on failure the code returns unusable URLs; the cache is unbounded and survives sign-out | `services/receipt_storage_service.dart:106-145` | Fixed `ef203c1` + tests |
+| MOB-23 | Medium | `WEBHOOK_SECRET` (HMAC for chat and receipt calls) is compiled into the client and can be extracted | `supabase_config.dart:37`, `ai_service/routes/chat.py:32`, `routes/receipts.py:33` | Resolved (external review BLOCKER 2): the backend authenticates by JWT; a stale signature next to a valid JWT is logged and ignored; `WEBHOOK_SECRET` is an optional define and its absence never stops the app |

+
+## Details
+
+### MOB-01: offline chat replay never commits
+- **Root cause:** `SyncWorker._dispatchItem('chat')` called `ApiService.postChatTransaction`, whose `previewOnly` defaults to `true`. The server returns `pending_confirmation` and inserts nothing. When the backend was unreachable, `ChatApiClient` fell back to a local parse with `status:'preview'`, which the worker listed as a success, so it deleted the queue row.
+- **Reproduction:** queue `{'message': 'Coffee 15 SAR'}`, then drain against a mock server. The request body has `preview_only: true`. With an unreachable server the row is deleted and no transaction exists.
+- **Impact:** every expense captured offline through chat was lost, either silently or after 5 retries.
+- **Fix:** replay with `preview_only:false`. Only `success`/`enriched` (and `simulation`, which has nothing to store) count as committed. A local `preview` is treated as transient. `pending_confirmation`, `duplicate_candidate`, `non_transactional` and a missing status are permanent failures.
+- **Tests:** `test/services/offline_sync_regression_test.dart`, group MOB-01.
+
+### MOB-02: client configuration and static secrets
+- **Root cause:** `SUPABASE_URL`, the publishable key and the backend URLs had production default values, so any build without defines, including CI and tests, talked to production. `BaseApiClient` sent `X-App-Token` (APP_AUTH_TOKEN) whenever it was defined at build time. A token compiled into an APK can be extracted, and that token alone bypasses the FastAPI firewall.
+- **Fix:**
+  - Removed all defaults.
+  - `validateClientConfig` / `ensureValidClientConfig` (called first in `main`) throw a `StateError` naming each missing flag.
+  - Service-role keys (`sb_secret_…`, or a JWT with `role=service_role`) are rejected.
+  - Release builds must use `https://` and must define `WEBHOOK_SECRET`.
+  - `X-App-Token` is no longer sent; the per-user Supabase JWT is the only credential (the firewall already accepts a verified Bearer token).
+  - README documents the flags.
+- **Tests:** `test/services/client_config_test.dart`, plus updated `base_api_client_test`s.
+- **Ops note:** builds that relied on the defaults must now pass `--dart-define`s.
+
+### MOB-03: manual expense payer lost and every save diverted offline
+- **Root cause:** `public.transactions` has no `paid_by` column. I checked this against all repository migrations and the migrated local audit DB, but could not check the live DB. The online insert therefore always failed (PGRST204). The `catch` queued a free-text chat message with `paid_by:'wife'`, which the worker never forwarded. The chat endpoint also accepts only `me`/`partner`.
+- **Impact:** the user sees "Saved offline" while online. The replay goes through the AI parser, which loses account, payer, beneficiary and time. Islamic-compliance tracking of the wife's reimbursable spending (Nafaqah) silently disappears.
+- **Fix:** `models/manual_expense_row.dart` builds a schema-valid row:
+  - a client-generated `id`;
+  - a UTC timestamp;
+  - the payer recorded in the `raw_sms` `PaidBy:` tag, which `Transaction.fromMap` and the settlement engine already parse (wife becomes partner).
+
+  The same row is queued as `transaction_insert` and replayed verbatim through Supabase (RLS still applies). A `23505` unique violation on replay means the earlier attempt committed. Legacy `chat` rows now forward `spent_by`/`paid_by`/`category_code`.
+- **Tests:** `test/models/manual_expense_row_test.dart`; regression group MOB-03.
+- **Follow-up (DB owner):** if the live DB does have `paid_by`/`beneficiary`, add them to the migrations. `TransactionProvider.updateTransaction` (unused) and `edit_transaction_sheet` (has a `raw_sms` fallback) also write those columns.
+
+### MOB-04, MOB-05, MOB-09, MOB-10, MOB-11: queue mechanics
+- **MOB-04:**
+  - Root cause: `markSyncing` persists `syncing`, but `getPendingItems` reads only `pending`.
+  - Repro: an app kill between those two calls leaves the row stuck forever, while it still counts in the pending badge.
+  - Fix: `recoverInterruptedItems()` at the start of every drain. This is safe because drains are single-flight per process.
+- **MOB-05:**
+  - Root cause: the key was a SHA-256 of `(op, household, payload)`, so a second identical coffee returned the first row's id.
+  - Fix: a per-enqueue nonce. Callers can still pass an explicit `idempotencyKey` for double-submit protection.
+- **MOB-09:**
+  - Root cause: every failure did `retry_count+1` and became `failed` at 5, so five connectivity flaps (for example, Wi-Fi without internet) parked the expense where the UI never shows it.
+  - Fix: outcomes are classified.
+    - Transient (no HTTP status, 401/403, 408/425/429, 502-504, Socket/Timeout/Client exceptions): keep `pending`, keep the retry budget, halt the drain to preserve FIFO.
+    - Permanent: count toward `maxPermanentRetries`, then park as `failed`.
+  - New `getFailedCount` / `requeueFailed` / `OfflineSyncService.retryFailed` give the UI a retry entry point.
+- **MOB-10:** concurrent callers now share `_inFlightDrain`, and the drain loops over batches.
+- **MOB-11:** images are written to `<databases>/offline_blobs/<id>_<n>.b64` and the row stores only relative file names (iOS container paths change between updates). Rows are loaded one by one, and an unreadable row is quarantined as `failed` instead of throwing for the batch. A test covers a 4 MB image and a corrupt row.
+
+### MOB-06 / MOB-12: idempotency and original time (needs backend)
+- **Client fix:**
+  - Each replay sends `Idempotency-Key: <row key>`, stable across retries (test: timeout followed by retry reuses the key).
+  - It also sends `client_occurred_at` (the enqueue time, UTC).
+  - Manual expenses are fully idempotent through the client `id` and keep their own timestamp.
+- **Backend still to do (ai_service owner):**
+  - Persist `Idempotency-Key` for `/agent/chat-transaction` and `/agent/scan-receipt`, and return the original result on a repeat.
+  - Use `client_occurred_at`, clamped to the past few days, as the transaction timestamp.
+- Until then, a chat or receipt replay that times out after the server commits can still create a duplicate.
+
+### MOB-07 / MOB-08 / MOB-21: API client
+- All verbs now go through a single `_send`:
+  - It refreshes before sending when `session.isExpired`.
+  - On 401, or on the firewall's `403 "Untrusted endpoint access"`, it refreshes once and replays the identical request (same body and signature).
+  - A real authorisation 403 is not retried.
+  - Errors are normalised to `{..., status:'error', status_code, message}`.
+  - A non-object JSON success body no longer throws a `TypeError`.
+- `archiveBudgetCategory`, `renameSubCategory` and `removeSubCategory` now use the shared client.
+
+### MOB-13: salary cycle parity
+- `services/salary_cycle_service.dart` is a line-by-line port of the SQL:
+  - Riyadh date (UTC+3, no DST) of the instant;
+  - payday clamp 1..31 (null → 27), then per-month clamp;
+  - payday 1 means the calendar month;
+  - cycles labelled by the start month for payday ≤ 15 and by the next month for payday ≥ 16.
+- `test/services/salary_cycle_service_test.dart` holds an explicit table of 109 cases. I generated their expected values by running the migrated `get_saudi_cycle_for_timestamp` on local Postgres 16, never the live project. The table covers:
+  - the brief's cases (Oct 28 2026 → `2026-11`; Dec 27 → `2027-01`);
+  - the 21:00Z boundary;
+  - devices at +05:00 and -05:00;
+  - Feb and leap years with paydays 27/29/30/31;
+  - 30-day months with payday 31;
+  - paydays 1/10/15/16, out-of-range values and null;
+  - 60 seeded random instants.
+- Invariant tests check that, for 10 paydays, every day from 2026 to 2030 falls in exactly one cycle of 28-31 days, cycles are contiguous, and keys advance one month at a time.
+- The six scattered client computations now call the service. `BudgetProvider` caches the household payday (from `/households/{id}/payday`, persisted under the existing `payday_day` preference). `SalaryCycleInfo.daysTotal`/`daysElapsed` use UTC date arithmetic on the Riyadh "today".
+- **Repro of the old bug:**
+  - A device at UTC+5 at `2026-10-27T01:00+05:00` (Oct 26 23:00 in Riyadh) computed `2026-11`; the DB says `2026-10`.
+  - With payday 25, the client kept Oct 25-26 in `2026-10`; the DB says `2026-11`.
+- **Also found (backend, not mine):** `ai_service/salary_cycle.py` uses `datetime.now(timezone.utc).date()` rather than the Riyadh date, so it disagrees with the DB between 21:00 and 24:00 UTC.
+
+### MOB-14: Arabic-Indic digits
+- `models/money.dart` `parseMoneyInput` handles:
+  - digits U+0660-0669 and U+06F0-06F9;
+  - `٫` (decimal) and `٬`/`،`/`,` (grouping);
+  - NBSP and bidi marks;
+  - `SAR`/`ر.س`/`ريال`/`﷼`.
+- It rounds to halalas and returns null for non-numbers, keeping the old validation semantics. It replaced all 39 money-input `double.tryParse(...text)` sites. The dependent-allowance input formatter now accepts Arabic digits.
+
+### MOB-15 / MOB-16 / MOB-17: auth gate and providers
+- **AuthGate** (`main.dart`, now public and injectable):
+  - It looks up the household once per user id.
+  - `HouseholdResolver` caches the household per user, so an offline start opens the dashboard. Offline with no cache shows a "try again" retry state (existing l10n key), never onboarding.
+  - It initialises providers once per household and resets them on sign-out.
+  - Household join and leave flows navigate back through `AuthGate`, so sign-out is always observed (before, they replaced the gate route).
+- **Providers:** `TransactionProvider` and `BudgetProvider` clear their state and the Realtime channel on household change or `reset()`. In-flight responses for a superseded request are dropped using generation counters.
+
+### MOB-18: Android
+- Manifest:
+  - `allowBackup="false"`, `fullBackupContent="false"`;
+  - `dataExtractionRules` excludes every domain from cloud backup and device transfer;
+  - explicit `usesCleartextTraffic="false"`.
+- Gradle: release signing comes from the git-ignored `android/key.properties`. The debug key is used only when that file is missing, with a build warning. The TODO is gone.
+- Zero SMS policy: verified that there are no SMS permissions, receivers or SMS plugins (a test enforces this).
+
+### MOB-23: client-side HMAC secret (resolved)
+- The HMAC secret ships in every APK, so `X-Signature` proves nothing about the caller. The chat and receipt routes already call `verify_household_access` with the user's JWT.
+- **Resolution (external review BLOCKER 2):** user routes are authenticated by the JWT; `X-Signature` is optional defense in depth. A stale or unverifiable signature next to a valid JWT is logged and ignored (installed builds sign with the rotated-out secret); without a valid JWT it is 401 (`auth.verify_signature_if_present` on every router). `validateClientConfig` no longer requires `WEBHOOK_SECRET` in release builds, and `BaseApiClient` signs only when a secret was supplied (`signingSecret`, tests in `test/services/api/base_api_client_test.dart`). Builds can now drop the define entirely.
+
+### MOB-19: session in secure storage (follow-up fix)
+- **Fix:** `services/secure_session_storage.dart` implements supabase_flutter's `LocalStorage` on `flutter_secure_storage` 11 and is passed to `Supabase.initialize(authOptions: FlutterAuthClientOptions(localStorage: ...))` in `main.dart`. It uses the same key as the default storage (`sb-<project>-auth-token`).
+- **Migration:** on start, a plaintext session in SharedPreferences is written to secure storage, read back to verify, then deleted. If the secure write fails, the plaintext copy is kept so the user stays signed in, and the move is retried on the next start. A stale plaintext copy next to a secure session is deleted. `persistSession` and `removePersistedSession` always delete the plaintext key and never write it again.
+- **Android options:** `AndroidOptions()` (Keystore RSA-OAEP wrapped AES-GCM). The `encryptedSharedPreferences` flag relied on the deprecated Jetpack Security library and no longer exists in v10+; the plugin migrates data written by it (`migrateOnAlgorithmChange`). `resetOnError` drops an undecryptable value (e.g. after a restore) and the user signs in again instead of the app crashing. Plugin minSdk 24, app minSdk 26. `allowBackup` stays off (MOB-18). iOS: `first_unlock_this_device`.
+- **Not covered:** the PKCE code verifier (short-lived, used only during an OAuth/magic-link exchange) still uses the default SharedPreferences store.
+- **Limits:** I could not build the APK (no Android SDK). The Gradle/Kotlin compatibility of `flutter_secure_storage` 11 and `share_plus` 13 must be confirmed with a real `flutter build apk`.
+- **Tests:** `test/services/secure_session_storage_test.dart` (fake stores: migration, failed secure write, stale copy, persist/remove, unreadable keystore, wiring, minSdk/backup source checks).
+
+### MOB-26: statement PDF download (follow-up fix)
+- **Backend contract:** `GET /reports/statement-pdf?household_id=&cycle_key=` returns the PDF bytes behind `verify_household_access` (JWT). There is no signed-URL endpoint, so no backend change was needed or made.
+- **Fix:** `BaseApiClient.getBinary` reuses the JSON calls' auth path (refresh an expired session, one replay on 401 or the firewall's 403). It throws `ApiDownloadException` on any HTTP or network error. `BudgetApiClient.downloadStatementPdf` also rejects a 200 response without a `%PDF` header. `StatementPdfService` writes the file to `<cache>/statements/`, deleting earlier statements, and opens the system share sheet (`share_plus`) to open, save or send it. The transactions screen no longer shows or copies a URL; failures show a localized error.
+- **Tests:** `test/services/statement_pdf_download_test.dart`.
+
+### MOB-27: household settings saved server-first (follow-up fix)
+- **Fix:** `saveHouseholdSetting()` calls the API first. SharedPreferences, `SalaryCycleService.paydayDay` and screen state are updated only when the server returned `status: success`. A `false` result throws `HouseholdSettingNotSavedException` and shows "The server did not confirm the change. Your previous setting is still in effect." `PaydaySettingsCard` reverts its selection on failure. Monthly income and the rollover rule had the same bug and use the same helper. The best-effort direct `households` update now runs only after the API confirmed.
+- **Tests:** `test/services/household_setting_saver_test.dart`.
+
+### MOB-28: offline queue write failures (follow-up fix)
+- **Fix:** `OfflineQueueManager.enqueueOrThrow` and `OfflineQueueWriteException`. `OfflineSyncService.enqueue` now returns `Future<String>` and throws.
+- **Callers:**
+  - Chat used to enqueue fire-and-forget inside `setState`; it now awaits the write before replying.
+  - Manual expense keeps the sheet open with an error.
+  - Single and multi-page receipt scanners show the error and do not close.
+  - The batch review sheet no longer counts an unsaved receipt as saved; it stays on that receipt for a retry or skip.
+- **Tests:** `test/services/offline_queue_write_failure_test.dart` (closed SQLite DB, blob directory blocked, service contract, source checks).
+
+## For other owners
+- **Backend:** MOB-06/12 (Idempotency-Key, `client_occurred_at`), MOB-23 (HMAC with JWT), and `salary_cycle.py` using the UTC date.
+- **Secrets hygiene (ai_service, not mobile):** `ai_service/test_chat_endpoint.py` had a hard-coded fallback value for `WEBHOOK_SECRET` (default removed, file deleted in `71a3a70`, API-25). `ai_service/tests/test_sec04_jwt_and_secrets.py` lists previously leaked secret literals as scan patterns. Treat those values as compromised and rotate them if they were ever used in production.
+- **DB:** confirm whether the live `transactions` table has `paid_by`/`beneficiary` (MOB-03). After MOB-25 the households policy can hide `invite_code` from non-admins (DB-17).
+
+## Files outside the mobile-logic ownership touched (minimal logic edits)
+- `screens/home/dashboard_screen.dart`, `budget_management_screen.dart`, `screens/accounts/accounts_overview_screen.dart`: cycle-key helper (MOB-13); flush-listener cancel (MOB-20).
+- `screens/onboarding/household_screen.dart`, `screens/settings/ingestion_settings_screen.dart`: route through `AuthGate` (MOB-15), payday cache (MOB-13), membership RPC (MOB-25).
+- `widgets/transactions/manual_expense_sheet.dart`, `widgets/scanner/batch_item_review_sheet.dart`: schema-valid rows (MOB-03/24).
+- `widgets/accounts/record_income_sheet.dart`, `widgets/salary/payday_income_sheet.dart`, `widgets/dashboard/budget_hero_card.dart`: cycle service (MOB-13).
+- 17 screen and widget files: `double.tryParse` replaced by `parseMoneyInput` (MOB-14).

+# Live database pre-flight for the 20261020 audit batch
+
+Date: 2026-10-20 · Branch: `audit/claude-comprehensive-review` (from `8971d4a`) · Related: [`db.md`](db.md) (DB-15), [`MASTER_AUDIT_REPORT.md`](MASTER_AUDIT_REPORT.md) §6.2
+
+> Round 2 (2026-10-21, `20261020700000` + `20261020800000`): see [`live_db_preflight_round2.md`](live_db_preflight_round2.md).
+> Round 3 (2026-10-21, all four pending files `20261020700000`, `750000`, `800000`, `900000`): see [`live_db_preflight_round3.md`](live_db_preflight_round3.md).
+
+This document covers the 13 new migrations (`supabase/migrations/20261020010000_*` to `20261020400000_*`) and one pre-flight migration added by this review (`20261020005000_preflight_live_alignment.sql`). It answers four questions before the owner applies them to the live Supabase project:
+
+- How does live differ from the repository?
+- Do the migrations apply cleanly to a faithful copy of live?
+- Does the database test suite pass there?
+- In what order, and how, should the files be applied?
+
+Live was only read. Access was a read-only Management API role (`read_only=true`, connected as `supabase_read_only_user`) that ran catalog queries and aggregate `count(*)` queries. No DDL or DML was sent, no row was copied, and nothing was written to live.
+
+## 1. Verdict
+
+> **Status (2026-10-20): applied to live.** Backup taken (read-only JSON export of all `public` tables and `storage.buckets`), part A matched §4, the 14 files ran in order without error, part B matched §7, and the versions were recorded in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations` (§5.3).
+
+**Safe to apply: yes**, under these conditions:
+
+1. Apply the 14 files one at a time, in the order of §5, starting with the pre-flight migration.
+2. Deploy the backend (ai_service) only after the last file. Release the new app build after that.
+
+Why it is safe:
+
+- **Everything applied cleanly.** All 14 files applied without error to a replica of live built from live's own catalog. That replica:
+  - matches live on every table, column, constraint, index, policy, function body, EXECUTE grant, trigger, table and column grant, bucket setting and realtime table;
+  - was owned by a non-superuser `BYPASSRLS` role, as live's `postgres` is;
+  - held synthetic data that matches 49 of live's 50 aggregate counts. The one exception is the row count of the backup table (D8), which no migration reads.
+- **All tests passed.** The full DB suite passes on the migrated replica: **20/20** with live-shaped data, **20/20** on an empty replica, and **20/20** on a repo rebuild.
+- **No money moves.** Budget `spent_amount` totals and account balances are identical before and after.
+- **No existing row breaks a new constraint.** See the counts in §4.
+- **No privilege is missing.** Live's `postgres` owns every object the batch alters. It may create policies on `storage.objects` (`supautils.policy_grants` includes it) and may `UPDATE storage.buckets`. The storage triggers fire only on the bucket `name` and lifecycle columns, which the batch does not touch.
+- **There is a tested rollback.** [`../rollback/20261020_audit_batch_rollback_snapshot.sql`](../rollback/20261020_audit_batch_rollback_snapshot.sql) returns the replica's catalog exactly to live's pre-batch state. Re-applying the batch afterwards passes 20/20 again.
+
+The first replica run found one problem, now fixed. Test 14 (catalog guardrails) failed because live has functions in `public` that `anon` can execute and the repository does not:
+
+- the `unaccent` extension functions (live installs the extension into `public`);
+- `rls_auto_enable()`, the function behind the platform's `ensure_rls` event trigger.
+
+The fix is in §6. With it, the result is 20/20.
+
+Known consequences, all expected:
+
+- **Legacy transactions become admin-only.** All **14** live transactions have no recorded creator (`user_id IS NULL`). After `20261020400000` only household admins can edit or delete them. The owner decided on 2026-10-20 to keep this. One non-admin member (a `family_member` in a household with an admin) loses the ability to edit those legacy rows.
+- **One household has no primary admin.** One household has no members at all. It gets no primary admin (`owner_user_id` stays `NULL`). The other 3 get their single admin.
+- **SMS labels change.** The 10 `source = 'sms'` rows are relabelled to 8 `chat` and 2 `receipt_scan`, with 0 `manual`. Only the label changes: no amount or budget is touched, and the app already displayed these rows this way.
+- **Existing receipts are not rechecked.** Two existing receipt objects (`text/plain`, `application/octet-stream`) do not match the new bucket MIME list. Bucket limits apply only to new uploads, so they stay readable.
+
+## 2. Method
+
+| Step | What | Tool (all in this repo or reproducible) |
+|---|---|---|
+| Live inventory | `schema_migrations`; for `public`: tables, columns (type, default, nullability, generated), constraints (`pg_get_constraintdef`), indexes (`pg_get_indexdef`), RLS flags, `pg_policies` (`public`, `storage`), functions (`pg_get_functiondef`, `SECURITY DEFINER`, `proconfig`, EXECUTE for anon/authenticated/service_role), triggers (`public` + `auth.users`), views, types, table and column ACLs, owners, default ACLs, `storage.buckets`, publications, extensions, event triggers, supautils settings | Read-only catalog SELECTs |
+| Repo baseline | Stubs + `schema.sql` + `seed.sql` + every migration before `20261020`, then the same inventory | `run_tests.py --psql --rebuild --stop-before 20261020005000 --no-tests --db bt_repo_baseline` |
+| Diff | Keyed comparison (table, column, constraint name, policy, function signature, …) | §3 |
+| Replica | DDL generated from the live inventory, applied after `supabase/tests/00_local_supabase_stubs.sql`; public objects owned by a non-superuser `BYPASSRLS` role standing in for live `postgres` (member of anon/authenticated/service_role); live's `ensure_rls` event trigger and `unaccent`-in-`public` reproduced | Diff against live afterwards: only platform-only rows differ (§3.4) |
+| Live-shaped data | Invented rows matching every aggregate in §4 except the backup table's row count (4 households including the orphan, 14 creator-less transactions with the same `sms` note buckets, 39 receipt objects, …) | No live rows copied |
+| Apply + test | Each file applied as the owner role (`SET ROLE`), then `run_tests.py --psql --db <replica>`; also `run_tests.py --psql --apply-from 20261020005000 --db <replica>` | §6 |
+
+Local server: PostgreSQL 16.15. Live: PostgreSQL 17.6. Nothing in the batch depends on the version. The only catalog difference is the PG17 `MAINTAIN` table privilege, which is ignored in the diff.
+
+## 3. Live vs repository drift
+
+Classification:
+
+- **(a)** affects one of the 14 files;
+- **(b)** harmless drift;
+- **(c)** live has something the repository lacks and must capture.
+
+### 3.1 Schema objects
+
+| # | Drift (live vs repo baseline before `20261020`) | Class | Effect on the batch / action |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| D1 | `public.reallocate_budget(uuid,uuid,numeric)` **does not exist on live**, although `schema.sql` defines it. Today ai_service falls back to a two-step update (`ai_service/supabase_client.py:276`). | (a) `20261020030000` | `CREATE OR REPLACE` creates it with the admin/service-role checks. Its REVOKE/GRANT run after the create. Verified. |
+| D2 | `household_invites` already has RLS **enabled** on live. | (a) `20261020010000` §1 | `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` is a no-op. The rest of the file applies. |
+| D3 | `memberships_admin_manage` (the recursive policy, DB-02) **is absent** on live. | (a) `20261020020000` §2 | `DROP POLICY IF EXISTS` is a no-op. The recursion was never live. |
+| D4 | `cost_control_codes_insert` / `_update` / `_delete` policies **are absent** on live (only `_select` exists), so clients cannot write custom categories today. | (a) `20261020040000` | Creates the admin-only insert/update policies. Household admins gain the intended ability. |
+| D5 | `transactions` has **no CHECK on `source`** on live (the repo has one that includes `sms`). Live labels: `sms` 10, `chat` 3, `receipt_scan` 1. | (a) `20261020200000` | The DO-loop finds nothing to drop, then adds `transactions_source_check (chat, receipt_scan, manual)`. All 14 rows satisfy it after the relabel. |
+| D6 | `transactions_spent_by_check` (`me`/`partner`/`both`) **is absent** on live. All 14 live rows are valid. | (b) | Not touched by the batch. Deliberately not added in the pre-flight: the receipt scanner forwards the model's `spent_by` lower-cased, and today live accepts any value. Add it only after the API normalises `spent_by`. |
+| D7 | `households.rollover_rule text DEFAULT 'accumulate'` **exists only on live**. All 4 rows are `accumulate`. ai_service reads and writes it (`get_/set_household_rollover_rule`) and treats unknown values as `send_to_savings`. | (c) | **Captured** by `20261020005000` (`ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, same default; a no-op on live). `20261020400000` builds its column-list `UPDATE` grant from the live column list, so `rollover_rule` stays client-updatable for admins as today. The default `accumulate` is not a value the app recognises; whether to change it is a product decision. |
+| D8 | `public.budgets_spent_backup_20261019` **exists only on live**: 24 rows, RLS on, no policies. It was created by `supabase/backups/backup_budgets_spent_amount.sql`. | (b) | Not captured: it is a one-off backup. RLS hides its rows from clients. Drop it once the 2026-10-19 recompute is confirmed (owner). |
+| D9 | `public.rls_auto_enable()` + event trigger `ensure_rls` **exist only on live**. This is the platform feature that enables RLS on every new `public` table. The function keeps the default EXECUTE for `PUBLIC`, so `anon` can execute it. | (c), test 14 | **Handled** by `20261020005000`: `REVOKE EXECUTE … FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated` (guarded; the function is owned by `postgres`). An event-trigger function cannot be called directly, and the event trigger still fires after the revoke (verified on the replica with a non-superuser `CREATE TABLE`). The two new tables of `20261020300000` get RLS from the migration either way. |
+| D10 | The `unaccent` extension is installed in **`public`** on live (`extensions` in the repo stubs). Its 4 functions are anon-executable and owned by `supabase_admin`, so `postgres` can neither revoke nor relocate them. | (b), test 14 | Test 14 now skips extension member functions (`pg_depend.deptype = 'e'`); they are not app RPCs. |
+| D11 | Function bodies differ only in comments (`consume_quota`, `get_saudi_cycle_for_timestamp`) or CRLF line endings (`get_auth_user_household_id`, `get_auth_user_role`). Signatures, `SECURITY DEFINER`, `search_path` and grants are identical. | (b) | `20261020020000` replaces the two helpers anyway. |
+| D12 | Five column comments are missing on live (`budgets.sub_allocations`, `households.monthly_income`, `households.payday_day`, `transactions.qr_code_raw`, `users.payday_day`), and the old SMS wording remains on the `transactions`, `transactions.raw_sms` and `cost_control_codes` comments. | (b) | `20261020200000` rewrites the SMS comments. The five missing ones are cosmetic. |
+| D13 | Table grants are identical apart from PG17 `MAINTAIN`. Column grants (`accounts` ×7, `users` ×3) and storage policies (`receipts_*` ×3) are identical. Triggers (11 on `public` + `on_auth_user_created` on `auth.users`) and indexes (64) are identical. | (b) | None. |

+## 5. Apply plan
+
+### 5.1 Before you start
+
+1. **Take a backup.** Download one (Dashboard → Database → Backups), or `pg_dump` the `public` schema with data.
+2. **Run part A** of [`live_db_preflight_checks.sql`](live_db_preflight_checks.sql) in the SQL editor and compare it with §4. Note the two totals it prints (`budgets_spent_total`, `accounts_balance_total`).
+3. **Pick a quiet moment.** There are 4 users. Each file takes well under a second.
+
+### 5.2 Order and method
+
+**SQL editor, one file per run, in this order:**
+
+1. Open the file from this branch and paste the **whole** file.
+2. Click Run and expect "Success. No rows returned". Live runs it as `postgres`.
+3. Do not start the next file until the current one succeeds.
+
+All files except `20261020080000` (a single `UPDATE`) are wrapped in `BEGIN … COMMIT`, so a failure leaves nothing half-applied. If a file fails, stop and keep the error text. The files before it are complete and consistent on their own.
+
+| # | File | What it does on live (given §3/§4) | Coupling |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 1 | `20261020005000_preflight_live_alignment.sql` | `rollover_rule`: no-op (exists). Revokes PUBLIC/anon/authenticated EXECUTE on `rls_auto_enable()`. | — |
+| 2 | `20261020010000_audit_invites_rls_and_targeted_claims.sql` | RLS already on. Revokes anon on invites. Adds the target-member trigger. Fixes the two claim RPCs (DB-01, DB-05). | — |
+| 3 | `20261020020000_audit_membership_policy_recursion.sql` | Adds `is_household_admin`. Replaces the memberships read policy and revokes client writes. Backfills 0 rows. Makes the helpers membership-backed (DB-02). | — |
+| 4 | `20261020030000_audit_reallocate_budget_authz.sql` | **Creates** `reallocate_budget` (missing on live). EXECUTE for authenticated and service_role only (DB-03). | — |
+| 5 | `20261020040000_audit_cost_control_codes_policies.sql` | Admin-only category insert/update. Revokes anon/DELETE (DB-04). | — |
+| 6 | `20261020050000_audit_ledger_precision_and_income_append_only.sql` | 2-decimal and sign checks in `transfer_between_accounts` and `record_income`. Income and transfer ledgers become client read-only (DB-06, DB-07). | — |
+| 7 | `20261020060000_audit_transaction_cycle_key_integrity.sql` | The cycle-key trigger also fires on `cycle_key` writes (DB-08). 0 mismatching rows. | — |
+| 8 | `20261020070000_audit_definer_search_path_and_household_insert.sql` | Pins the `sync_user_household_membership` search_path. Drops direct household INSERT (DB-09, DB-10). | — |
+| 9 | `20261020080000_audit_receipts_bucket_limits.sql` | `receipts` bucket: 20 MiB, jpeg/png/webp, private (DB-11). | — |
+| 10 | `20261020090000_audit_sole_admin_account_deletion.sql` | Sole-admin handover before user delete (DB-12). | — |

+| 12 | `20261020200000_remove_sms_artifacts.sql` | Relabels 10 rows. Default becomes `manual`. New source CHECK (API-25). | Rejects new `source='sms'`. Released builds that still send `sms` explicitly would get a CHECK error, so release the new app build promptly. |
+| 13 | `20261020300000_nafaqah_wife_allowance_and_reimbursements.sql` | Nafaqah columns, `member_allowances`, `spouse_reimbursements`, RPCs. | Before the new backend. |

+
+Then run part B of the checks file (§7). Then deploy ai_service, then the app (MASTER §6.2 steps 2–3).

+Alternative to the SQL editor: run each file with `psql "<session-pooler connection string as postgres>" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 --single-transaction -f <file>`, in the same order.

+### 5.3 Recording the history, and the CLI (DB-15)
+
+**Do not run `supabase db push`, `supabase db reset --linked` or `supabase migration up` against this project yet.** No local file version matches a recorded live version (§3.3), so the CLI would treat all 41 local files as pending and try to replay the whole chain from `20260925_*` on the live database. The duplicate 8-digit prefixes (`20261008` ×3, `20261018` ×3, …) would then abort it part-way.
+
+After all 14 files succeed, optionally record them in the format the CLI expects: `version` = the file's 14-digit prefix, `name` = the rest of the filename. This is a write, so the owner runs it:
+
+```sql
+INSERT INTO supabase_migrations.schema_migrations (version, name)
+SELECT v, n FROM (VALUES
+  ('20261020005000', 'preflight_live_alignment'),
+  ('20261020010000', 'audit_invites_rls_and_targeted_claims'),
+  ('20261020020000', 'audit_membership_policy_recursion'),
+  ('20261020030000', 'audit_reallocate_budget_authz'),
+  ('20261020040000', 'audit_cost_control_codes_policies'),
+  ('20261020050000', 'audit_ledger_precision_and_income_append_only'),
+  ('20261020060000', 'audit_transaction_cycle_key_integrity'),
+  ('20261020070000', 'audit_definer_search_path_and_household_insert'),
+  ('20261020080000', 'audit_receipts_bucket_limits'),
+  ('20261020090000', 'audit_sole_admin_account_deletion'),
+  ('20261020100000', 'audit_rls_initplan_and_fk_indexes'),
+  ('20261020200000', 'remove_sms_artifacts'),
+  ('20261020300000', 'nafaqah_wife_allowance_and_reimbursements'),
+  ('20261020400000', 'admin_permissions_and_co_admins')
+) AS m(v, n)
+WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM supabase_migrations.schema_migrations s WHERE s.version = m.v);
+```
+
+The SEC-01..07 files (`20261019030000`, `060000`, `070000`, `080000`, `090000`) are applied on live but unrecorded. They can be added the same way. This is what `supabase migration repair --status applied <version>` writes.
+
+The DB-15 re-baseline is still an owner task, to do before using the CLI:
+
+1. Run `supabase db pull` to create a baseline migration from live.
+2. Mark it applied with `migration repair`.
+3. Move the pre-`20261020` files to an archive folder, so they are no longer replayed.
+4. Keep the 14-digit `20261020*` files after the baseline.
+

+  - `--no-tests` builds or applies without running the suite.

+## 8. Rollback notes
+
+[`../rollback/20261020_audit_batch_rollback_snapshot.sql`](../rollback/20261020_audit_batch_rollback_snapshot.sql) undoes the whole batch in one transaction. It was generated from the live catalog before the batch and verified on the replica (§6).
+
+What it cannot undo:
+
+- The relabel of `source` stays.
+- It drops the new tables and columns, so allowances, reimbursements, Nafaqah classes and primary-admin assignments made after the batch are lost.
+
+Undo per file, if only the last files have to go (roll back from the bottom up):
+
+| File | Undo | Data impact |
+|---|---|---|
+| 14 `…400000` | Drop the triggers `trg_bind_transaction_creator`, `trg_enforce_transaction_write_permission`, `trg_protect_primary_admin`, `trg_maintain_primary_admin` and the new functions. Restore `set_member_role`, `remove_member`, `get_user_households` (drop + create), `update_account_balance_on_transaction` and the transactions insert/update policies from the snapshot. Re-run `transfer_between_accounts` from file 6 and `nafaqah_husband_id` from file 13. Revoke the `households` column grants and grant table `UPDATE` back. Drop `households.owner_user_id`. | Primary-admin choices are lost. |
+| 13 `…300000` | Drop the trigger `trg_validate_transaction_nafaqah_class`, the tables `member_allowances` and `spouse_reimbursements`, the columns `transactions.nafaqah_*` and the `nafaqah_*`/allowance/reimbursement functions. | Allowances and reimbursements recorded are lost. Export them first. |
+| 12 `…200000` | `ALTER TABLE transactions DROP CONSTRAINT transactions_source_check; ALTER TABLE transactions ALTER COLUMN source SET DEFAULT 'sms';` Restore the comments. Live had no source CHECK before. | Relabel not reverted (label only). |
+| 11 `…100000` | Re-create the pre-batch policies (snapshot §7). Drop the 7 indexes. | None. |
+| 10 `…090000` | `DROP TRIGGER trg_handover_households_on_user_delete ON users; DROP FUNCTION handover_households_on_user_delete();` | None. |
+| 9 `…080000` | `UPDATE storage.buckets SET file_size_limit = NULL, allowed_mime_types = NULL WHERE id = 'receipts';` | None. |
+| 8 `…070000` | Restore `sync_user_household_membership` without `SET search_path`. Re-create `households_insert_authenticated`. Re-grant `INSERT`/`DELETE` and the anon privileges. | None. |
+| 7 `…060000` | Re-create `trg_populate_transaction_cycle_key` as `BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF timestamp, household_id`. | None. |
+| 6 `…050000` | Restore `transfer_between_accounts` and `record_income`. Re-create `income_insert_household`. Re-grant write privileges on `income_records` and `account_transfers`. | None. |
+| 5 `…040000` | Drop the two new `cost_control_codes` policies. Re-grant anon and `DELETE`. Live had no write policies before. | None. |
+| 4 `…030000` | `DROP FUNCTION reallocate_budget(uuid, uuid, numeric);` It did not exist on live, and ai_service falls back to a two-step update. | None. |
+| 3 `…020000` | Restore the two helpers. Replace `memberships_select_own_or_admin` with the pre-batch policies. Re-grant membership privileges. Drop `is_household_admin`. | Backfilled memberships (0 on live) stay. |
+| 2 `…010000` | Restore `join_household_by_code` and `claim_household_role_invite`. Drop the trigger `trg_validate_invite_target_member` and its function. Re-grant anon on `household_invites`. RLS stays on (it was on before). | None. |
