+-- ============================================================================
+-- Live pre-flight and post-apply checks for the 20261020 audit batch.
+-- Read-only: every statement is a SELECT. Run in the Supabase SQL editor.
+-- Context, expected values and the apply plan: docs/review/audit/live_db_preflight.md
+-- ============================================================================
+
+-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- A. PRE-APPLY: aggregate counts only (no row data). Expected values at
+--    2026-10-20 are in live_db_preflight.md, section 4. Run right before
+--    applying and compare; a difference means data changed since then, so
+--    re-read the "Impact" column of that section.
+-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+select
+ (select count(*) from public.households) as households,
+ (select count(*) from public.users) as users,
+ (select count(*) from auth.users) as auth_users,
+ (select count(*) from public.users u where not exists (select 1 from auth.users a where a.id=u.id)) as public_users_without_auth,
+ (select count(*) from public.household_memberships) as memberships,
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions) as transactions,
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions where user_id is null) as tx_user_id_null,
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions t where t.user_id is not null and not exists (select 1 from public.household_memberships m where m.household_id=t.household_id and m.user_id=t.user_id)) as tx_creator_not_member,
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions where source='sms') as tx_source_sms,
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions where source='sms' and raw_sms like 'Chat:%') as sms_to_chat,
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions where source='sms' and raw_sms like 'Receipt Scan:%') as sms_to_receipt_scan,
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions where source='sms' and (raw_sms is null or (raw_sms not like 'Chat:%' and raw_sms not like 'Receipt Scan:%'))) as sms_to_manual,
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions where source is null) as tx_source_null,
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions where source is not null and source not in ('sms','chat','receipt_scan','manual')) as tx_source_other,
+ (select string_agg(s, ',' order by s) from (select distinct source as s from public.transactions where source is not null) x) as tx_source_labels,
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions where spent_by is not null and spent_by not in ('me','partner','both')) as tx_spent_by_invalid,
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions where cycle_key is null) as tx_cycle_key_null,
+ (select count(*) from (select t.cycle_key, (coalesce(t.timestamp, t.created_at) at time zone 'Asia/Riyadh')::date d, greatest(1, least(31, coalesce(h.payday_day, 27))) pp
+     from public.transactions t join public.households h on h.id=t.household_id) x
+   where x.cycle_key is distinct from to_char(date_trunc('month', d) + (case when extract(day from d) >= least(pp, extract(day from (date_trunc('month', d) + interval '1 month - 1 day')))
+        then case when pp <= 15 then 0 else 1 end else case when pp <= 15 then -1 else 0 end end) * interval '1 month', 'YYYY-MM')) as tx_cycle_key_mismatch,
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions t join public.accounts a on a.id=t.account_id
+   where a.is_shared_pool=false and (t.user_id is null or a.owner_user_id <> t.user_id)) as tx_personal_account_not_creator,
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions t join public.accounts a on a.id=t.account_id where a.household_id<>t.household_id) as tx_account_other_household,
+ (select count(*) from public.households h where not exists (select 1 from public.household_memberships m where m.household_id=h.id and m.role='admin')) as hh_without_admin,
+ (select count(*) from public.households h where not exists (select 1 from public.household_memberships m where m.household_id=h.id)) as hh_without_members,
+ (select count(*) from public.households h where not exists (select 1 from public.household_memberships m where m.household_id=h.id and m.role='admin') and exists (select 1 from public.household_memberships m where m.household_id=h.id)) as hh_members_but_no_admin,
+ (select count(*) from (select household_id from public.household_memberships where role='admin' group by 1 having count(*)>1) x) as hh_multi_admin,
+ (select count(*) from public.users u where u.household_id is not null and not exists (select 1 from public.household_memberships m where m.user_id=u.id and m.household_id=u.household_id)) as users_active_hh_without_membership,
+ (select count(*) from public.users u join public.household_memberships m on m.user_id=u.id and m.household_id=u.household_id where u.role is distinct from m.role) as users_role_ne_membership_role,
+ (select count(*) from public.users u join public.household_memberships m on m.user_id=u.id and m.household_id=u.household_id where u.role='admin' and m.role<>'admin') as users_admin_but_member_membership,
+ (select count(*) from public.household_invites) as invites,
+ (select count(*) from public.household_invites i where i.target_member_id is not null and not exists (select 1 from public.household_dependents d where d.id=i.target_member_id and d.household_id=i.household_id)) as invites_target_other_household,
+ (select count(*) from public.household_dependents) as dependents,
+ (select count(*) from public.users where financial_role='spouse') as users_spouse,
+ (select count(*) from public.users where financial_role='provider') as users_provider,
+ (select count(*) from public.accounts) as accounts,
+ (select count(*) from public.accounts where is_shared_pool) as shared_pools,
+ (select count(*) from public.accounts a where a.is_shared_pool and not exists (select 1 from public.household_memberships m where m.household_id=a.household_id and m.user_id=a.owner_user_id and m.role='admin')) as pools_owner_not_admin,
+ (select count(*) from public.income_records) as income_records,
+ (select count(*) from public.account_transfers) as account_transfers,
+ (select count(*) from public.budgets) as budgets,
+ (select count(*) from public.cost_control_codes where household_id is not null) as custom_categories,
+ (select count(*) from public.api_quota) as api_quota_rows,
+ (select count(*) from public.invite_attempt_log) as invite_attempts,
+ (select count(*) from public.budgets_spent_backup_20261019) as backup_rows,
+ (select count(*) from storage.objects where bucket_id='receipts') as receipt_objects,
+ (select count(*) from storage.objects where bucket_id='receipts' and coalesce((metadata->>'size')::bigint,0) > 20*1024*1024) as receipts_over_20mib,
+ (select count(*) from storage.objects where bucket_id='receipts' and coalesce(metadata->>'mimetype','') not in ('image/jpeg','image/png','image/webp')) as receipts_other_mime,
+ (select count(*) from information_schema.columns where table_schema='public' and table_name='transactions' and column_name in ('paid_by','beneficiary')) as tx_paid_by_beneficiary_cols,
+ (select count(*) from information_schema.columns where table_schema='public' and table_name='transactions' and column_name in ('nafaqah_class','nafaqah_spouse_id')) as tx_nafaqah_cols,
+ (select count(*) from information_schema.columns where table_schema='public' and table_name='households' and column_name='owner_user_id') as hh_owner_col,
+ (select count(*) from public.households where rollover_rule is not null and rollover_rule not in ('send_to_savings','rollover_to_categories','fresh_start')) as hh_rollover_rule_unrecognised,
+ (select string_agg(r, ',' order by r) from (select distinct coalesce(rollover_rule,'<null>') as r from public.households) x) as hh_rollover_rule_values
+;
+
+-- Also note these two totals (your own aggregates) before AND after applying;
+-- they must not change (no migration in the batch moves money):
+SELECT (SELECT sum(spent_amount) FROM public.budgets) AS budgets_spent_total,
+       (SELECT sum(balance) FROM public.accounts) AS accounts_balance_total;
+
+-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+-- B. POST-APPLY: run after the last file. Expected values are in
+--    live_db_preflight.md, section 7 (budgets_spent_total and
+--    accounts_balance_total must equal the values noted before applying).
+-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+select
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions) as transactions,
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions where source = 'sms') as tx_sms,
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions where source = 'chat') as tx_chat,
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions where source = 'receipt_scan') as tx_receipt_scan,
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions where source = 'manual') as tx_manual,
+ (select pg_get_expr(d.adbin, d.adrelid) from pg_attrdef d join pg_attribute a on a.attrelid = d.adrelid and a.attnum = d.adnum
+   where d.adrelid = 'public.transactions'::regclass and a.attname = 'source') as source_default,
+ (select pg_get_constraintdef(oid) from pg_constraint where conrelid = 'public.transactions'::regclass and conname = 'transactions_source_check') as source_check,
+ (select count(*) from public.transactions where user_id is null) as tx_user_id_null,
+ (select sum(spent_amount) from public.budgets) as budgets_spent_total,
+ (select sum(balance) from public.accounts) as accounts_balance_total,
+ (select count(*) from public.households) as households,
+ (select count(*) from public.households where owner_user_id is not null) as hh_with_primary_admin,
+ (select count(*) from public.households h where owner_user_id is not null and not exists
+   (select 1 from public.household_memberships m where m.household_id = h.id and m.user_id = h.owner_user_id and m.role = 'admin')) as hh_primary_not_admin,
+ (select count(*) from public.households h where owner_user_id is null and exists
+   (select 1 from public.household_memberships m where m.household_id = h.id and m.role = 'admin')) as hh_admin_but_no_primary,
+ (select count(*) from public.household_memberships) as memberships,
+ (select relrowsecurity from pg_class where oid = 'public.household_invites'::regclass) as invites_rls,
+ (select relrowsecurity from pg_class where oid = to_regclass('public.member_allowances')) as member_allowances_rls,
+ (select relrowsecurity from pg_class where oid = to_regclass('public.spouse_reimbursements')) as spouse_reimbursements_rls,
+ (select count(*) from information_schema.columns where table_schema = 'public' and table_name = 'transactions' and column_name in ('nafaqah_class', 'nafaqah_spouse_id')) as tx_nafaqah_cols,
+ (select count(*) from information_schema.columns where table_schema = 'public' and table_name = 'households' and column_name in ('owner_user_id', 'rollover_rule')) as hh_new_cols,
+ (select file_size_limit from storage.buckets where id = 'receipts') as receipts_size_limit,
+ (select allowed_mime_types::text from storage.buckets where id = 'receipts') as receipts_mimes,
+ (select public from storage.buckets where id = 'receipts') as receipts_public,
+ (select count(*) from pg_policies where schemaname = 'public' and tablename = 'household_memberships' and policyname = 'memberships_admin_manage') as recursive_policy_left,
+ (select string_agg(policyname, ',' order by policyname) from pg_policies where schemaname = 'public' and tablename = 'cost_control_codes') as ccc_policies,
+ (select string_agg(policyname, ',' order by policyname) from pg_policies where schemaname = 'storage' and tablename = 'objects') as storage_policies,
+ (select count(*) from pg_policies where schemaname in ('public', 'storage') and not (roles <@ array['authenticated', 'service_role']::name[])) as policies_to_public_or_anon,
+ (select count(*) from pg_class c join pg_namespace n on n.oid = c.relnamespace where n.nspname = 'public' and c.relkind in ('r', 'p') and not c.relrowsecurity) as tables_without_rls,
+ (select string_agg(p.proname, ',' order by p.proname) from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace
+   where n.nspname = 'public' and has_function_privilege('anon', p.oid, 'EXECUTE')
+     and not exists (select 1 from pg_depend d where d.classid = 'pg_proc'::regclass and d.objid = p.oid and d.deptype = 'e')) as anon_executable_app_functions,
+ (select string_agg(p.proname, ',' order by p.proname) from pg_proc p join pg_namespace n on n.oid = p.pronamespace
+   where n.nspname = 'public' and p.prosecdef and not exists (select 1 from unnest(coalesce(p.proconfig, '{}')) cfg where cfg like 'search_path=%')) as definer_without_search_path,
+ (select count(*) from unnest(array[
+    'reallocate_budget(uuid,uuid,numeric)', 'consume_quota(uuid,text,integer,integer)', 'check_quota_status(uuid,text,integer,integer)',
+    'transfer_between_accounts(uuid,uuid,uuid,numeric,numeric,text)', 'record_income(uuid,uuid,text,text,text,numeric,numeric,numeric,numeric,timestamptz,text)',
+    'join_household_by_code(text)', 'claim_household_role_invite(text,uuid)', 'create_household_and_claim(text)', 'get_user_households()',
+    'switch_active_household(uuid)', 'leave_household()', 'revoke_invite(text)', 'set_member_role(uuid,text)', 'remove_member(uuid)',
+    'get_member_allowance_status(uuid,uuid,text,uuid)', 'set_member_allowance(uuid,uuid,numeric,text,uuid)',
+    'get_spouse_reimbursement_balance(uuid,uuid,uuid)', 'record_spouse_reimbursement(uuid,uuid,numeric,text,text,uuid)',
+    'get_household_members(uuid,uuid)', 'promote_member_to_admin(uuid,uuid,uuid)', 'revoke_admin(uuid,uuid,uuid)',
+    'transfer_primary_admin(uuid,uuid,uuid)', 'reconcile_account_balance(uuid,numeric)', 'get_saudi_cycle_for_timestamp(timestamptz,integer)'
+  ]) f where to_regprocedure('public.' || f) is null) as expected_functions_missing,
+ (select string_agg(tgname, ',' order by tgname) from pg_trigger where tgrelid = 'public.transactions'::regclass and not tgisinternal) as transactions_triggers,
+ (select count(*) from pg_trigger where tgrelid = 'public.household_memberships'::regclass and tgname in ('trg_protect_primary_admin', 'trg_maintain_primary_admin')) as membership_role_triggers,
+ (select has_function_privilege('anon', 'public.reallocate_budget(uuid,uuid,numeric)', 'EXECUTE')) as anon_can_reallocate,
+ (select has_table_privilege('authenticated', 'public.income_records', 'INSERT')) as auth_can_insert_income,
+ (select has_column_privilege('authenticated', 'public.households', 'owner_user_id', 'UPDATE')) as auth_can_update_owner
+;

--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/review/audit/live_db_preflight_round2.md
@@ -0,0 +1,266 @@
+# Live database pre-flight, round 2: `20261020700000` and `20261020800000`
+
+Date: 2026-10-21 · Branch: `audit/claude-db-preflight-round2` (from `893bd67`) · Method: same as [`live_db_preflight.md`](live_db_preflight.md) §2 and §6 · Checks: [`live_db_preflight_round2_checks.sql`](live_db_preflight_round2_checks.sql) · Rollback: [`../rollback/20261020_round2_rollback_snapshot.sql`](../rollback/20261020_round2_rollback_snapshot.sql)
+
+> Superseded for the apply plan by [round 3](live_db_preflight_round3.md) (2026-10-21), which covers all four pending files (`20261020700000`, `750000`, `800000`, `900000`) on a fresh live inventory. This round's findings for 700000 and 800000 still hold.
+
+This pre-flight covers the two migrations that are not yet applied anywhere:
+
+- `supabase/migrations/20261020700000_fable_db_hardening.sql` (FABLE-DB-02, -04 to -09);
+- `supabase/migrations/20261020800000_household_roles_and_nafaqah_integrity.sql` (FABLE-LOGIC-01, -02, -04 to -06, FABLE-DB-01, -03).
+
+Live already has every migration up to `20261020600000`. It was only read, through the Management API with `read_only=true` (connected as `supabase_read_only_user`). Only catalog queries and aggregate counts were sent. No row was copied and nothing was written.
+
+## 1. Verdict
+
+**Safe to apply: yes.** Apply the two files in order (700000, then 800000), each as one SQL editor run, using the plan in §6.
+
+Why:
+
+- **Both files applied cleanly to a faithful replica of live.**
+  - The replica was generated from live's own catalog and is owned by a non-superuser `BYPASSRLS` role, as live's `postgres` is. Its catalog is identical to live apart from platform-only objects (§3).
+  - It held synthetic data matching **63 of 64** of live's aggregate checks, including the per-household shape (§4). The one mismatch is a PG17-only privilege check, which reads NULL on the local PG16 server.
+  - Each file's own guard and post-check blocks passed.
+- **The full DB suite passes, 24/24, in every setup:**
+  - on the migrated live-shaped replica;
+  - on an empty replica migrated as the owner role;
+  - on an empty replica migrated with `run_tests.py --apply-from`;
+  - after rollback and re-apply;
+  - on a full repo rebuild.
+- **No existing row changes.** A fingerprint of all 21 tables (`public`, `auth.users`, `storage.objects`) is identical before and after the pair, apart from the two new columns. Budget totals stay at spent 9112.42 / allocated 20844.52, and the account balance total stays at 360.00.
+- **Nothing re-keys at apply time.** The payday trigger fires only when `payday_day` changes, and neither file updates `payday_day`. All 14 transactions and 24 budgets keep cycle `2026-10`. Live's budget `spent_amount` already equals the recompute rule for all 24 budgets (drift 0), so a later payday change moves no money beyond the designed re-keying.
+- **The provider backfill is unambiguous:**
+  - 3 households get their primary admin as Nafaqah provider. Each has exactly one admin, who is the primary admin and has `financial_role = provider`.
+  - The memberless household gets NULL, because it has no primary admin.
+  - No household has a spouse member or a spouse owner, so the provider is inert everywhere for now.
+- **After the pair, the replica catalog equals the repo HEAD rebuild**, apart from the same pre-existing drift items (§5).
+- **There is a tested rollback.** On the migrated replica it returns the catalog exactly to live's current state, including function bodies, grants and the one function comment. Re-applying afterwards is clean and passes 24/24. It also works on a dirty database (after the test suite ran) and refuses to run twice.
+
+**Migration fixes needed: none.** Neither file was changed.
+
+Known consequences, all intended by the review:
+
+- After 800000, members who are not admins can no longer read invite codes. On live this affects the 1 member (`family_member`). The released app never reads `household_invites` (checked in `flutter_app/lib`).
+- The 1 used invite is now deleted with its claimer (`ON DELETE CASCADE`) instead of blocking account deletion. Its `created_by` is already NULL.
+- Clients lose TRUNCATE/TRIGGER/REFERENCES on every public table, anon loses INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, and on PG17 anon and authenticated also lose MAINTAIN. That is 15 tables (16 for MAINTAIN). PostgREST never uses these privileges.
+- Admins can update only `name`, `payday_day`, `monthly_income` and `rollover_rule` on `households`. That is all the app writes.
+
+## 2. Method (what was reused, what changed)
+
+Tooling from the round-1 scratch pre-flight was reused: inventory, replica generator, owner-role apply, catalog diff and rollback generator. Changes in this round:
+
+| Item | Change | Why |
+|---|---|---|
+| Live-shaped fixture | Rebuilt for live's current counts. 4 households: H1 payday 27 with 2 members (admin/provider + member/family_member), 8 transactions, 6 budgets, 1 personal account (360.00), and 1 used `family_member` invite with `created_by` NULL. H2 payday 27, 1 admin, 5 transactions, 11 budgets. H3 **payday 1**, 1 admin, 1 transaction, 6 budgets. H4 payday 27, memberless, owner NULL, 1 budget. Totals: 14 creator-less transactions (`chat` 11 / `receipt_scan` 3) whose total equals live's spent total, 24 budgets (17 with sub-allocations, 20 active), 24 backup rows, 11 system categories, 27 sub-categories, 39 receipt objects. | Live's data changed since round 1: payday 1 household, relabelled sources, provider/primary admin. |
+| Rollback generator | (1) After `REVOKE ALL` on a table, it re-grants every target **column** grant on that table. Before, column grants present both before and after, such as `accounts` ×7 and `users` ×2, were silently dropped. (2) It restores **MAINTAIN** through a `server_version_num >= 170000` block, since live is PG17. | 700000 changes table privileges on 15 tables that also carry column grants. |
+| Row fingerprint | New `md5` of every row per table, ignoring only the two new columns. | Proves the pair changes no existing row. |
+| Part A / part B | New checks for the provider backfill, membership financial roles, invite FKs and policies, column grants, PG17 MAINTAIN, and budget spent drift. | §4 and §7. |
+
+Servers: PostgreSQL 16.15 locally, PostgreSQL 17.6 on live.
+
+## 3. Drift since the last batch (live vs repo rebuilt up to `20261020600000`)
+
+Live now matches the repository much more closely than in round 1. The diff, keyed by table, column, constraint, policy, function signature, trigger, grant and bucket, shows only these items:
+
+| # (round 1) | Drift | Status | Effect on the pair |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| D1–D5, D7 | `reallocate_budget`, invite RLS, recursive policy, category policies, source CHECK, `rollover_rule` | **Resolved** by the round-1 batch | — |
+| D6 | `transactions_spent_by_check` exists only in the repo | Unchanged (deliberate) | None. All 14 rows are `me` 9 / `both` 4 / `partner` 1. |
+| D8 | `budgets_spent_backup_20261019` exists only on live: 24 rows, RLS on, no policies, owner `postgres`, full anon/authenticated privileges | Unchanged | 700000 §6 also revokes TRUNCATE, TRIGGER, REFERENCES, anon DML and MAINTAIN on it. Afterwards anon has SELECT and authenticated has SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, and RLS shows no rows. Its DB-08 guard covers it. |
+| D9 | `rls_auto_enable()` and the `ensure_rls` event trigger exist only on live (EXECUTE: postgres, service_role) | Unchanged | Not touched. |
+| D10 | `unaccent` lives in `public` (4 functions owned by `supabase_admin`) | Unchanged | Not touched. 700000 §6 loops over tables only. |
+| D11 | Comment-only body differences in `consume_quota` and `get_saudi_cycle_for_timestamp` | Unchanged | Neither function is touched. |
+| D12 | 5 column comments missing on live | Unchanged | Cosmetic. |
+| — | Function comments on `household_primary_admin_id` and `nafaqah_is_spouse_member` | Present on live and in the repo; the replica generator does not emit function comments | Not touched by the pair. The rollback restores the one comment the pair changes (`nafaqah_husband_id`). |
+| — | `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`: 28 rows; the 16 `20261020*` files are recorded with their 14-digit prefix as `version` | **New (good)** | Record the pair the same way (§6.3). |
+
+Everything else is identical, apart from the platform-only items listed in round 1 §3.4: realtime messages publication, `pg_stat_statements`, `supabase_vault`, schema ACL grantors and storage triggers. That covers the 19 tables, 198 columns, 85 constraints, 82 indexes, 39 policies (public + storage), 62 functions (bodies, `SECURITY DEFINER`, `search_path`, EXECUTE), 19 triggers, 48 table grants and 19 column grants (`accounts` ×7, `households` ×10, `users` ×2), the bucket and the realtime tables. All 19 public tables are owned by `postgres`, and all table, column and function privileges were granted by `postgres`. `REVOKE` run as `postgres` therefore removes them, and the guards cannot trip on a grant made by another grantor. The function lists the guards need are all present.

+## 6. Apply plan
+
+### 6.1 Before you start
+
+1. **Take a backup**, as in round 1 (Dashboard → Database → Backups, or `pg_dump` of `public` with data).
+2. **Run part A** of [`live_db_preflight_round2_checks.sql`](live_db_preflight_round2_checks.sql) and compare it with §4. Write down `budgets_spent_total`, `budgets_allocated_total` and `accounts_balance_total`. If `hh_owner_is_spouse`, `users_multi_membership`, `memberships_user_fr_null` or `users_fr_unknown` is no longer 0, stop and re-read §4.
+3. **Pick a quiet moment.** Both files take ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks on `households`, `household_memberships`, `household_invites` and `users` for well under a second (4 rows each).
+
+### 6.2 Order and method
+
+**SQL editor, one file per run, in this order. Live runs each one as `postgres`.**
+
+| # | File | What it does on live | Expected output |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 1 | `20261020700000_fable_db_hardening.sql` | Re-creates the invite FKs (`created_by` SET NULL, `used_by` CASCADE). `reallocate_budget` fails closed. Revokes client EXECUTE on `nafaqah_current_cycle_key` and `generate_secure_invite_code`. Sets the client UPDATE columns on `households` (4) and the INSERT/UPDATE columns on `household_dependents` and `users`. Revokes TRUNCATE/TRIGGER/REFERENCES, anon DML and MAINTAIN (PG17) on all 19 public tables. Ends with a guard that aborts if anything differs. | "Success. No rows returned" |
+| 2 | `20261020800000_household_roles_and_nafaqah_integrity.sql` | Adds `household_memberships.financial_role` (backfilled: provider 3, family_member 1) and `households.nafaqah_provider_user_id` (backfilled: 3 = primary admin, 1 NULL). Adds the role, provider, invite-claim and ledger-guard triggers and functions. Makes invites admin-only. Budget triggers ignore `wife_personal`. Adds the payday re-key trigger, which fires only on a later change. Ends with post-checks. | Success. In the notices: "guard: 0 user(s) belong to more than one household …", "guard: 0 classified (Nafaqah) transaction(s)", "post-check: 3 household(s) have a Nafaqah provider" |
+
+Each file is wrapped in `BEGIN … COMMIT`, and its guard blocks abort the transaction on any mismatch. A failure therefore leaves nothing half-applied. Stop and keep the error text. File 2's §0 guard checks only the round-1 prerequisites, so it would also apply without file 1. Keep the order anyway: file 2's grant comments assume file 1's households column list, and the replica and suite results cover this order only.
+
+Alternative: `psql "<session-pooler connection string as postgres>" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f <file>`, run on each file in the same order. Each file has its own transaction, so do not add `--single-transaction`.
+
+Then run part B (§7), deploy ai_service, then release the app build (MASTER §6.2).
+
+### 6.3 Recording the history
+
+Live records the 16 `20261020*` files with `version` = the 14-digit prefix. After both files succeed, the owner records the pair the same way (this is a write):
+
+```sql
+INSERT INTO supabase_migrations.schema_migrations (version, name)
+SELECT v, n FROM (VALUES
+  ('20261020700000', 'fable_db_hardening'),
+  ('20261020800000', 'household_roles_and_nafaqah_integrity')
+) AS m(v, n)
+WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM supabase_migrations.schema_migrations s WHERE s.version = m.v);
+```
+
+The round-1 CLI warning still holds. Do not run `supabase db push`, `db reset --linked` or `migration up` against live until the DB-15 re-baseline is done (round 1 §5.3).

+## 8. Rollback notes
+
+[`../rollback/20261020_round2_rollback_snapshot.sql`](../rollback/20261020_round2_rollback_snapshot.sql) undoes **both** files in one transaction. It was generated from live's catalog before the pair, and it refuses to run unless 800000 is applied. Section by section, it:
+
+1. drops the 7 new triggers;
+2. drops `invites_select_admin`;
+3. drops the new or changed constraints and the provider index;
+4. drops the two new columns;
+5. drops the 12 new functions and restores 14 function bodies and the EXECUTE grants of 16 functions;
+6. re-adds the invite FKs with NO ACTION;
+7. re-creates `invites_select_household`;
+8. restores the table and column privileges of 15 tables, plus MAINTAIN on PG17;
+9. restores the `nafaqah_husband_id` comment.
+
+Verification on the replica:
+
+- live-shaped replica → pair → rollback: catalog identical to live (and to the pre-pair replica), function comments identical, and the row fingerprint of all 21 tables identical to the pre-pair data;
+- then pair re-applied: catalog and part B identical to the first apply, and the suite passes 24/24;
+- rollback on the replica after the full suite (extra memberships, providers and invites): it applies, and the catalog again equals the pre-pair state;
+- a second run is refused by its guard.
+
+The MAINTAIN block cannot be exercised locally (PG16). It uses `EXECUTE 'GRANT MAINTAIN …'` behind a version check, and the same privilege checks were confirmed on live's PG17 with a read-only query (16 tables have client MAINTAIN today).
+
+Data impact of a rollback:
+
+- per-membership financial roles and chosen Nafaqah providers are lost, because the columns are dropped;
+- `users.financial_role` keeps its last cached value;
+- invites deleted by the new cascade are not recreated;
+- cycle keys re-keyed by a payday change made while the pair was live stay re-keyed.
+
+To undo only file 2, use the commented rollback at the end of `20261020800000`. Run its function re-definitions before the column drops, as that comment says. To undo only file 1, take sections 3, 5 (only `reallocate_budget`, `nafaqah_current_cycle_key` and `generate_secure_invite_code`) and 8 of the snapshot.
+
+## 9. PostgreSQL 17 notes
+
+- **MAINTAIN** (PG17-only) is the one version-dependent part:
+  - 700000 §6 revokes it from PUBLIC, anon and authenticated only when `server_version_num >= 170000`;
+  - the rollback re-grants it the same way;
+  - part B checks it (`tables_client_maintain_pg17`, expected 0 on live).
+
+  The 700000 guard does not check MAINTAIN. Part B does.
+- Nothing else in either file depends on the version: FK actions, column privileges, `has_*_privilege`, triggers, `pg_get_constraintdef` output and the `information_schema` reads all behave the same in PG16 and PG17. The diff tool ignores MAINTAIN in table-grant comparisons.
+- Follow-up (not blocking): live's default privileges for `postgres` and `supabase_admin` in `public` still grant `arwdDxtm` on new tables to anon and authenticated. A future migration that creates a table must revoke those privileges explicitly. The catalog-wide check in test 23 (FABLE-DB-08) will flag it otherwise.
+
+## 10. Artefacts
+
+- [`live_db_preflight_round2_checks.sql`](live_db_preflight_round2_checks.sql): part A (before) and part B (after). Read-only; validated on live (part A) and on the migrated replica (both parts).
+- [`../rollback/20261020_round2_rollback_snapshot.sql`](../rollback/20261020_round2_rollback_snapshot.sql): the tested rollback for both files.
+- Scratch tooling (not committed): replica generator and inventory as in round 1, plus the round-2 fixture, the row fingerprint and the patched rollback generator.

+# Live database pre-flight, round 3: the four pending files
+
+Date: 2026-10-21 · Branch: from `audit/claude-comprehensive-review` at `7f97e7f` · Method: same as [`live_db_preflight_round2.md`](live_db_preflight_round2.md) §2 · Checks: [`live_db_preflight_round3_checks.sql`](live_db_preflight_round3_checks.sql) · Rollbacks: [`../rollback/20261020_round3_rollback_snapshot.sql`](../rollback/20261020_round3_rollback_snapshot.sql), then [`../rollback/20261020_round2_rollback_snapshot.sql`](../rollback/20261020_round2_rollback_snapshot.sql)
+
+This pre-flight covers the four migrations that are in the repository but not yet on live. They must be applied in this order:
+
+1. `supabase/migrations/20261020700000_fable_db_hardening.sql` (FABLE-DB-02, -04 to -09);
+2. `supabase/migrations/20261020750000_installment_pay_atomic.sql` (FABLE-API-10);
+3. `supabase/migrations/20261020800000_household_roles_and_nafaqah_integrity.sql` (FABLE-LOGIC-01, -02, -04 to -06, FABLE-DB-01, -03);
+4. `supabase/migrations/20261020900000_household_type_and_round2_fixes.sql` (owner decisions D1 to D3, FABLE2-DB-01, -02, -05, -07).
+
+Live already has every migration up to `20261020600000`. It was only read, through the Management API with `read_only=true`. Only catalog queries and aggregate counts were sent. No row was copied and nothing was written.
+
+## 1. Verdict
+
+**Safe to apply: yes.** Apply the four files in order (700000, 750000, 800000, 900000). Run each one in its own SQL editor run, following the plan in §6.
+
+Why:
+
+- **Live has not changed since round 2.** Its catalog is identical to the round-2 inventory; the only difference is two new daily realtime partitions, which belong to the platform. All 64 round-2 part-A values are identical, and the per-household shape is unchanged (§3, §4). The round-2 findings therefore still hold for 700000 and 800000.
+- **All four files applied cleanly to a faithful replica of current live.**
+  - The replica was regenerated from today's live inventory. It is owned by a non-superuser `BYPASSRLS` role, as live's `postgres` is. This time the replica also carries live's three function comments.
+  - Its catalog is identical to live apart from platform-only objects.
+  - Its synthetic data reproduces **80 of 81** part-A values, all 50 round-1 data checks, the value distributions and the per-household shape. The one mismatch is `tables_client_maintain_pg17`, which PostgreSQL 16 cannot report.
+  - Every guard and post-check block in the four files passed. The notices are listed in §6.2.
+- **The full DB suite passes, 26/26, in every setup:**
+  - the migrated live-shaped replica;
+  - an empty replica migrated as the owner role;
+  - an empty replica migrated with `run_tests.py --apply-from 20261020700000`;
+  - after the double rollback and a re-apply, on both a clean and a post-suite ("dirty") database;
+  - a full repo rebuild with `--rebuild`.
+- **No existing row changes.** A per-table `md5` fingerprint of all 21 tables (19 `public` tables, `auth.users`, `storage.objects`) is identical before and after the four files. Only the three new columns are excluded.
+  - Budget totals stay at spent 9112.42 / allocated 20844.52.
+  - The account balance total stays at 360.00.
+  - Transactions (14) and budgets (24) all stay on cycle `2026-10`.
+- **The household outcomes are as expected:**
+  - all 4 households end with `household_type = 'family'`. Live has no `peer`, so no household becomes `roommates`;
+  - the Nafaqah provider is the primary admin for the 3 households that have one, and NULL for the memberless household;
+  - membership financial roles are unchanged: `admin/provider` ×3 and `member/family_member` ×1, all of which fit `family`;
+  - live has **0 installment plans**, so the new `paid_installments` CHECK is added and validated straight away (`[validated]`).
+- **After the four files, the replica's catalog equals the repo HEAD rebuild.** The only differences are the same pre-existing drift items as in round 2 (D6, D8, D9, D10, D11, D12). Every object the four files create or change matches HEAD exactly: bodies, grants, triggers, constraints and comments.
+- **Both rollbacks are tested on the live replica and work in sequence:**
+  - the round-3 rollback returns the catalog exactly to "live + 700000/750000/800000";
+  - the round-2 rollback then returns it exactly to current live: catalog, function bodies, EXECUTE grants, the three function comments, the row fingerprint and all 81 part-A values;
+  - each rollback refuses to run out of order or twice;
+  - re-applying the four files afterwards reproduces the first apply exactly and passes 26/26.
+- **Re-running all four files in order is idempotent.** The catalog, all 89 part-B values and the row fingerprint are unchanged.
+
+**Migration fixes needed: none.** None of the four files was changed.
+
+Known consequences, all intended by the review:
+
+- Round 2's consequences apply unchanged (round 2 §1):
+  - members who are not admins can no longer read invite codes;
+  - the 1 used invite cascades with its claimer;
+  - clients lose TRUNCATE/TRIGGER/REFERENCES, anon loses DML, and on PG17 anon and authenticated also lose MAINTAIN;
+  - `households` gets a client UPDATE column list.
+- `create_household_and_claim(text)` is replaced by `create_household_and_claim(text, text DEFAULT 'family')`. The released app calls `{p_name}` only, and that call still resolves (tested). It returns the same JSON row, now with `household_type`.
+- Clients lose UPDATE of `installment_plans.paid_installments` and `status`. They keep UPDATE on the other 10 columns. The app never writes this table. The deployed ai_service writes it with the service role, which keeps full UPDATE.
+- `pay_installment_plan` (new in 750000, tightened in 900000) is EXECUTE for `service_role` only. The deployed ai_service (`origin/main`) does not call it yet; the HEAD ai_service does. Hence the deployment order: migrations, then ai_service, then the app.
+- `households.household_type` is not client-writable. It changes only through `set_household_type` (admins).
+
+## 2. Method (what was reused, what changed)
+
+The round-2 tooling was reused: inventory, replica generator, owner-role apply, catalog diff, row fingerprint and `cmpjson`. The fixture was also reused, because live's data shape is unchanged. Changes in this round:
+
+| Item | Change | Why |
+|---|---|---|
+| Live inventory | Taken again today (21 catalog queries, read-only) | Detect drift since round 2 |
+| Function comments | Added to the inventory, the catalog diff and the replica generator (`COMMENT ON FUNCTION`) | Round 2's replica lacked live's 3 function comments. 750000 adds a 4th, and the rollbacks must restore the comment set exactly. |
+| Part A | Round 2's 64 columns plus 17 new ones: expected household type, `is_settlement` / `nafaqah_spouse_id` rows, installment plans (count, range violations, status, grants), presence of `household_type` / `pay_installment_plan` / both `create_household_and_claim` signatures, function comment list, public function count, and **per-table row counts** (`table_rows`) | 750000 / 900000 inputs |
+| Part B | Round 2's 54 columns plus 35 new ones: type distribution, NOT NULL / default / CHECK, roles fitting the type, installment CHECK and column grants, new RPC privileges, provider trigger definition, comments, `table_rows`, migration history | 750000 / 900000 outputs |
+| Per-household shape | One aggregate line per household: payday, owner present, members, admins, role/financial-role pairs, transactions, cycle keys, budgets, accounts, invites, plans, income records. No ids or names. | Proves the fixture still mirrors live |
+| Apply | Four files, each as its own `psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1` run under `SET ROLE live_owner`, mirroring one SQL editor run per file | — |
+| Rollback round trip | Round-3 rollback, then round-2 rollback, each diffed against the matching replica state. Also tested on a database the suite had already run on. | The round-3 snapshot was generated from a repo rebuild, so it needed proving against live's real state |
+

+## 6. Apply plan
+
+### 6.1 Before you start
+
+1. **Take a backup**, as in rounds 1 and 2: Dashboard → Database → Backups, or a `pg_dump` of `public` with data.
+2. **Run part A** of [`live_db_preflight_round3_checks.sql`](live_db_preflight_round3_checks.sql) and compare it with §4.
+   - Write down `budgets_spent_total`, `budgets_allocated_total`, `accounts_balance_total` and `table_rows`.
+   - Stop and re-read §4 if any of these is no longer 0: `hh_owner_is_spouse`, `users_multi_membership`, `memberships_user_fr_null`, `users_fr_unknown`, `installment_plans_out_of_range` or `hh_with_peer_member`.
+   - Also stop if `expected_hh_roommates` is no longer 0. A peer member would make that household `roommates`, with provider NULL.
+3. **Pick a quiet moment.** The files take ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks on `households`, `household_memberships`, `household_invites`, `users` and `installment_plans` for well under a second each (4 rows or fewer, 0 plans).
+
+### 6.2 Order and method
+
+**SQL editor, one file per run, in this order. Live runs each one as `postgres`.**
+
+| # | File | What it does on live | Expected output |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| 1 | `20261020700000_fable_db_hardening.sql` | Re-creates the invite FKs (`created_by` SET NULL, `used_by` CASCADE). `reallocate_budget` fails closed. Revokes client EXECUTE on `nafaqah_current_cycle_key` and `generate_secure_invite_code`. Sets the client column lists on `households`, `household_dependents` and `users`. Revokes TRUNCATE/TRIGGER/REFERENCES, anon DML and MAINTAIN (PG17) on all 19 public tables. Ends with a guard that aborts on any mismatch. | "Success. No rows returned"; no notices |
+| 2 | `20261020750000_installment_pay_atomic.sql` | Adds `pay_installment_plan(uuid, uuid, uuid)`: an atomic conditional increment, `SECURITY DEFINER`, EXECUTE for `service_role` only, with a comment. Changes no table and no data. | "Success. No rows returned"; no notices |
+| 3 | `20261020800000_household_roles_and_nafaqah_integrity.sql` | Adds `household_memberships.financial_role` (backfilled: provider 3, family_member 1) and `households.nafaqah_provider_user_id` (backfilled: 3 = primary admin, 1 NULL). Adds the role, provider, invite-claim, ledger-guard and payday re-key triggers and functions. Makes invites admin-only. Budget triggers ignore `wife_personal`. | Notices: `guard: 0 user(s) belong to more than one household (their memberships are backfilled from users.financial_role)`, `guard: 0 classified (Nafaqah) transaction(s)`, `post-check: 3 household(s) have a Nafaqah provider`, plus eight harmless `trigger/policy "…" does not exist, skipping` from `DROP … IF EXISTS` |
+| 4 | `20261020900000_household_type_and_round2_fixes.sql` | Adds `households.household_type text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'family'` with a CHECK (`family`/`roommates`). The backfill makes 0 households `roommates`, so all 4 are `family`. Financial roles follow the type. The provider is defaulted only at creation. Classification rights go to the wife, the provider or an admin (D2). A wife's ledger is removed when her membership ends (D3). Budget triggers skip settlement rows. Replaces `create_household_and_claim(text)` with `(text, text DEFAULT 'family')`. Adds `set_household_type` and `set_member_financial_role`. Adds the validated `installment_plans_paid_installments_range` CHECK. Clients lose UPDATE of `paid_installments`/`status`. `pay_installment_plan` counts only ACTIVE plans. The orphaned-ledger cleanup touches 0 rows. Ends with post-checks. | Notices: `guard: 0 installment plan(s) outside 0..installment_count (CHECK stays NOT VALID if > 0)`, `guard: 0 classified row(s) of a wife who is no longer a member (declassified by D3)`, `post-check: 0 roommates household(s), 4 family household(s)`, plus one harmless `trigger "trg_remove_nafaqah_ledger_on_membership_end" … does not exist, skipping` |
+
+Each file is wrapped in `BEGIN … COMMIT`, and its guard and post-check blocks raise on any mismatch. A failure therefore leaves nothing half-applied: stop and keep the error text.
+
+- The guards of 800000 and 900000 check their prerequisites: 900000 needs 750000's `pay_installment_plan` and 800000's columns and functions.
+- **Keep the order.** The replica and suite results cover this order only.
+- If the notice text differs from the table (for example "1 roommates household(s)"), the data changed after part A. The file has still been applied consistently, but compare part B with the new values.
+- Whatever the SQL editor shows, part B is the authoritative check.
+
+**Do not re-run a single earlier file after file 4.** Re-running file 2 or 3 alone (tested on the replica) brings back the 750000/800000 versions:
+
+- `create_household_and_claim(text)` returns as a second overload, which makes `{p_name}` ambiguous for PostgREST;
+- `pay_installment_plan` loses its ACTIVE-only rule;
+- the provider trigger loses `household_type`.
+
+If that happens, re-run file 4. That restores the exact post-apply catalog (tested). Re-running all four files in order is idempotent.
+
+Alternative: `psql "<session-pooler connection string as postgres>" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f <file>`, run on each file in the same order. Each file has its own transaction, so do not add `--single-transaction`.
+
+Then run part B (§7), deploy ai_service (its HEAD build calls `pay_installment_plan`), then release the app build. This is the README deployment order. The deployed backend and app (`origin/main`) keep working between steps:
+
+- they call `create_household_and_claim` with `{p_name}` only;
+- they write `installment_plans` with the service role;
+- the HEAD app falls back to `{p_name}` against an older database.
+
+Supabase reloads the PostgREST schema cache after DDL. If an RPC call returns PGRST202 right after file 4, wait a few seconds. Do not add another overload.
+
+### 6.3 Recording the history
+
+Live records the `20261020*` files with `version` = the 14-digit prefix and `name` = the rest of the file name. `statements`, `created_by`, `idempotency_key` and `rollback` are nullable, and `postgres` may INSERT. After **all four files and part B** succeed, the owner records them in one statement. This is a write, and it is safe to run twice:
+
+```sql
+INSERT INTO supabase_migrations.schema_migrations (version, name)
+SELECT v, n FROM (VALUES
+  ('20261020700000', 'fable_db_hardening'),
+  ('20261020750000', 'installment_pay_atomic'),
+  ('20261020800000', 'household_roles_and_nafaqah_integrity'),
+  ('20261020900000', 'household_type_and_round2_fixes')
+) AS m(v, n)
+WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM supabase_migrations.schema_migrations s WHERE s.version = m.v);
+```
+
+On the replica, the first run printed `INSERT 0 4` and the second `INSERT 0 0`. Afterwards part B shows `migrations_recorded` 32, `last_migration` `20261020900000` and `round3_versions_recorded` 4.
+
+The round-1 CLI warning still holds. Do not run `supabase db push`, `db reset --linked` or `migration up` against live until the DB-15 re-baseline is done (round 1 §5.3).
+

+## 8. Rollback notes
+
+Undo in this order: first [`../rollback/20261020_round3_rollback_snapshot.sql`](../rollback/20261020_round3_rollback_snapshot.sql) (undoes 900000), then, if needed, [`../rollback/20261020_round2_rollback_snapshot.sql`](../rollback/20261020_round2_rollback_snapshot.sql) (undoes 800000, 750000 and 700000 together). Run each one in the SQL editor as `postgres`. Each is one transaction.
+
+- **Guards (tested):**
+  - the round-2 script refuses while `household_type` exists ("run 20261020_round3_rollback_snapshot.sql first");
+  - the round-3 script refuses when 900000 is not applied;
+  - the round-2 script refuses when 800000 is not applied.
+
+  So neither script can run twice or out of order.
+- **The round-3 rollback**, on the migrated live-shaped replica:
+  - the catalog is identical to the replica with only 700000/750000/800000 applied: function definitions, EXECUTE, function comments (4) and the `installment_plans` grants (back to table-level UPDATE for authenticated);
+  - `create_household_and_claim(text)` is back;
+  - `household_type`, both new CHECKs and the new trigger are gone.
+- **Then the round-2 rollback:**
+  - the catalog is identical to the pre-apply replica, which equals live. That covers function definitions, EXECUTE grants, the 3 live function comments and the table and column privileges;
+  - `pay_installment_plan` is gone;
+  - the row fingerprint of all 21 tables is identical to the pre-apply data;
+  - all 81 part-A values equal the pre-apply values.
+- **Re-apply** of the four files afterwards gives the same notices, a catalog identical to the first apply, and all 89 part-B values identical. The suite passes 26/26.
+- **Dirty database:** the same round trip on a copy on which the full suite had already run (8 households, extra memberships, plans and invites) gives the same catalog results. The re-apply passes 26/26.
+
+The MAINTAIN block of the round-2 rollback still cannot be exercised locally (PG16); see round 2 §8. The round-3 rollback does not touch MAINTAIN: it changes only authenticated's UPDATE on `installment_plans`.
+
+Data impact of a rollback, in addition to round 2 §8:
+
+- the household types are lost, because the column is dropped;
+- roles changed by `set_household_type` or `set_member_financial_role` stay as they are (valid 800000 values);
+- D3 removals (a wife's ledger when her membership ends) are permanent;
+- a provider left NULL after owner succession stays NULL;
+- installment payments recorded through `pay_installment_plan` stay recorded.
+
+## 9. PostgreSQL 17 notes
+
+- MAINTAIN behaves as described in round 2 §9:
+  - 700000 revokes it from clients on PG17;
+  - part B checks `tables_client_maintain_pg17` (expected 0);
+  - the round-2 rollback re-grants it behind a version check.
+- 750000 and 900000 contain nothing version-dependent. The calls they use behave the same on PG16 and PG17: `REVOKE UPDATE ON … FROM …` plus a column-level `GRANT UPDATE (…)`, `ADD CONSTRAINT … NOT VALID` / `VALIDATE CONSTRAINT`, `DROP FUNCTION IF EXISTS`, `pg_get_triggerdef` and `has_*_privilege`.
+- Live's default privileges for `postgres` in `public` grant EXECUTE on new functions to anon, authenticated and service_role, and the replica emulates that. Every function that 900000 creates is explicitly revoked from PUBLIC and anon, and from authenticated where it is internal. Part B checks the result.
+
+## 10. Artefacts
+
+- [`live_db_preflight_round3_checks.sql`](live_db_preflight_round3_checks.sql): part A (before) and part B (after). Read-only, SELECT only. Part A was validated on live today and on the replica; part B on the migrated replica, before and after the history INSERT.
+- [`../rollback/20261020_round3_rollback_snapshot.sql`](../rollback/20261020_round3_rollback_snapshot.sql) and [`../rollback/20261020_round2_rollback_snapshot.sql`](../rollback/20261020_round2_rollback_snapshot.sql): the tested rollbacks, unchanged.
+- Scratch tooling (not committed): today's live inventory (with function comments), the replica generator, `build_shaped.sh` / `apply4.sh` / `roundtrip.sh`, the per-household shape query, the row fingerprint and the functional smoke.

+## Round 3b: 20261021000000
+
+Date: 2026-10-21 · Branch: `audit/claude-taxonomy-bnpl` from `33399b5` · File: [`supabase/migrations/20261021000000_saudi_taxonomy_and_bnpl_schedule.sql`](../../../supabase/migrations/20261021000000_saudi_taxonomy_and_bnpl_schedule.sql) · Proof test: [`supabase/tests/27_taxonomy_and_bnpl.sql`](../../../supabase/tests/27_taxonomy_and_bnpl.sql) · Rollback: [`../rollback/20261021_taxonomy_bnpl_rollback.sql`](../rollback/20261021_taxonomy_bnpl_rollback.sql)
+
+A fifth pending file, from the product review (R4 Saudi taxonomy, R10 BNPL schedule). **Apply it after the four files above, as file 5**, in its own SQL editor run as `postgres`. Its guard aborts (and changes nothing) when 900000 is not applied yet.
+
+### 3b.1 What it does on live
+
+- **Taxonomy.** It inserts 8 system categories into `cost_control_codes` (`household_id` NULL, `is_system` true, `is_flexible` false): `OPEX-HOUSING`, `OPEX-EDUCATION`, `OPEX-DOMESTIC-HELP`, `OPEX-FAMILY-SUPPORT`, `OPEX-CHARITY`, `OPEX-TRANSPORT`, `OPEX-INSURANCE` and `OPEX-REMITTANCE`. It also inserts 23 system sub-categories under them into `cost_control_sub_categories`.
+  - No existing row is updated or deleted. `OPEX-UTILITIES/housing_rent` stays as it is, because transactions and sub-allocations reference it and sub-categories have no lifecycle column. A second `housing_rent`, with the same names, is added under `OPEX-HOUSING`.
+  - No `household_category_settings` row and no budget row is written. For the 4 households, the new categories appear in the category library as inactive and are budgeted only once an admin activates them or adds a budget.
+  - None of the new top-level keywords overlaps a keyword of the ten seeded codes, so no existing merchant changes category. Test 27 proves this.
+- **BNPL schedule.** `installment_plans` gains:
+  - `frequency text NOT NULL DEFAULT 'monthly'`, with the CHECK `installment_plans_frequency_check` (`monthly`/`biweekly`);
+  - `next_due_at date` (nullable);
+  - the index `idx_installment_plans_next_due` (`WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'`);
+  - the IMMUTABLE helper `installment_next_due_at(date, text, integer, integer, text)`, with a comment. Its EXECUTE goes to `authenticated` and `service_role`, and is revoked from PUBLIC and anon;
+  - the trigger function `installment_plans_schedule()`, which no client may execute, and the trigger `trg_installment_plans_schedule` (BEFORE INSERT / UPDATE of the schedule columns). It keeps `next_due_at` derived, so a client INSERT cannot forge it.
+
+  `pay_installment_plan` is re-created with the same signature, grants (`service_role` only), comment and ACTIVE-only rule, and it now advances `next_due_at`. The client UPDATE column list of 900000 is unchanged: `frequency` and `next_due_at` are not client-writable. Live has 0 plans, so the backfill touches no row.
+- **Locks:** a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE on `installment_plans` for the ALTER. It is metadata only, because the default is a constant. ROW EXCLUSIVE on the two category tables.
+
+### 3b.2 Read-only pre-check (run before file 5)
+
+```sql
+SELECT
+  (SELECT count(*) FROM public.cost_control_codes
+    WHERE household_id IS NOT NULL
+      AND code IN ('OPEX-HOUSING','OPEX-EDUCATION','OPEX-DOMESTIC-HELP','OPEX-FAMILY-SUPPORT',
+                   'OPEX-CHARITY','OPEX-TRANSPORT','OPEX-INSURANCE','OPEX-REMITTANCE')) AS household_code_collisions,
+  (SELECT count(*) FROM public.cost_control_sub_categories
+    WHERE parent_code IN ('OPEX-HOUSING','OPEX-EDUCATION','OPEX-DOMESTIC-HELP','OPEX-FAMILY-SUPPORT',
+                          'OPEX-CHARITY','OPEX-TRANSPORT','OPEX-INSURANCE','OPEX-REMITTANCE')) AS subs_under_new_parents,
+  (SELECT count(*) FROM public.cost_control_codes) AS codes,
+  (SELECT count(*) FROM public.cost_control_sub_categories) AS sub_categories,
+  (SELECT count(*) FROM public.installment_plans) AS installment_plans;
+```
+
+Expected values:
+
+- `household_code_collisions` = 0 and `subs_under_new_parents` = 0. Otherwise the guard aborts: rename that household's code, or remove those sub-categories, first.
+- `codes` = 11, `sub_categories` = 27 and `installment_plans` = 0 (part A, §4).
+
+Live has one code and four sub-categories more than the repo seed. Their content was not read, so this query is what tells whether one of them collides.

+### 3b.5 Deployment and compatibility

+# Product & engineering review (Fable) — 2026-10-21
+
+Independent, report-only review of how the product works (not a bug hunt), branch `audit/claude-comprehensive-review` @ `10a96cf`.
+
+## ملخص لصاحب المشروع (١٠ سطور)
+
+1. البرنامج صار آمن ومتين بعد التدقيقات، بس من ناحية "المنتج" هو حالياً أثقل وأعقد من اللي يحتاجه بيت سعودي عادي: لوحة رئيسية فيها ١٠ كروت، و٥ طرق لتسجيل مصروف، وإعدادات طويلة فيها خيارات ما لها أثر.
+2. السؤال الأساسي "كم باقي لي لحد الراتب؟" الجواب موجود بس مبني على "المخصصات" اللي المستخدم لازم يعبّيها بند بند بنفسه أول ما يسجّل؛ المستخدم الجديد يشوف أصفار. لازم معالج بداية: راتبك كم → نقترح لك المظاريف → أول مصروف.
+3. أهم شي ناقص: **التنبيهات**. ما في ولا تنبيه (لا يوم الراتب، لا فاتورة مستحقة، لا قسط تابي/تمارا) رغم إن المكتبة موجودة بالتطبيق. هذا أكبر سبب إن الناس ينسون التطبيق.
+4. **الأقساط**: تابي وتمارا يسحبون كل أسبوعين (٤ دفعات)، والتطبيق يحسبها شهرية — لازم تتصلح لأنها أكثر حالة واقعية.
+5. **التصنيفات** ناقصة أشياء سعودية أساسية: الإيجار كبند رئيسي (حالياً تحت "الخدمات")، المدارس، الخادمة/السائق، مساعدة الأهل والصدقة/الزكاة، التحويلات للخارج، تأمين وقسط السيارة، وادخار لأهداف (إيجار سنوي، عيد، حج/عمرة).
+6. **الذكاء الاصطناعي**: التكلفة شبه صفر (أقل من ريال بالشهر لكل بيت)، بس كل مصروف بالشات أو الفاتورة يروح للنموذج **مرتين** (مرة للمعاينة ومرة للحفظ)، فالمستخدم ينتظر ضعف الوقت بلا فايدة. سهلة تنصلح.
+7. **النفقة**: المنطق سليم شرعياً ومحمي بقاعدة البيانات، بس تجربة الزوجة الموظفة محتاجة تلطيف (لو ما عندها "مصروف" محدد يظهر لها إنها "تجاوزت"). مصروف الأطفال يُخزَّن بس ما يُتابع.
+8. **التشغيل**: ما في نسخ احتياطي ولا مراقبة أعطال؛ مطلوب فوراً: خطة Supabase Pro (نسخ يومي) أو نسخة أسبوعية تلقائية، وخدمة مراقبة أخطاء بسيطة، وتوحيد الهجرات (٤٨ ملف ينسخ باليد).
+9. **وقّف**: مسودة الفاتورة "بدون إنترنت" اللي تطلّع دايماً "العثيم ٨٥ ريال" (كود تجريبي)، صفحات التسويق الثلاث المكررة، الأرقام التسويقية غير الحقيقية ("دقة ٩٩.٤٪")، وكروت مقارنة الأسعار قبل ما يكون فيه بيانات.
+10. الخلاصة: البرنامج جاهز تقنياً، والمرحلة الجاية لازم تكون **تبسيط + تنبيهات + تصنيفات سعودية + معالج بداية** مش مزايا جديدة.
+
+---
+
+# Budget Tracker — Product & Engineering Review (how the product works, not a bug hunt)
+
+Scope: `/home/user/budget-tracker` @ `10a96cf`, branch `audit/claude-comprehensive-review`. Read: `docs/PROJECT_DETAILS.md`, `README.md`, `.agents/rules/*`, `docs/review/audit/MASTER_AUDIT_REPORT.md`, `fable_review.md`, then the code behind each feature (dashboard, chat, scanner, manual entry, budgets/cycles, Nafaqah, settlement, installments, recurring bills, settings, API, migrations, web landing). Report-only; nothing modified, no live service contacted.
+
+Legend per recommendation: **Problem** (evidence) → **Change** → **Impact** → **Effort** S/M/L → **Risk**.
+
+---
+
+## 1. Core loop & value
+
+### 1.1 Verdict on the promise ("how much is left until payday / where is it going / who owes whom")
+
+- **"How much is left until payday"** — answered by `BudgetHeroCard` (`/home/user/budget-tracker/flutter_app/lib/widgets/dashboard/budget_hero_card.dart`, lines 22–57): remaining = Σ allocated − Σ spent across *budget rows*, daily allowance, days to payday. It is correct only once the household has typed allocations for every category. A fresh household sees "No allocations for {cycle}" (`dashboard_screen.dart` ~line 953) and must go to the Budgets tab and add categories one by one. The salary the user records (`income_records`, `households.monthly_income`) is **not** what drives "left until payday"; allocations are. For a Saudi family the natural model is: salary in on the 27th → fixed commitments (rent/installments/bills) → what's left for daily life. The app has every ingredient (income records, recurring reserves, installments) but does not compose them into one number.
+- **"Where is it going"** — good: category cards, sub-allocations, feed with filters, ZATCA line items, PDF statement. Weak points: taxonomy (see 1.3) and the silent "flexible pool" raiding (see 2.2).
+- **"Who owes whom"** — good and now sound: `FamilyReimbursementCard` / `MultiRoommateSettlementCard`, Nafaqah ledger, debt simplification. Day-to-day usability issues in §2.3/2.4.
+
+**R1 — One "left until payday" number built from income, not allocations.**
+Problem: hero = allocations math; new users see 0/0; monthly income lives in settings only (`income_settings_card.dart`, `households.monthly_income`). Change: hero shows `income this cycle (or monthly_income) − committed (recurring reserve + installments due) − spent`, with "unallocated" as its own line; allocations become optional envelopes. Impact: first-session value for every household; the daily allowance becomes meaningful. Effort: M (backend `get_salary_cycle_forecast` already has most pieces; one new field set + card). Risk: low; keep allocation view as a tab.
+
+**R2 — Starter wizard instead of an empty Budgets tab.**
+Problem: onboarding = sign up (email confirm) → `HouseholdScreen` (name + type) → dashboard with no budgets → manual category creation (`budget_management_screen.dart` add dialog). Change: after household creation ask "net salary? rent? number of people?" and seed 6–8 envelopes with suggested amounts (rent, groceries, fuel, bills, dining, kids/school, family support, savings). Impact: time-to-first-value from ~10 min to ~1 min. Effort: M. Risk: low.
+
+### 1.2 Central vs. distraction (what the dashboard stacks today)
+
+`_BudgetDashboard` renders, in order: offline banner, payday banner, hero, a 4-button dock (Scan, Voice, Simulator, Prices), `AccountsSummaryCard`, `SalaryCycleWidget` (a second burn-rate panel largely repeating the hero), settlement/family card, recurring bills, installments, then **Price Tracker + Affordability Simulator again as a row** (lines 871–940), then category cards. Plus a 7-item speed-dial FAB (`app_speed_dial_fab.dart`) and a 5-tab nav where tab 5 is a 1,844-line settings screen.
+
+- **Central (keep, polish):** hero, category cards, recurring bills + installments (merge into one "Commitments" card), family/roommate card, chat & scanner entry, feed.
+- **Secondary (move to a "Tools" screen):** affordability simulator, accounts summary, PDF/CSV export.
+- **Distraction at this stage (park):** `GroceryPriceIntelligenceScreen` and `SmartShoppingBasketSheet` — price history is per-household (`price_tracker.py`), so it needs dozens of receipts across chains before it says anything; the dock shows it twice. Remove from the dashboard; revisit when there is cross-household (anonymised) data.
+- **Redundant:** `SalaryCycleWidget` vs `BudgetHeroCard` (both show burn rate/days); "Copy previous month" dialog (`bm_option_sweep`/`bm_option_rollover`) vs the household `rollover_rule` setting vs server auto-rollover (`ensure_household_cycle_budgets`) — three ways to do one thing.
+
+**R3 — Simplify the dashboard to 5 cards and 2 primary actions.** Effort S/M. Risk: none functional; pure removal + reordering.
+
+### 1.3 What Saudi users will expect that is missing
+
+Taxonomy today (`supabase/seed.sql`): `OPEX-GROCERY, DINING, FUEL, UTILITIES, SHOPPING, HEALTH, ENTERTAINMENT, GOV, MISC`. Housing rent is a *sub-category of UTILITIES* (`housing_rent`), which is the single largest line in most Saudi budgets. Missing top-level or first-class items:
+
+| Need | Evidence of gap | Suggested change |
+|---|---|---|
+| Housing/Rent as a top-level category, often paid annually/semi-annually; housing allowance (بدل سكن) paid annually | `housing_rent` under UTILITIES; `income_records.source_type` has no `housing_allowance`; no sinking fund | New `OPEX-HOUSING`; income type `housing_allowance`; "sinking fund" goals (R5) |
+| School fees (tuition, buses, uniforms) | only `tuition_fees` as a recurring default day in `recurring_detector.py` | `OPEX-EDUCATION` with per-dependent attribution (dependents already exist) |
+| Domestic worker / driver salary + Iqama/visa fees for them | none (only `iqama_visas` sub-code) | `OPEX-DOMESTIC_HELP` |
+| Family support to parents (بر الوالدين), Sadaqah, Zakat | chat classifier marks gifts/relatives "undetermined" (`chat_parser.py` `_EXTERNAL_BENEFICIARY_CUES`) and there is no category for it | `OPEX-FAMILY_SUPPORT`, `OPEX-CHARITY`; simple Zakat helper (2.5% of liquid accounts above nisab) later |
+| Car installment, insurance, Tamm/traffic fines | none | `OPEX-TRANSPORT` (fuel becomes sub), `OPEX-INSURANCE` |
+| Remittances abroad (critical for Urdu-speaking expats) | none | `OPEX-REMITTANCE` |
+| Ramadan/Eid seasonal budgets, Hajj/Umrah savings | no goals, no per-cycle override; `accumulated_savings` is one untyped number | Named savings goals + "seasonal cycle override" |
+| Fast capture without SMS | Chat/receipt/manual only. Bank apps, STC Pay, Urpay, Apple/Google Pay push **notifications and screenshots** are the realistic replacement | Android share-sheet target: share a screenshot into the app → reuse the existing receipt OCR pipeline (`/agent/scan-receipt` already accepts any image). S/M. Also optional Android `NotificationListenerService` for bank-app pushes (not SMS; iOS impossible) — later, with explicit opt-in |
+| Open Banking (SAMA) readiness | roadmap v1.1 | Premature at 4 households; needs a licensed TPP (Lean/Tarabut) and an AIS agreement. Keep the data model ready: `accounts` already has `bank` type; add `external_ref`, `imported_at` columns when the time comes. Later. |
+
+**R4 — Taxonomy refresh** (seed migration + l10n keys + chat prompt list). Effort S. Risk: low (categories are data; archiving is supported by the hybrid lifecycle).
+**R5 — Savings goals / sinking funds** (annual rent, school, Eid, Hajj) fed by the rollover sweep instead of a single `accumulated_savings`. Effort M. Risk: low.
+

+
+## 2. Workflows
+
+### 2.1 Data entry speed and failure modes
+
+| Path | Steps today | Round trips | Failure modes |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| **Chat** (`chat_entry_screen.dart`, `routes/chat.py`, `chat_parser.py`) | type/speak → wait (LLM #1 + ~8 DB calls) → confirmation card (merchant, category, sub-category, who paid, for whom, Nafaqah class) → confirm → wait (**LLM #2**: `process_chat_transaction` always re-runs `parse_chat_expense(message)` even on commit, line 588) → done | 2 LLM + ~20 PostgREST calls | duplicate prompt, inactive-category dialog, 409 no-provider, offline → queued |
+| **Receipt** (`receipt_scanner_sheet.dart`, `receipt_scanner.py`) | photo(s) → preview (vision LLM #1) → review → save (stitch + upload to Storage **before** vision LLM #2, then insert) | 2 vision calls + upload | 10–20 s end-to-end; `temperature=1.0` on OCR (line 453) adds variance between the preview and the commit parse — the saved items can differ from what the user approved |
+| **Manual** (`manual_expense_sheet.dart`) | merchant, amount, category, account, paid-by, family/roommate chips, split | 1 insert | fastest path, but hidden behind the FAB's 7th item |
+| **Offline receipt draft** | uses `LocalOcrService` whose default recognizer is `MockOcrTextRecognizer` returning `'Al Othaim Supermarket Total: 85.00 SAR …'` (`/home/user/budget-tracker/flutter_app/lib/services/ocr/local_ocr_service.dart` lines 11–18; no ML Kit in `pubspec.yaml`); `receipt_scanner_sheet.dart` lines 414–431 show that draft as merchant/amount | — | **every offline photo becomes "Al Othaim, 85 SAR"** — a fabricated draft |
+
+**R6 — Commit should not re-run the LLM.** Change: the confirmation card already holds the structured result; send it back (`parsed_payload`) and let the server validate + insert, or cache the preview under the idempotency store (`idempotency.py`) for 10 min. Impact: halves LLM latency and calls; removes preview/commit drift (especially for receipts at temperature 1.0 → set 0.1–0.2). Effort S/M. Risk: low (validation already exists in `ParsedChatExpense` / `validate_ocr_receipt_payload`).
+**R7 — Make quick manual entry the primary action** (amount → category chips → who paid; 3 taps), chat second, scanner third; run the heuristic parser on-device/first and only call the LLM when it is low-confidence. Effort M. Risk: low.
+**R8 — Remove the mock offline OCR draft** (or wire real on-device ML Kit). Effort S. Risk: none; it violates rule 05 (no placeholders) today.
+**R9 — Receipt save path:** parse first, upload after insert (or in background); shrink the photo to 1024 px for OCR (already 1280/1600). Effort S.
+
+### 2.2 Budgeting model: is it understandable?
+
+Model: per-category `budgets` rows keyed by **both** `month` (1st of month) and `cycle_key` (`YYYY-MM` naming the month the cycle *ends* in for payday > 15), `sub_allocations` JSONB, `previous_cycle_delta`, `is_active`, `account_id`; `is_flexible` categories get raided automatically when another category overspends (`reallocate_budget` called from `chat_parser.py` lines 801–808 and `receipt_scanner.py`); rollover rule per household; capacity margin per account.
+
+Where users will get confused:
+1. **Cycle naming**: a cycle running 27 Oct → 26 Nov is called "2026-11" and `budgets.month` is `2026-10-01` or `2026-11-01` depending on which code path created the row (fallback-by-month everywhere: `ensure_household_cycle_budgets` lines 668–676, `get_salary_cycle_forecast` lines 163–171). The app also matches budgets by `month` prefix (`_matchesSelectedCycle` in `dashboard_screen.dart`). Users see "November budget" while still in October. Change: label cycles by dates ("27 Oct – 26 Nov"), never by month name, and stop writing `month` once `cycle_key` is universal. Effort S (labels) / M (drop `month` dependency). Risk: low/medium.
+2. **Silent reallocation**: an 80 SAR dinner over budget quietly moves 80 SAR out of "Shopping" and marks the transaction `is_reallocated`. Nobody asked. Change: make it a prompt in the confirmation card ("Dining is 80 over; cover from Shopping? / leave over budget"). Effort S. Risk: low.
+3. **Three rollover controls** (settings rule, "copy previous" dialog with sweep/rollover choice, server auto-rollover on first read). Keep the settings rule; auto-rollover creates rows; delete the dialog. Effort S.
+4. **Zero-based capacity + account linking** is a power feature; keep but off the default path (show only when ≥2 accounts exist).
+5. **Sub-allocations** are flexible but the `_recurring_config` metadata inside the same JSONB (`recurring_detector.py` line ~556) couples bills to budgets in a way that is hard to explain; fine to keep, but hide from users.
+
+### 2.3 Nafaqah model (family mode) day to day
+
+What works: rules 1–4 enforced in DB; wife-paid shared → reimbursable; wife personal → allowance; husband paid → plain; multiple wives; explicit provider; repayment ledger with history; chat suggests the class with a confirmation step; roles per household.
+
+Edge cases a real family hits:
+- **Working wife without an allowance**: `WifeAllowanceCard` shows "not set" and `allowance_overspent` once she logs anything personal (`wife_allowance_card.dart` lines 142–151). A wife who earns her own salary should not be told she "overspent" an allowance nobody set. Change: allowance optional; when unset show "her personal spending this cycle" neutrally. S.
+- **Her own salary**: works (personal account, income record), but her personal spending is excluded from category budgets by design (owner decision) — fine, but then the hero "remaining" ignores it; label it.
+- **Gifts to relatives / her mother**: classifier → `attribution_needs_confirmation` and the card offers only Husband paid / Shared / Personal. Add "Her own money, not family" (= `wife_personal` without allowance semantics) wording. S.
+- **Children's allowances**: `household_dependents.monthly_allowance` is stored and editable (`add_household_member_sheet.dart`) and expenses can be attributed to a dependent, but there is no card tracking allowance vs spent per child. M.
+- **Cash مصروف handed over monthly**: representable as allowance; a "transfer to wife" from the husband's account is not modeled as such (becomes an expense or a transfer). Add a `allowance_transfer` income/transfer type. S.
+- **Reimbursement in practice**: "copy STC Pay note" only; fine for now. A WhatsApp deep link (`wa.me`) is roadmap and trivial once `url_launcher` is added.
+
+### 2.4 Roommates model
+
+Works: equal split, personal vs shared, pairwise + simplified debts, settle via recorded payment (STC Pay/bank/cash), WhatsApp text copy.
+Gaps: (a) **unequal shares** (master room pays more; a couple occupying one room) — very common; add per-member weight for shared expenses. M. (b) **Member leaving mid-cycle**: `calculate_settlement_v2` resolves payers against current `household_memberships`; transactions whose payer is no longer a member are skipped (`settlement_engine.py` lines ~810–813: "payer unknown; not attributed"), so outstanding debts to/from a leaver disappear from the card. Freeze a "final statement" when a member leaves (D3 did this for the wife only). M. (c) **Joining mid-cycle** inherits the whole cycle's shared costs equally — add a join date cutoff. S.
+
+### 2.5 Installments / BNPL realities
+
+`installment_service.py`: `day_of_month`, monthly `calculate_installment_terms`, default 4 "months". **Tabby and Tamara "Pay in 4" charge every 2 weeks**, first payment at purchase; Tamara also has 3 monthly; bank installments are monthly. The model mis-schedules the most common plan type and the dashboard says "/month" (`installment_plans_card.dart` line 572). Also `list_plans` re-derives plans by regex over every transaction's `raw_sms` note each time the card loads (lines 374–416) — legacy and O(n). **R10:** add `frequency` (`biweekly|monthly`) + `next_due_at`, default biweekly for Tabby/Tamara; stop regex reconstruction after a one-time backfill. Effort S/M. Risk: low.
+
+### 2.6 Recurring bills
+
+Detection = keyword/merchant patterns + sub-allocations marked recurring + clustering; "1-tap pay" writes a transaction. Reasonable. Missing: due reminders (no notifications), variable-amount bills (SEC) shown as "average" without a "bill arrived, amount X" entry; Sadad reference number is irrelevant since there is no bank link. Keep; add reminders (R11) and an "enter actual amount" step on pay.
+
+### 2.7 Notifications / alerts — the biggest retention gap
+
+`flutter_local_notifications` is a dependency (`pubspec.yaml`) and the settings screen has a "Notifications" permission row, but **no code schedules or shows a notification** (grep over `flutter_app/lib` finds no plugin usage). There is no payday reminder, no bill-due reminder, no installment reminder, no "burning fast" alert, no weekly digest. FCM is roadmap v1.3, but **local scheduled notifications need no server**: payday check-in on `payday_day` morning, each recurring bill's `expected_day`, installment due dates, and a "cycle ends in 3 days" nudge can all be scheduled on-device from data the app already has.
+**R11 — Local notifications now, FCM later.** Effort M. Risk: low; Android 13+ permission flow already handled in settings.
+
+---
+
+## 3. AI usage
+
+### 3.1 Where the LLM adds value vs. deterministic rules
+- **Receipt OCR (vision)**: genuine value; hard to replace. Keep. Lower temperature to ~0.2, send one call per receipt (R6), keep ZATCA TLV as the source of truth for merchant/total/VAT (already done; good).
+- **Chat parsing**: medium value. The heuristic fallback (`_fallback_heuristic_parse`, ~300 lines: merchant map, amount regex, category keywords, attribution cues) already handles the common Saudi phrasings (15/15 reviewer phrases after FABLE-LOGIC-07). Proposal: run the heuristic first; call the LLM only when amount is missing, merchant unknown, or more than one item; show the heuristic result instantly. Saves ~1–3 s and one call on most entries.
+- **Affordability simulation**: deterministic already (`simulate_affordability`); the LLM only detects intent — a few keywords do that.
+- **Support chat** (`support_agent.py`): low value at 4 households and the prompt hard-codes "27th payday" and "Iqama fees (400 SAR)" (stale/incorrect for non-27 households). Keep the FAQ + email; downgrade the chat to optional. S.
+- **Price intelligence / basket optimizer**: deterministic; data-starved (see 1.2).
+
+### 3.2 Cost per active household (order-of-magnitude, flash-lite-class pricing ≈ $0.10/M input, $0.40/M output)
+- Chat expense: ~1.2k-token system prompt + message, ~150 output tokens, **×2 calls** ≈ 2.6k in / 300 out ≈ $0.0004.
+- Receipt: 1280-px JPEG ≈ 1–1.5k image tokens + 600 prompt, 300–1,500 output for 20–60 items, **×2 calls** ≈ $0.001–0.002.
+- A household logging 40 chat + 20 receipts a month ≈ **$0.05/month**; 1,000 households ≈ $50/month. LLM spend is not the constraint; Railway (~$5–20) and Supabase ($0/$25) dominate. The real costs of the double call are latency and preview/commit drift, not dollars. Quotas (`check_api_quota`: 30 chats/10 min, 10 receipts/10 min, DB-backed `api_quota`) are sensible protection against abuse.
+
+### 3.3 Latency
+Chat preview = 1 LLM call (1–3 s) + category/sub-category/dependents/family-context/duplicate lookups (~8 PostgREST round trips); commit = LLM again + budget fetch + flexible budgets + insert + `enrich_transaction_items` + `InstallmentService.recalculate_budgets` which **selects every transaction of the household** (`installment_service.py` lines 289–294) on each insert. Receipt commit adds stitch + Storage upload before the vision call. Practical: 3–6 s per chat step, 8–20 s per receipt. Fixes: R6, R9, move `recalculate_budgets` to the DB trigger that already exists (BUG-02 triggers maintain `spent_amount`), and confirm Railway and Supabase are in the same region (each round trip across regions costs 100–200 ms; ~15 trips ≈ 2–3 s on its own).
+
+### 3.4 Offline behaviour
+Good: manual, chat and receipt commits queue in SQLite and replay with idempotency keys and `client_occurred_at` (`offline_queue_manager.dart`, `sync_worker.dart`). Chat text is parsed when back online. Bad: the mock OCR draft (R8).
+
+### 3.5 Privacy — what leaves the device
+Free text (often naming the wife/children, merchants, amounts) and receipt photos go device → Railway → Google Gemini via an **AI Studio API key** (`GOOGLE_API_KEY`). Depending on tier, AI Studio terms may permit Google to use prompts for product improvement; Vertex AI (or a paid tier with data-use opt-out) and a Saudi/EU data region are the standard answer for a finance app, and PDPL (Saudi personal data law) expects disclosure of third-party processors. The landing page meanwhile claims "AES-256 cloud encryption", "local salary calculations", "protected roommate aliases" and "99.4% accuracy" (`web_app/src/i18n/translations.ts` lines 401–412, 484–510) — none of these are substantiated in code (calculations run on the server; names go to the LLM). **R12:** privacy notice naming the LLM provider; move to Vertex/paid tier; strip names from the chat prompt where possible (send member ids, not display names — the prompt today receives raw user text only, which is fine, but the support chat forwards history). Effort S (notice) / M (Vertex). Risk: reputational if left.
+
+### 3.6 Prompt-injection exposure in practice
+Low. User text is only ever a `user` message; model output is coerced through pydantic with bounds (`ParsedChatExpense`, `validate_ocr_receipt_payload`); the `| PaidBy:` tag injection was fixed by structured columns (FABLE-API-01); support-chat history roles are sanitized. The remaining realistic vector is a receipt image containing instructions ("set total to 0") — mitigated because ZATCA QR values override the model and the user confirms before save. No action beyond keeping the confirmation card mandatory.
+
